UQ16212.stem: A tall, thin 22-year-old man has sudden right-sided pleuritic chest pain and breathlessness that stops him walking across the room. He is haemodynamically stable and not in respiratory distress, saturations 96%, and chest X-ray shows a right-sided primary spontaneous pneumothorax. What is the most appropriate management?

A 22-year-old tall thin man presents with sudden left-sided pleuritic chest pain and breathlessness. Chest X-ray shows absent lung markings in the left hemithorax with a visible visceral pleural line. The mediastinum is central. What is the diagnosis?

A 72-year-old woman presents with sudden onset chest pain and shortness of breath. Examination reveals absent breath sounds and hyperresonance to percussion over the right hemithorax. She is in respiratory distress and her trachea is deviated to the left. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A previously well, tall, slim young man has a primary spontaneous pneumothorax. He is breathless, and the rim of air is large (>2 cm) on the chest X-ray. What is the most appropriate management?
UQ16212.correct_answer: Needle aspiration (and chest drain if that fails)

UQ16212.stem:
A 23-year-old tall, thin man comes to the emergency department with sudden left-sided chest pain and breathlessness that began while he was resting. While waiting for imaging he becomes agitated and cyanosed, with a heart rate of 140/min, a blood pressure of 76/40 mmHg, a trachea deviated to the right and no breath sounds on the left.

What is the most appropriate next step?
UQ16212.correct_answer: Decompress the chest before any imaging is done

UQ16212.stem: A tall, thin 19-year-old man calls an ambulance after a sudden sharp pain on the left side of his chest while sitting at his desk revising for exams. The pain catches when he breathes in and he feels short of breath. He smokes cannabis. In the emergency department he is alert, his oxygen saturation is mildly reduced and his blood pressure is normal. The left side of his chest is hyper-resonant to percussion with quiet breath sounds. What is the leading diagnosis?

A 46-year-old woman presents with sudden pleuritic chest pain and shortness of breath. She is tachycardic at 118/min and mildly hypoxic. She recently returned from a long-haul flight. Her blood pressure is 118/76 mmHg. What is the most appropriate next step?
UQ16212.correct_answer: Calculate the Wells score, then D-dimer or CTPA accordingly

UQ16212.stem: A 55-year-old woman presents with chest pain and shortness of breath. ECG demonstrates sinus tachycardia and an S wave in lead I, Q wave in lead III and T-wave inversion in lead III. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UQ12633.stem: A 34-year-old woman has repeated episodes of wheeze and cough, especially at night and after exposure to house dust, with no symptoms in between episodes. Which feature of her history most supports a diagnosis of asthma?
UQ12633.correct_answer: The variability of her respiratory symptoms

UQ12633.presentation: Trigger-Related Wheeze in a Preschool Child
UQ12633.stem: A 3-year-old girl has had several episodes of wheeze and dry cough over the past six months, each triggered by running around or by cold weather, and fully settling between episodes. What is the most appropriate way to approach this presentation?
UQ12633.correct_answer: Treat as suspected asthma based on the clinical pattern

UQ12633.stem: A 2-year-old child has had three episodes of wheeze and breathlessness over the past year, all occurring exclusively during viral upper respiratory tract infections. Between episodes he is completely asymptomatic. There is no personal history of atopy, no eczema, and no family history of asthma. What is the most appropriate diagnosis?

A 10-year-old boy develops a cough and audible wheeze whenever he plays football, but is entirely symptom-free at other times, including at rest between episodes. What does this pattern most likely suggest?
A 15-year-old boy develops wheeze, tightness in his chest and a cough whenever he exercises, which settles once he rests. What is the likely underlying diagnosis?

A 65-year-old woman has recurrent episodes of severe, brief, electric shock-like pain over her right cheek and jaw, each lasting a few seconds. The pain is triggered by brushing her teeth, eating and cold air. Neurological examination is normal. What is the most appropriate first-line treatment?

A 19-year-old university student attends her GP with three months of a dry cough that wakes her most nights. She becomes wheezy and tight-chested when cycling in cold air, and the symptoms ease completely over a few days at a time. She had eczema as a child. Examination today is normal and she has never smoked. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 9-year-old boy is brought to the GP by his mother. For the past year he has had a dry cough at night and episodes of wheeze, which happen even without colds. They are worse in spring and after visits to his grandmother's house, where there is a dog. He had eczema as a baby and his father has hay fever. A salbutamol inhaler from the out-of-hours service helped quickly. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UQ12656.stem: A 42-year-old man who has never smoked presents with progressive breathlessness. CT shows emphysema that is most marked at the lung BASES. He also has deranged liver function tests, and his father died of liver disease. What is the most likely underlying diagnosis?

A 50-year-old man has ongoing liver trouble and keeps catching chest infections one after another. Testing confirms he lacks sufficient alpha-1 antitrypsin. Besides the liver, which organ is typically damaged by this condition?

A 44-year-old woman who has never smoked is seen in the respiratory clinic with progressive breathlessness. CT shows panacinar emphysema mainly in the lower lobes, and blood tests confirm a low alpha-1 antitrypsin level with the PiZZ phenotype. She asks whether any other organ could be affected so that it can be monitored. Which organ is most characteristically affected in this condition besides the lungs?

UQ12656.presentation: Early Lung Disease With Liver Involvement
UQ12656.stem: A 38-year-old non-smoker presents with breathlessness and is found to have evidence of emphysema on CT chest, alongside deranged liver enzymes. Blood testing reveals a deficiency of a specific protease inhibitor. Which pulmonary condition is this deficiency particularly associated with?

A 34-year-old woman who drinks very little alcohol is seen in the hepatology clinic after ultrasound showed a cirrhotic liver. Viral hepatitis serology and autoimmune liver screen are negative, and her ferritin and caeruloplasmin are normal. She mentions she has become breathless climbing stairs, and spirometry shows airflow obstruction. Her older brother needed a lung transplant in his forties. Which inherited disorder is most likely?
A patient with known alcohol-related cirrhosis is brought in vomiting large volumes of fresh blood. Which vascular complication of chronic liver disease should be considered as the source?

A 70-year-old woman has years of chronic productive cough with large volumes of purulent sputum and recurrent chest infections. HRCT shows dilated, thickened bronchi with a 'signet-ring' sign. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UQ12656.presentation: INR as Liver Synthetic Function Marker
UQ12656.stem: Which blood test result is most useful for assessing the liver's synthetic capacity in a patient with suspected chronic liver disease?

UQ12696.stem: A patient with severe COPD has chronic hypoxaemia confirmed on arterial blood gases (when clinically stable). Which statement best describes long-term oxygen therapy (LTOT)?
UQ12696.correct_answer: LTOT improves survival in stable chronic hypoxaemia if used at least 15 hours a day

UQ12696.stem: A patient with severe COPD is being assessed for long-term oxygen therapy. Which measurement is the key determinant of whether they meet the criteria for this treatment?

UQ12696.presentation: Long-term oxygen therapy in COPD — eligibility
UQ12696.stem: A patient with stable COPD has persistent chronic hypoxaemia (a low PaO₂ on repeated measurements when stable). They have stopped smoking. What intervention improves survival?
UQ12696.correct_answer: Long-term oxygen therapy (used at least 15 hours a day)

UQ12696.stem: A 70-year-old man on long-term amiodarone for atrial fibrillation presents with unintentional weight loss, a fine tremor and palpitations. Which investigation is particularly relevant?

A 74-year-old woman with severe COPD, who uses nebulisers at home, is brought to the emergency department with increased breathlessness and green sputum. The paramedics have been giving her 15 L/min oxygen via a reservoir mask, and she has become drowsy. Her oxygen saturation is 99%. Which oxygen strategy is most appropriate?
UQ12696.correct_answer: Change to controlled oxygen via a Venturi mask, aiming for 88-92%, and check an arterial blood gas

UQ12696.presentation: Long-Term Risk of Chronic Hepatitis C
UQ12696.stem: A patient is newly diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C infection. Over the following years, which complication represents the most significant long-term risk?

UQ12696.presentation: Adverse Effect of Long-Term NSAID Use
UQ12696.stem: A 55-year-old man who has been taking regular ibuprofen for chronic knee osteoarthritis develops new epigastric discomfort. Which adverse effect is particularly associated with long-term NSAID use?

A 69-year-old man with known COPD is brought to the emergency department by ambulance with an exacerbation. The crew gave high-flow oxygen through a non-rebreathe mask throughout the journey. On arrival he is increasingly drowsy and difficult to rouse. Pulse oximetry reads 99%, his hands are warm with a bounding pulse, and he has a coarse flapping tremor. His temperature is 37.3°C, capillary glucose is normal, he has not received any sedating medicines and he has no known liver disease. What is the most likely cause of his reduced consciousness?
UQ12696.correct_answer: Carbon dioxide retention worsened by uncontrolled oxygen

UQ12697.stem: During an exacerbation of severe COPD, a patient is given high-flow oxygen before arrival in hospital and becomes increasingly drowsy on arrival. Which complication should be specifically considered?
A patient with an acute exacerbation of COPD has an arterial blood gas showing a LOW oxygen level together with a HIGH carbon dioxide level. How is this respiratory failure best classified?

UQ12697.presentation: Acute Hypercapnic Respiratory Failure in COPD

A 68-year-old man with known COPD and a history of chronic carbon dioxide retention is admitted with an infective exacerbation. Which oxygen saturation target is generally appropriate?

Which is the most likely explanation for her deterioration?

What is the most appropriate next investigation?
UQ12821.correct_answer: Serial peak flow measurements at and away from work

UQ12821.correct_answer: Treat as suspected asthma based on the clinical pattern

UQ12821.stem: A factory worker notices that his cough and wheeze are consistently worse during his shifts and improve markedly over weekends and while on annual leave. What is the most likely explanation?
A 2-year-old boy wheezes repeatedly whenever he catches a cold, but is entirely well between these episodes. Which diagnosis is most likely?

UQ12828.stem: A patient treated for pneumonia remains febrile after several days of appropriate antibiotics, and imaging-guided aspiration of a pleural collection yields frank pus. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UQ12828.presentation: Gallbladder empyema unfit for surgery — next step
UQ12828.stem: An 88-year-old man with severe heart failure has been treated for 72 hours with intravenous antibiotics and fluids for acute calculous cholecystitis. The anaesthetic and surgical teams have agreed that he is not fit for a general anaesthetic. Despite treatment he remains febrile and tachycardic, and repeat ultrasound shows a distended gallbladder containing echogenic fluid consistent with empyema. What is the most appropriate next step?

A 47-year-old man is admitted with left-sided pneumonia. After four days of IV antibiotics he still has swinging fevers and his CRP is rising. A chest X-ray shows a new left pleural effusion. Ultrasound-guided diagnostic aspiration yields thick, cloudy, foul-smelling fluid that looks like pus. What is the most appropriate management?
UQ12828.correct_answer: Insert an image-guided chest drain and continue antibiotics

UQ12828.stem: A 60-year-old man treated for pneumonia is not improving after five days of antibiotics, with swinging fevers and ongoing breathlessness. A pleural effusion is present. Diagnostic aspiration yields turbid fluid with a pH of 7.1 and a low glucose. What is the most appropriate next step?
UQ12828.correct_answer: Insert a chest drain to drain the pleural space

UQ12828.stem: A 58-year-old man with alcohol dependence has had three weeks of fever and cough productive of foul-smelling sputum after an episode of heavy intoxication. CT chest shows a 4 cm thick-walled cavity with an air-fluid level in the right lower lobe and no pleural collection. He is haemodynamically stable. What is the most appropriate initial management?

A 62-year-old man is on day 4 of intravenous antibiotics for community-acquired pneumonia. He still has a fever and his CRP is rising. A chest X-ray shows a new moderate right-sided pleural effusion. What is the most appropriate next investigation?

UQ12828.presentation: Parapneumonic effusion — interpreting pleural fluid pH
UQ12828.stem: A 55-year-old woman with pneumonia has a persistent fever and a pleural effusion. Ultrasound-guided aspiration yields cloudy fluid that is not frank pus. The pleural fluid pH, measured in a blood gas analyser, is 7.05. Ultrasound shows a large volume of fluid that can be safely reached. Based on this result, what is the most appropriate next step?

A patient with a recent stroke and impaired swallowing develops a pneumonia, with consolidation seen in the right lower lobe. What is the most likely type of pneumonia and an important management consideration?
UQ12828.correct_answer: Aspiration pneumonia — antibiotics and a swallow assessment

UQ12829.stem: A 70-year-old woman has years of chronic productive cough with large volumes of purulent sputum and recurrent chest infections. HRCT shows dilated, thickened bronchi with a 'signet-ring' sign. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 56-year-old woman has just been diagnosed with bronchiectasis on high-resolution CT after years of daily productive cough. She has had one chest infection needing antibiotics in the past year. She has no asthma or COPD, and her spirometry is near normal. Which treatment should be offered to her as part of routine management?

A 55-year-old man with a history of alcohol excess and a recent episode of reduced consciousness has two weeks of swinging fevers, malaise and a cough productive of large amounts of foul-smelling purulent sputum. Chest X-ray shows a cavity with an air–fluid level. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old woman attends the emergency department with fevers for two weeks and a cough producing blood-streaked sputum. Her chest X-ray shows several rounded cavitating lesions in both lungs, and echocardiography finds a large vegetation on the tricuspid valve. Which part of her history most likely explains this?

UQ12829.presentation: Bronchiectasis exacerbation in pregnancy — antibiotic choice
UQ12829.stem: A 31-year-old woman who is 20 weeks pregnant has known bronchiectasis. For 3 days she has had more breathlessness and an increase in the volume and purulence of her sputum. She is well enough for oral treatment, and her previous sputum cultures grew only Haemophilus influenzae sensitive to amoxicillin. She has no drug allergies. A sputum sample has been sent. Which antibiotic is most appropriate to start while waiting for results?

UQ12829.presentation: Nasal polyps in a child — first investigation
UQ12829.stem: A 9-year-old boy is seen in the paediatric clinic after his GP found bilateral nasal polyps. He has had a chronic wet cough, recurrent chest infections and poor weight gain for several years. He was born abroad, where newborn blood spot screening was not done, and moved to the UK aged 6. Which investigation should be arranged first?
A patient with known alcohol-related cirrhosis is brought in vomiting large volumes of fresh blood. Which vascular complication of chronic liver disease should be considered as the source?

UQ12844.presentation: Preventing Oral Thrush from Inhaled Steroids
UQ12844.stem: A 16-year-old with asthma develops white patches on his tongue and buccal mucosa shortly after being started on a steroid preventer inhaler. What simple measure can reduce this problem going forward?
UQ12844.correct_answer: Rinsing the mouth with water after each inhaler use

UQ12844.presentation: Asthma–COPD overlap — stepping down inhaled corticosteroid
UQ12844.stem: A 62-year-old woman with asthma–COPD overlap is stable on an inhaled corticosteroid and long-acting beta-2 agonist combination inhaler. A locum proposes switching her to a long-acting muscarinic antagonist plus long-acting beta-2 agonist inhaler, with no inhaled corticosteroid, to reduce her pneumonia risk. She had a life-threatening asthma attack 4 years ago. Which is the most important risk of this change?
UQ12844.correct_answer: Severe asthma attack from loss of corticosteroid

UQ12844.stem: A patient with asthma continues to have frequent symptoms despite being on an inhaled corticosteroid. On questioning, he admits he often forgets doses and is unsure how to use the inhaler properly. What should be addressed before anything else?

UQ12844.presentation: Essential tremor — drug choice when propranolol is contraindicated
UQ12844.stem: A 52-year-old woman has essential tremor diagnosed by her GP. The tremor now makes it hard for her to write and drink from a cup, and she would like medication. She has asthma treated with an inhaled corticosteroid and a reliever inhaler, and has needed oral steroids for an exacerbation in the last year. Thyroid function is normal. Which drug is most appropriate to offer?

A 66-year-old man with COPD has finished a course of doxycycline for an exacerbation. He uses a high-dose steroid inhaler and admits he rarely rinses his mouth afterwards. He now complains of a sore mouth and an odd taste. Creamy white patches are seen on his tongue and inner cheeks, and they wipe away with a spatula to leave a raw red surface. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old woman with mild asthma that is normally well controlled with a low-dose inhaled corticosteroid attends her GP. A neurologist recently started propranolol to prevent her migraines. Since then she has needed her reliever inhaler several times a day and wakes at night wheezing. What is the most likely explanation?
UQ12844.correct_answer: Blockade of beta-2 receptors in the airways has caused bronchoconstriction

UQ12844.stem: A 67-year-old man has taken prednisolone daily for two years for polymyalgia rheumatica. This winter he has had three chest infections and an episode of oral thrush. Which effect of his treatment best explains this pattern?

During an asthma review with the practice nurse, a 33-year-old woman who is ten weeks pregnant says she has been thinking of giving up her beclometasone preventer because she is worried it could hurt the baby. Her asthma has been well controlled, with no attacks in the past year. What is the most appropriate advice?
UQ12844.correct_answer: Continue her inhaled corticosteroid at her usual dose

UQ12077.stem: A patient with a persistent cough, weight loss and night sweats is being investigated for possible active pulmonary tuberculosis. Which investigation is especially important for microbiological confirmation?
A patient is diagnosed with active pulmonary tuberculosis. What is the most appropriate standard initial drug regimen?
UQ12077.correct_answer: Rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide and ethambutol, with pyridoxine

UQ12077.stem:
A 45-year-old man who works as a bus driver is diagnosed with sputum smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis after months of cough and weight loss. His wife, who shares his bedroom, is referred to the TB service for contact screening.

By which route is she most likely to have been exposed?
UQ12077.correct_answer: Inhaling droplet nuclei released when he coughs

UQ12077.stem: A 61-year-old man presents with central chest pain and is being assessed for possible acute coronary syndrome. Which blood test is used to detect myocardial injury?

A 26-year-old woman with active pulmonary tuberculosis is reviewed in the TB clinic six weeks after starting standard four-drug treatment. She takes a combined oral contraceptive pill and has noticed irregular bleeding between periods since starting treatment. The nurse explains that one of her TB medicines makes her pill less reliable. Which mechanism explains this?
UQ12077.correct_answer: Rifampicin increases the activity of liver cytochrome P450 enzymes

He smokes 15 cigarettes a day. Which is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old man sees his GP with several months of cough at night, wheeze and chest tightness that come and go, with good weeks and bad weeks. He has never smoked. The GP plans objective testing to confirm the suspected diagnosis. Which result would most strongly support asthma?
UQ12023.correct_answer: Airflow obstruction that improves substantially after a bronchodilator

UQ12023.stem: A 32-year-old woman with asthma, controlled on a regular inhaled corticosteroid, saw a locum GP and was started on propranolol for anxiety before job interviews. UQ12023.correct_answer: Bronchoconstriction from beta-2 receptor blockade by propranolol

UQ12026.stem: A 63-year-old man who smokes 20 cigarettes a day is admitted to the medical ward after four weeks of fever, cough and weight loss. He has no history of alcohol misuse, seizures, dental disease or swallowing problems. A chest X-ray shows a cavitating lesion with an air-fluid level in the right upper lobe. Which imaging is most appropriate next to characterise the lesion and look for an underlying cause?

UQ11482.stem: A 19-year-old man has recurring wheeze and cough, along with eczema and hay fever. Which condition commonly occurs together with this pattern?
A family history of asthma, recurring wheeze and longstanding eczema are described for a 6-year-old boy. Which underlying predisposition best explains this pattern?

A 2-year-old child has had three episodes of wheeze and breathlessness over the past year, all occurring exclusively during viral upper respiratory tract infections. Between episodes he is completely asymptomatic. There is no personal history of atopy, no eczema, and no family history of asthma. What is the most appropriate diagnosis?

A 34-year-old woman has repeated episodes of wheeze and cough, especially at night and after exposure to house dust, with no symptoms in between episodes. Which feature of her history most supports a diagnosis of asthma?
UQ11482.correct_answer: The variability of her respiratory symptoms

UQ11482.stem: A 22-year-old man has recurrent episodes of visible haematuria that occur within 1 to 2 days of an upper respiratory tract infection. Complement levels are normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UQ11482.presentation: Trigger-Related Wheeze in a Preschool Child
UQ11482.stem: A 3-year-old girl has had several episodes of wheeze and dry cough over the past six months, each triggered by running around or by cold weather, and fully settling between episodes. What is the most appropriate way to approach this presentation?
UQ11482.correct_answer: Treat as suspected asthma based on the clinical pattern

UQ11482.stem: A 9-year-old boy is brought to the GP by his mother. For the past year he has had a dry cough at night and episodes of wheeze, which happen even without colds. They are worse in spring and after visits to his grandmother's house, where there is a dog. He had eczema as a baby and his father has hay fever. A salbutamol inhaler from the out-of-hours service helped quickly. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 38-year-old woman with long-standing asthma has worsening wheeze and recurrent episodes of cough productive of thick brownish mucus plugs. Investigations show a markedly raised total IgE, blood eosinophilia, positive Aspergillus-specific IgE, and central bronchiectasis on CT. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UQ11556.stem: A 19-year-old woman with known asthma develops worsening wheeze and breathlessness over several hours. She can only manage short sentences, and her peak flow measures 32% of her predicted best. What is the most appropriate immediate treatment?
UQ11556.correct_answer: Oxygen, nebulised salbutamol and ipratropium, and a steroid

UQ11556.stem: A 24-year-old woman with asthma is acutely breathless and cannot complete sentences. Respiratory rate 32, heart rate 120, SpO2 89% on air, peak flow 33% of predicted. The chest is quiet in places. What is the most appropriate immediate management?
UQ11556.correct_answer: High-flow oxygen with back-to-back nebulised salbutamol and ipratropium

UQ11556.stem: A 19-year-old man is in the emergency department resuscitation bay with acute severe asthma. Over the past two hours he has received back-to-back nebulised salbutamol with ipratropium and oral prednisolone. His wheeze is easing, but the nurse notices new flattened T waves and U waves on his cardiac monitor. Which blood abnormality is most likely?
A known asthmatic develops increasing breathlessness, audible wheeze and is now unable to complete full sentences. What is the appropriate immediate treatment?
An 8-year-old boy with known asthma becomes so breathless during an exacerbation that he can only speak in short, broken phrases rather than full sentences. What does this indicate?

A patient with asthma is acutely breathless. Peak flow is 40% of predicted, with a respiratory rate of 26 and inability to complete full sentences, but no features of life-threatening asthma. How is this classified?

A 31-year-old man with asthma is brought to the emergency department by ambulance. The paramedics gave one salbutamol nebuliser with little effect. He is speaking in single words, his respiratory rate is 28 per minute and his pulse is 118 beats per minute. He is alert, his chest is wheezy throughout with good air entry, and oxygen saturation is 94% on air. His peak flow is about 45% of his best. What is the most appropriate next step?
UQ11556.correct_answer: Repeated oxygen-driven salbutamol nebulisers with ipratropium, and oral prednisolone

UQ11556.stem: A 24-year-old woman with asthma is brought to the emergency department by her partner after two days of worsening wheeze despite frequent use of her blue inhaler. She is now drowsy and responds only to voice, her lips look blue and she is too breathless to attempt a peak flow reading. On auscultation there is very little air entry and almost no audible wheeze. How should this attack be classified?

UQ11563.stem: A 51-year-old woman develops fever, a productive cough and increasing breathlessness over two days. A chest X-ray demonstrates a new area of focal consolidation. What is the most appropriate treatment?
UQ11563.correct_answer: Antibiotics guided by CURB-65 and local guidance

UQ11563.stem: A 70-year-old man has fever, productive cough and right-sided pleuritic pain. He is confused, with a respiratory rate of 32, blood pressure 88/56, and urea 8 mmol/L. What does his CURB-65 assessment indicate?
UQ11563.correct_answer: High severity — admit and treat as severe pneumonia

UQ11563.stem: A 72-year-old man with community-acquired pneumonia has a new-onset confusion, urea 12 mmol/L, respiratory rate 30 breaths/min, and blood pressure 100/70 mmHg. What is his CURB-65 score?
A 68-year-old with pneumonia has new confusion, a urea of 8 mmol/L, a respiratory rate of 32, and a blood pressure of 88/56. What does the CURB-65 score indicate about his management?
UQ11563.correct_answer: High score — admit and manage as high-severity pneumonia

UQ11563.stem: A 62-year-old man is on day 4 of intravenous antibiotics for community-acquired pneumonia. He still has a fever and his CRP is rising. A chest X-ray shows a new moderate right-sided pleural effusion. What is the most appropriate next investigation?

A 68-year-old man develops fever, shaking chills and a cough productive of rust-coloured sputum over 24 hours. He has sharp right-sided chest pain on breathing in. A chest X-ray shows consolidation confined to the right lower lobe. He has no recent travel, hospital admission or exposure to others who are unwell.

Which organism most commonly causes this community-acquired pneumonia?

A 74-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department by her daughter after 3 days of cough, fever and increasing drowsiness. She is newly confused about the date and place. Respiratory rate is 32 per minute, blood pressure 96/58 mmHg, pulse 112 beats per minute and oxygen saturation 90% on air. Urea is raised. Chest X-ray shows left lower lobe consolidation. What is the most appropriate management?
UQ11563.correct_answer: Admission, oxygen and IV antibiotics for high-severity pneumonia

UQ11563.stem: A 71-year-old woman is seen on a GP home visit. For three days she has had shivering attacks, a cough bringing up rust-coloured sputum and a sharp pain in her right side when she breathes in. Her temperature is 38.6°C and she is mildly tachypnoeic but fully oriented. There is dullness to percussion at the right base with bronchial breathing and coarse crackles over the same area. Which diagnosis best fits?

UN208.stem: A 22-year-old man with known brittle asthma is brought to the Emergency Department by ambulance. He has received back-to-back oxygen-driven salbutamol and ipratropium nebulisers and IV hydrocortisone from the paramedics. He has been deteriorating over the past 24 hours despite using his salbutamol inhaler frequently at home. On arrival, he is sitting upright, leaning forward, and cannot complete sentences. He is tachycardic (HR 120 bpm), tachypnoeic (RR 32/min), and his SpO₂ is 88% on a non-rebreather mask (15 L/min). On auscultation, you note bilaterally reduced air entry and no audible wheeze. What is the single most appropriate immediate next step?
UN208.correct_answer: Immediate anaesthetic review for intubation and mechanical ventilation

UN208.presentation: Acute severe asthma in a child
UN208.stem:
A 10-year-old girl with known asthma is brought to the GP surgery by her father after a day of worsening cough and chest tightness that followed a cold. She can say only a few words between breaths and is using her neck muscles to breathe. She is alert and talking sensibly, her lips are pink and there is widespread wheeze. Her blue reliever inhaler has given little benefit at home.

What is the most appropriate next step?
UN208.correct_answer: Treat as a severe attack with bronchodilator and steroid

UN208.presentation: Metabolic Effect of Repeated Bronchodilator Doses

UN209.correct_answer: Prescribe oxygen to a target saturation range suited to him and titrate to it

UN209.stem: A 70-year-old man with known COPD attends with increased breathlessness, increased sputum volume and purulence. He is alert. While awaiting blood gases, what is the most appropriate INITIAL oxygen approach?
UN209.correct_answer: Controlled oxygen titrated to a target saturation of 88–92% pending blood gases

UN209.stem: A 74-year-old woman with severe COPD, who uses nebulisers at home, is brought to the emergency department with increased breathlessness and green sputum. The paramedics have been giving her 15 L/min oxygen via a reservoir mask, and she has become drowsy. Her oxygen saturation is 99%. Which oxygen strategy is most appropriate?
UN209.correct_answer: Change to controlled oxygen via a Venturi mask, aiming for 88-92%, and check an arterial blood gas

UN209.stem: A 74-year-old woman with severe COPD, who has had previous admissions needing non-invasive ventilation, is brought to the emergency department breathless with an exacerbation. The paramedics have given 15 L/min of oxygen via a non-rebreather mask throughout the journey. On arrival her oxygen saturation is 98%, but she has become increasingly drowsy and has a bounding pulse and warm hands. An arterial blood gas shows a raised PaCO2 and acidosis. Which is the most likely explanation for her deterioration?

A 69-year-old man with known COPD is brought to the emergency department by ambulance with an exacerbation. The crew gave high-flow oxygen through a non-rebreathe mask throughout the journey. On arrival he is increasingly drowsy and difficult to rouse. Pulse oximetry reads 99%, his hands are warm with a bounding pulse, and he has a coarse flapping tremor. His temperature is 37.3°C, capillary glucose is normal, he has not received any sedating medicines and he has no known liver disease. What is the most likely cause of his reduced consciousness?
UN209.correct_answer: Carbon dioxide retention worsened by uncontrolled oxygen

UN209.stem: A patient with an acute exacerbation of COPD has an arterial blood gas showing a LOW oxygen level together with a HIGH carbon dioxide level. How is this respiratory failure best classified?

A 55-year-old woman with breast cancer presents with sudden breathlessness and pleuritic chest pain. Wells score for PE is calculated as 5. What is the most appropriate next step?

A 34-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department three weeks after a caesarean section. This morning she developed a sharp pain in the right side of her chest that catches when she breathes in, together with sudden breathlessness. Her pulse is 112/min and oxygen saturation is lower than expected on air. Breath sounds are normal and equal on both sides, and she has no cough or fever. Which condition is the leading concern?

UN210.presentation: Suspected pulmonary embolism in pregnancy — investigation
UN210.stem: A woman at 30 weeks' gestation attends with sudden pleuritic chest pain and breathlessness. She is alert, with a heart rate of 104 beats per minute, respiratory rate 24, oxygen saturation 95% on air and a blood pressure of 118/72 mmHg. Her legs are not swollen or tender. Pulmonary embolism is suspected. What is the most appropriate initial approach to investigation?
UN210.correct_answer: Chest X-ray, followed by V/Q scanning or CTPA

UN210.stem: A 58-year-old woman develops sudden severe breathlessness, pleuritic chest pain, a rapid heart rate and a low blood pressure shortly after a long-haul flight. Which complication of pulmonary embolism is particularly concerning in this presentation?

A 46-year-old woman presents with sudden pleuritic chest pain and shortness of breath. She is tachycardic at 118/min and mildly hypoxic. She recently returned from a long-haul flight. Her blood pressure is 118/76 mmHg. What is the most appropriate next step?
UN210.correct_answer: Calculate the Wells score, then D-dimer or CTPA accordingly

She feels hot, her pulse is 124/min, BP 84/50 mmHg, respiratory rate 28/min and oxygen saturation 89% on air. A venous lactate is markedly raised. She has no history of heart failure and her care plan supports full active treatment. What is the most appropriate immediate management?
UN234.correct_answer: Oxygen, blood cultures, IV broad-spectrum antibiotics within 1 hour, IV crystalloid bolus, repeat lactate and urine output monitoring

UN234.stem: A 47-year-old man is on day 2 of an admission with severe acute pancreatitis. He becomes increasingly breathless, with a respiratory rate of 36/min, oxygen saturation of 86% on 15 L/min oxygen via a non-rebreathe reservoir mask, and he is using his accessory muscles. A chest X-ray shows bilateral diffuse infiltrates. His jugular venous pressure is not raised and his fluid balance is even. What is the most appropriate next step?

A 64-year-old man is admitted on day 8 of PCR-confirmed COVID-19. His oxygen saturation is 89% on air, rising to 95% on 2 L/min of oxygen via nasal cannulae. Chest X-ray shows bilateral patchy shadowing and there is no clinical suspicion of bacterial co-infection. Which medicine should be offered?

On the second evening after a hip hemiarthroplasty, a 79-year-old woman has an oxygen saturation of 89% on room air, a respiratory rate of 26 and new confusion. She received morphine this afternoon and has had intravenous fluids since surgery. Her early warning score is high.

What is the most appropriate approach?
UN234.correct_answer: Give oxygen, start an ABCDE assessment and call for senior help

UN236.stem: A 70-year-old man has fever, productive cough and right-sided pleuritic pain. He is confused, with a respiratory rate of 32, blood pressure 88/56, and urea 8 mmol/L. What does his CURB-65 assessment indicate?
UN236.correct_answer: High severity — admit and treat as severe pneumonia

UN236.correct_answer: High score — admit and manage as high-severity pneumonia

UN236.stem: A 78-year-old man with a history of stroke and dysphagia is admitted with a 48-hour history of cough, fever (38.8°C), and purulent sputum. He is tachypnoeic (RR 28/min) with coarse crackles in the right lower zone. A chest X-ray shows consolidation in the right lower lobe. He has a nasogastric (NG) tube in situ that was placed 5 days ago for feeding. What is the single most important immediate management step to prevent *recurrent* aspiration?
UN236.correct_answer: Check the NG tube position with a chest X-ray or pH test (and confirm placement)

UN236.stem: A 23-year-old man who has sickle cell disease was admitted two days ago with a painful crisis in his legs and is using a morphine patient-controlled analgesia pump. Overnight he develops a temperature of 38.4°C, a cough and pleuritic chest pain. His respiratory rate is 28/min and oxygen saturation has fallen to 89% on air. He is alert and his pupils are normal in size. A chest X-ray shows new consolidation in the right lower zone. Which complication has occurred?

A 65-year-old man has fever, productive cough, and right-sided pleuritic chest pain. CXR shows opacification of the right lower zone with air bronchograms visible within the opacity. There is no volume loss. What is the diagnosis?

An 81-year-old woman is admitted from her care home with three days of cough productive of green sputum, and a chest X-ray shows right lower lobe consolidation. Staff say that until yesterday she was fully orientated, but she now does not know where she is or what day it is. She has bronchial breathing at the right base and a raised white cell count. A 58-year-old woman develops sudden severe breathlessness, pleuritic chest pain, a rapid heart rate and a low blood pressure shortly after a long-haul flight. Which complication of pulmonary embolism is particularly concerning in this presentation?

UN242.presentation: Sudden Breathlessness and Shock After Trauma
UN242.stem: After a road traffic collision, a patient suddenly becomes severely breathless and hypotensive, with markedly reduced breath sounds on one side of the chest consistent with obstructive shock. What is the most likely diagnosis?

She is grey and clammy, her systolic blood pressure is 75 mmHg despite a fluid bolus, her neck veins are distended and she needs high-flow oxygen. A bedside echo shows a dilated right ventricle. What is the most appropriate course of action?
UN242.correct_answer: Manage as high-risk pulmonary embolism: resuscitate, call senior and critical care help now and consider immediate thrombolysis

A 65-year-old man has a unilateral pleural effusion. A diagnostic tap shows a pleural fluid protein and LDH that, applied to Light's criteria, classify it as an exudate. Which underlying cause does this most support?

UN1332.stem: An 8-year-old boy with known asthma becomes so breathless during an exacerbation that he can only speak in short, broken phrases rather than full sentences. What does this indicate?

A patient with asthma is acutely breathless. Peak flow is 40% of predicted, with a respiratory rate of 26 and inability to complete full sentences, but no features of life-threatening asthma. How is this classified?

A 19-year-old woman with known asthma develops worsening wheeze and breathlessness over several hours. She can only manage short sentences, and her peak flow measures 32% of her predicted best. What is the most appropriate immediate treatment?
UN1332.correct_answer: Oxygen, nebulised salbutamol and ipratropium, and a steroid

UN1332.stem: A 24-year-old woman with asthma is acutely breathless and cannot complete sentences. Respiratory rate 32, heart rate 120, SpO2 89% on air, peak flow 33% of predicted. The chest is quiet in places. What is the most appropriate immediate management?
UN1332.correct_answer: High-flow oxygen with back-to-back nebulised salbutamol and ipratropium

UN1332.stem: A 34-year-old man eating at a restaurant notices, within half an hour of a prawn starter, raised itchy pale blotches across his chest and arms and puffiness of his eyelids. He is speaking in full sentences with no stridor or wheeze, his blood pressure and heart rate are normal, and he feels otherwise well. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 17-year-old boy is brought to the walk-in centre by his friend after eating a cake that may have contained nuts. His upper lip has swollen up over the past 20 minutes. He is speaking in full sentences, has no stridor or wheeze, and his blood pressure and oxygen saturation are normal. What should be the main focus of the initial assessment?
UN1332.correct_answer: Watch closely for signs that the reaction is progressing to involve the airway or circulation

UN1332.stem: A 31-year-old man with asthma is brought to the emergency department by ambulance. The paramedics gave one salbutamol nebuliser with little effect. He is speaking in single words, his respiratory rate is 28 per minute and his pulse is 118 beats per minute. He is alert, his chest is wheezy throughout with good air entry, and oxygen saturation is 94% on air. His peak flow is about 45% of his best. What is the most appropriate next step?
UN1332.correct_answer: Repeated oxygen-driven salbutamol nebulisers with ipratropium, and oral prednisolone

UN1332.presentation: Acute severe asthma in a child
UN1332.stem:
A 10-year-old girl with known asthma is brought to the GP surgery by her father after a day of worsening cough and chest tightness that followed a cold. She can say only a few words between breaths and is using her neck muscles to breathe. She is alert and talking sensibly, her lips are pink and there is widespread wheeze. Her blue reliever inhaler has given little benefit at home.

What is the most appropriate next step?
UN1332.correct_answer: Treat as a severe attack with bronchodilator and steroid

UN1333.stem: A 24-year-old woman with asthma is brought to the emergency department by her partner after two days of worsening wheeze despite frequent use of her blue inhaler. She is now drowsy and responds only to voice, her lips look blue and she is too breathless to attempt a peak flow reading. On auscultation there is very little air entry and almost no audible wheeze. How should this attack be classified?

A 35-year-old man sees his GP with several months of cough at night, wheeze and chest tightness that come and go, with good weeks and bad weeks. He has never smoked. The GP plans objective testing to confirm the suspected diagnosis. Which result would most strongly support asthma?
UN1333.correct_answer: Airflow obstruction that improves substantially after a bronchodilator

UN1333.stem: A patient with asthma is acutely breathless. Peak flow is 40% of predicted, with a respiratory rate of 26 and inability to complete full sentences, but no features of life-threatening asthma. How is this classified?

A critically ill patient (e.g. with severe sepsis or pancreatitis) develops rapidly worsening hypoxaemia with bilateral pulmonary infiltrates on chest imaging, not explained by cardiac failure or fluid overload. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN1333.presentation: Sudden Breathlessness and Shock After Trauma
UN1333.stem: After a road traffic collision, a patient suddenly becomes severely breathless and hypotensive, with markedly reduced breath sounds on one side of the chest consistent with obstructive shock. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A baby born at 29 weeks' gestation develops grunting, nasal flaring and intercostal recession within minutes of delivery. What is the main underlying mechanism of this respiratory distress?

UN1333.presentation: Respiratory Distress in a Premature Newborn
UN1333.stem: Delivered several weeks early without the benefit of steroid injections beforehand, a newborn begins struggling to breathe within minutes of birth. Which condition is most likely?

A 34-year-old woman who drinks very little alcohol is seen in the hepatology clinic after ultrasound showed a cirrhotic liver. Viral hepatitis serology and autoimmune liver screen are negative, and her ferritin and caeruloplasmin are normal. She mentions she has become breathless climbing stairs, and spirometry shows airflow obstruction. Her older brother needed a lung transplant in his forties. Which inherited disorder is most likely?

UN1410.stem: A 55-year-old woman with breast cancer presents with sudden breathlessness and pleuritic chest pain. Wells score for PE is calculated as 5. What is the most appropriate next step?

UN1410.presentation: Excluding PE With a Low Clinical Probability
UN1410.stem: A 35-year-old woman presents with mild pleuritic chest discomfort. Her calculated Wells score suggests pulmonary embolism is clinically unlikely. Which blood test is commonly used next to help exclude venous thromboembolism in this situation?

UN1410.presentation: Wells score and D-dimer — the pathway
UN1410.stem: A patient has a low Wells score for pulmonary embolism. A D-dimer is requested and comes back negative. What is the most appropriate next step?
UN1410.correct_answer: PE is effectively excluded — look for an alternative diagnosis

UN1410.presentation: Choosing a clinical probability score for DVT
UN1410.stem:
A 56-year-old woman comes to the emergency department 10 days after a total hip replacement. Her operated leg has become swollen below the knee and the calf is painful when squeezed. She has no breathlessness, chest pain or haemoptysis. The emergency medicine registrar wants to estimate how likely a DVT is before deciding on tests.

Which tool should be used?

A 34-year-old woman taking the combined oral contraceptive pill presents to the emergency department with sudden right-sided pleuritic chest pain, breathlessness and a small amount of haemoptysis. Her heart rate is 108/min, blood pressure 126/80 mmHg and oxygen saturation 94% on air. A chest X-ray is normal. The two-level Wells score places her in the 'PE likely' group. She is not pregnant, has normal renal function and no bleeding risk factors. The CT scanner will be unavailable for the next 6 hours. What is the most appropriate management?
UN1410.correct_answer: Start interim therapeutic anticoagulation and arrange CTPA

UN1410.stem: A 55-year-old man attends the emergency department with a painful, swollen right calf that started two days after a knee arthroscopy. The whole calf is tender and pitting oedema extends to the ankle. He has no chest pain or breathlessness. Using the two-level Wells score, DVT is assessed as likely. What is the most appropriate next step?

A 58-year-old man attends the ambulatory care unit with three days of a painful, swollen left calf after a long-haul flight. His two-level Wells score puts DVT in the likely category, and interim apixaban was started. A proximal leg vein Doppler performed this morning shows no thrombus.

What is the most appropriate next investigation?

A 44-year-old woman comes to the emergency department with a swollen, tender right calf that started two days after a long coach journey. She is not breathless and has no chest pain. What is the most appropriate approach to investigating a possible deep vein thrombosis?
UN1410.correct_answer: Calculate a two-level Wells score to direct D-dimer testing or proximal leg vein ultrasound

UN1427.stem:
A 24-year-old woman attends the emergency department with two days of burning on passing urine and a dull ache in her right flank. She feels tired but is alert, and her respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, blood pressure, pulse, level of consciousness and temperature are all within the normal range, giving a NEWS2 score of 0.

How should this NEWS2 result be interpreted?
UN1427.correct_answer: Very low risk, but sepsis is not excluded; keep reassessing

UN1427.presentation: Clinical concern despite a low NEWS2 score
UN1427.stem: An 88-year-old man with a urinary catheter is on a rehabilitation ward. His NEWS2 score this afternoon is low, but his granddaughter tells the nurse he is not himself and is far more confused than yesterday, and the nurse notices new mottling over his knees and cool hands. What is the most appropriate response?
UN1427.correct_answer: Reassess him urgently and escalate despite the low score

UN1427.stem:
A 73-year-old man with redness and swelling spreading up his left leg is assessed in the emergency department. His respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, blood pressure, pulse, temperature and level of consciousness are all within normal limits, giving a NEWS2 score of 0. However, his skin looks mottled over the knees and his face appears ashen.

How should his risk be judged?
UN1427.correct_answer: Higher risk than his NEWS2 score alone suggests

UN1427.stem:
A 46-year-old woman admitted with pyelonephritis has her observations recorded on the ward. Her pulse, blood pressure, temperature, oxygen saturation and alertness all score 0, but her respiratory rate of 26/min scores 3, giving a total NEWS2 score of 3.

According to NICE sepsis guidance, what is the most appropriate action?
UN1427.correct_answer: Ask for a high-priority review by an FY2 doctor or above

UN1427.presentation: NEWS2 in an older adult with infection
UN1427.stem: An 80-year-old woman admitted with a urinary tract infection is reviewed overnight on a care of the elderly ward. Her observations have changed and her NEWS2 score has risen to 10. She is not febrile. What does this score indicate?
UN1427.correct_answer: High risk of severe illness or death from sepsis, needing urgent senior review

UN1427.stem: A postoperative patient has a rising NEWS2 score driven by tachypnoea, tachycardia and new confusion. What is the most appropriate immediate approach?
UN1427.correct_answer: Reassess using a structured ABCDE approach and escalate to a senior

UN1427.stem: A 70-year-old man arrives at the emergency department feeling generally unwell, with a productive cough and fever for three days. The triage nurse wants to use the tool that NICE recommends in acute hospital settings to stratify his risk of severe illness or death from suspected sepsis. Which tool should be used?

A 2-year-old girl has had a fever for two days. Her parents ask what should worry them. She is irritable but can be consoled, has a runny nose and is drinking less than normal.

Which feature in the history would be the most concerning for dehydration and need prompt clinical assessment?
UN1427.correct_answer: Passing much less urine than usual in the past day

UN1501.stem: A patient with a recent stroke and impaired swallowing develops a pneumonia, with consolidation seen in the right lower lobe. What is the most likely type of pneumonia and an important management consideration?
UN1501.correct_answer: Aspiration pneumonia — antibiotics and a swallow assessment

UN1501.stem: A child develops a high fever with cough, a runny nose and red eyes, followed a few days later by a blotchy rash that starts on the face and spreads down the body. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN1501.presentation: Fever, cough and fast breathing in a child
UN1501.stem:
A 6-year-old girl has had three days of fever and cough. She is breathing faster than expected for her age and has a sharp pain on the right side of her chest when she breathes in deeply. On examination, air entry is reduced and there are coarse crackles at the right base. The rest of the chest is clear and there is no wheeze.

What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old man develops fever, cough and diarrhoea several days after returning from a hotel stay. The hotel reports that a handful of other guests have become unwell with similar symptoms around the same time. Which organism is the most likely cause?

Care home staff ask the visiting GP about an 82-year-old woman with advanced Alzheimer's disease. At mealtimes she holds food in her mouth for long periods, coughs while eating and drinking, and her voice sounds wet afterwards. Her weight is stable and she is not currently unwell. Which complication is she most at risk of?

A 58-year-old man with alcohol dependence has had three weeks of fever and cough productive of foul-smelling sputum after an episode of heavy intoxication. CT chest shows a 4 cm thick-walled cavity with an air-fluid level in the right lower lobe and no pleural collection. He is haemodynamically stable. What is the most appropriate initial management?

A 78-year-old man with a history of stroke and dysphagia is admitted with a 48-hour history of cough, fever (38.8°C), and purulent sputum. He is tachypnoeic (RR 28/min) with coarse crackles in the right lower zone. A chest X-ray shows consolidation in the right lower lobe. He has a nasogastric (NG) tube in situ that was placed 5 days ago for feeding. What is the single most important immediate management step to prevent *recurrent* aspiration?
UN1501.correct_answer: Check the NG tube position with a chest X-ray or pH test (and confirm placement)

UN1501.stem: An adult is choking on food. He is conscious, able to cough but distressed. What is the most appropriate immediate action?

UN1534.stem: A 22-year-old tall thin man presents with sudden left-sided pleuritic chest pain and breathlessness. Chest X-ray shows absent lung markings in the left hemithorax with a visible visceral pleural line. The mediastinum is central. What is the diagnosis?

UN1534.presentation: Bullous lung disease — pneumothorax versus bulla
UN1534.stem: A 72-year-old woman with severe emphysema and known large apical bullae presents to the emergency department with 2 days of increased breathlessness. She is haemodynamically stable with oxygen saturation of 90% on air. Her chest X-ray shows a large hyperlucent area at the right apex with no lung markings; the radiologist cannot say whether this is a pneumothorax or a large bulla. What is the most appropriate next investigation?

UN1534.presentation: Acute severe ulcerative colitis — abdominal X-ray interpretation
UN1534.stem:
A 31-year-old woman with acute severe ulcerative colitis is on day 2 of intravenous corticosteroids. She has become more unwell: temperature 38.6 °C, pulse 122/min, and her abdomen is distended and tender. An abdominal X-ray shows the transverse colon dilated to 7 cm with loss of haustral markings. An erect chest X-ray shows no free gas under the diaphragm.

What is the most appropriate interpretation of these findings?
UN1534.correct_answer: Toxic megacolon needing urgent surgical review

UN1534.stem: A 51-year-old woman develops fever, a productive cough and increasing breathlessness over two days. A chest X-ray demonstrates a new area of focal consolidation. What is the most appropriate treatment?
UN1534.correct_answer: Antibiotics guided by CURB-65 and local guidance

UN1534.stem: A previously well, tall, slim young man has a primary spontaneous pneumothorax. He is breathless, and the rim of air is large (>2 cm) on the chest X-ray. What is the most appropriate management?
UN1534.correct_answer: Needle aspiration (and chest drain if that fails)

UN1534.stem: An elderly man who worked in shipbuilding decades ago has progressive breathlessness, chest-wall pain and weight loss. A chest X-ray shows a unilateral pleural effusion with irregular pleural thickening. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old man is on day 4 of intravenous antibiotics for community-acquired pneumonia. He still has a fever and his CRP is rising. A chest X-ray shows a new moderate right-sided pleural effusion. What is the most appropriate next investigation?

A 71-year-old woman who smoked for 40 years is seen in the respiratory clinic. She has had a cough for 2 months, has lost 6 kg and has new finger clubbing. Her GP arranged a chest X-ray, which shows a left hilar mass with widening of the mediastinum. What is the most appropriate next investigation?
UN1534.correct_answer: Contrast-enhanced CT of the chest including the liver and adrenal glands

UN1539.stem: A 45-year-old woman has suspected asthma. She completes a 2-week peak flow diary showing an average morning peak flow of 320 L/min and average evening peak flow of 410 L/min. What does this indicate?
UN1539.correct_answer: Significant diurnal variability consistent with asthma

UN1539.stem: A 35-year-old man sees his GP with several months of cough at night, wheeze and chest tightness that come and go, with good weeks and bad weeks. He has never smoked. The GP plans objective testing to confirm the suspected diagnosis. Which result would most strongly support asthma?
UN1539.correct_answer: Airflow obstruction that improves substantially after a bronchodilator

UN1539.presentation: Peak flow variability and reversibility — asthma
UN1539.stem: A 23-year-old woman sees her GP with several months of night-time cough, chest tightness and wheeze, worse in cold air. Her twice-daily home peak flow diary shows wide swings, with the lowest readings on waking. Spirometry shows a reduced FEV1/FVC ratio, and repeat spirometry 15 minutes after inhaled salbutamol shows a substantial rise in FEV1. What do these findings indicate?

A 19-year-old woman with known asthma develops worsening wheeze and breathlessness over several hours. She can only manage short sentences, and her peak flow measures 32% of her predicted best. What is the most appropriate immediate treatment?
UN1539.correct_answer: Oxygen, nebulised salbutamol and ipratropium, and a steroid

UN1539.stem: An 8-year-old boy with known asthma becomes so breathless during an exacerbation that he can only speak in short, broken phrases rather than full sentences. What does this indicate?

A patient with asthma is acutely breathless. Peak flow is 40% of predicted, with a respiratory rate of 26 and inability to complete full sentences, but no features of life-threatening asthma. How is this classified?

UN1539.presentation: DOAC accumulation in acute kidney injury
UN1539.stem: A 77-year-old man taking dabigatran for atrial fibrillation is admitted with pneumonia and sepsis. His creatinine is several times his usual value and his urine output has fallen. He has no bleeding at present. What is the main concern about his anticoagulant?
UN1539.correct_answer: Reduced renal clearance increases dabigatran levels and bleeding risk

UN1539.stem: A 24-year-old woman with asthma is acutely breathless and cannot complete sentences. Respiratory rate 32, heart rate 120, SpO2 89% on air, peak flow 33% of predicted. The chest is quiet in places. What is the most appropriate immediate management?
UN1539.correct_answer: High-flow oxygen with back-to-back nebulised salbutamol and ipratropium

UN1940.stem: A patient with asthma admits to using their salbutamol inhaler most days, sometimes more than once a day, to manage breathlessness. What does this pattern of reliever use most likely indicate?
A known asthmatic develops increasing breathlessness, audible wheeze and is now unable to complete full sentences. What is the appropriate immediate treatment?

A patient with COPD remains breathless and has frequent exacerbations despite a long-acting bronchodilator. They have no asthmatic or steroid-responsive features. What is the most appropriate step up?
UN1940.correct_answer: Add a second long-acting bronchodilator (LABA + LAMA)

UN1940.stem: A 50-year-old man with asthma reports needing his reliever inhaler almost every day because of recurring wheeze and breathlessness. What does this level of reliever use indicate?
An adult with asthma uses a short-acting beta-agonist (salbutamol) inhaler several times a week for symptoms. What is the most appropriate next step in management?
UN1940.correct_answer: Switch to as-needed low-dose ICS/formoterol (AIR therapy)

UN1940.stem: An 8-year-old boy with known asthma becomes so breathless during an exacerbation that he can only speak in short, broken phrases rather than full sentences. What does this indicate?

Care home staff ask for a review of an 86-year-old resident with known Alzheimer disease. Usually settled, over the last day she has become far more muddled, is seeing insects crawling on the walls, has a temperature and is passing urine very frequently. What is the most likely explanation for the change?

UN1940.presentation: Acute severe asthma in a child
UN1940.stem:
A 10-year-old girl with known asthma is brought to the GP surgery by her father after a day of worsening cough and chest tightness that followed a cold. She can say only a few words between breaths and is using her neck muscles to breathe. She is alert and talking sensibly, her lips are pink and there is widespread wheeze. Her blue reliever inhaler has given little benefit at home.

What is the most appropriate next step?
UN1940.correct_answer: Treat as a severe attack with bronchodilator and steroid

UN1945.stem: A 72-year-old man with community-acquired pneumonia has a new-onset confusion, urea 12 mmol/L, respiratory rate 30 breaths/min, and blood pressure 100/70 mmHg. What is his CURB-65 score?
A 68-year-old with pneumonia has new confusion, a urea of 8 mmol/L, a respiratory rate of 32, and a blood pressure of 88/56. What does the CURB-65 score indicate about his management?
UN1945.correct_answer: High score — admit and manage as high-severity pneumonia

UN1945.stem: A 70-year-old man has fever, productive cough and right-sided pleuritic pain. He is confused, with a respiratory rate of 32, blood pressure 88/56, and urea 8 mmol/L. What does his CURB-65 assessment indicate?
UN1945.correct_answer: High severity — admit and treat as severe pneumonia

UN1945.stem: A 51-year-old woman develops fever, a productive cough and increasing breathlessness over two days. A chest X-ray demonstrates a new area of focal consolidation. What is the most appropriate treatment?
UN1945.correct_answer: Antibiotics guided by CURB-65 and local guidance

UN1945.stem: A 74-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department by her daughter after 3 days of cough, fever and increasing drowsiness. She is newly confused about the date and place. Respiratory rate is 32 per minute, blood pressure 96/58 mmHg, pulse 112 beats per minute and oxygen saturation 90% on air. Urea is raised. Chest X-ray shows left lower lobe consolidation. What is the most appropriate management?
UN1945.correct_answer: Admission, oxygen and IV antibiotics for high-severity pneumonia

UN1945.stem: A 71-year-old woman is seen on a GP home visit. For three days she has had shivering attacks, a cough bringing up rust-coloured sputum and a sharp pain in her right side when she breathes in. Her temperature is 38.6°C and she is mildly tachypnoeic but fully oriented. There is dullness to percussion at the right base with bronchial breathing and coarse crackles over the same area. Which diagnosis best fits?

UN1945.presentation: Excluding PE With a Low Clinical Probability
UN1945.stem: A 35-year-old woman presents with mild pleuritic chest discomfort. Her calculated Wells score suggests pulmonary embolism is clinically unlikely. Which blood test is commonly used next to help exclude venous thromboembolism in this situation?

A 45-year-old man attends his GP with a productive cough and fever, and community-acquired pneumonia is suspected. Before an antibiotic is chosen, he mentions that about ten years ago, within an hour of taking a penicillin tablet, he came out in itchy raised welts all over his body and his lips and eyelids swelled up. How should this history be interpreted?
UN1945.correct_answer: As a probable immediate, IgE-mediated allergy to penicillin

UN1946.stem: A patient with known heart failure develops dullness to percussion and reduced breath sounds at both lung bases. What is the most likely explanation?

A 70-year-old man with heart failure presents with acute breathlessness. CXR shows cardiomegaly, bilateral perihilar batwing opacification, Kerley B lines at the lung bases, and bilateral pleural effusions. What is the diagnosis?

A 65-year-old man has a unilateral pleural effusion. A diagnostic tap shows a pleural fluid protein and LDH that, applied to Light's criteria, classify it as an exudate. Which underlying cause does this most support?

A pleural effusion is sampled. The pleural-fluid:serum protein ratio is 0.53 and the pleural-fluid:serum LDH ratio is 0.7, although the absolute fluid protein is borderline at 32 g/L. Using Light's criteria, how is this effusion classified?

A pleural effusion is aspirated. The pleural fluid protein is high relative to serum (pleural:serum protein ratio > 0.5) and the pleural:serum LDH ratio is > 0.6. How is this effusion best classified, and what does it imply?
UN1946.correct_answer: An exudate — suggesting infection, malignancy or inflammation

UN1946.stem: A patient with chronic heart failure develops swelling of both ankles. What mechanism underlies this?
UN1946.correct_answer: Raised venous hydrostatic pressure with sodium and water retention

UN1946.stem: A 33-year-old woman attends the emergency department 4 weeks after an uncomplicated vaginal birth with 2 weeks of increasing breathlessness, orthopnoea and ankle swelling. Her heart rate is 112/min, oxygen saturation is 94% on air and there are crackles at both lung bases. The ECG shows sinus tachycardia. The chest X-ray shows cardiomegaly, upper lobe venous diversion and small bilateral pleural effusions. Peripartum cardiomyopathy is suspected. Which investigation is most appropriate to confirm this?

A 62-year-old man is on day 4 of intravenous antibiotics for community-acquired pneumonia. He still has a fever and his CRP is rising. A chest X-ray shows a new moderate right-sided pleural effusion. What is the most appropriate next investigation?

UN1949.stem: A 60-year-old man with cavitating tuberculosis coughs up 300 mL of fresh blood within an hour and continues to bleed. He is becoming hypoxic. After resuscitation, what is the most appropriate definitive intervention?

After a night of heavy drinking, a patient has several episodes of forceful retching and vomiting, and then vomits a small amount of fresh blood. They are haemodynamically stable. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 74-year-old man with atrial fibrillation who takes warfarin is brought to the emergency department by ambulance after vomiting fresh blood twice and passing black stools. He has been taking ibuprofen bought from a supermarket for back pain over the past fortnight. He is pale and clammy, with a pulse of 122 and a low blood pressure. What is the most appropriate approach to his anticoagulation?
UN1949.correct_answer: Assess severity, resuscitate, stop warfarin and urgently reverse it according to severity

UN1949.presentation: Unexplained haemoptysis with a normal chest X-ray — referral
UN1949.stem: A 47-year-old woman who has never smoked sees her GP after coughing up small amounts of fresh blood on several occasions over 3 weeks. She has no fever, no recent chest infection, no nosebleeds and takes no anticoagulants. Examination is normal. An urgent chest X-ray arranged last week is reported as normal. What is the most appropriate next step?
UN1949.correct_answer: Make a suspected cancer pathway referral

UN1949.presentation: Haematemesis after vomiting with chest pain and surgical emphysema — imaging
UN1949.stem:
A 52-year-old man attends the emergency department after an evening of heavy drinking. After repeated forceful vomiting he vomited a small amount of fresh blood and then developed severe retrosternal pain radiating to his back. Pulse is 112/min, blood pressure 118/74 mmHg and temperature 37.9 °C. There is crepitus in the soft tissues of his neck.

Which investigation is most appropriate to confirm the suspected complication?
UN1949.correct_answer: CT chest with oral water-soluble contrast

UN1949.stem:
A 66-year-old man who takes naproxen for knee osteoarthritis vomits a large amount of fresh red blood at home and is brought to the emergency department. He looks pale and sweaty, his heart rate is 122/min and his blood pressure is 94/58 mmHg. A full blood count has been sent.

What should be done first?
UN1949.correct_answer: Assess and resuscitate him using an ABCDE approach

UN1949.stem: A 49-year-old man who has known alcohol-related liver disease is brought to the emergency department after vomiting a large amount of fresh blood. He has spider naevi, a distended abdomen with shifting dullness, a heart rate of 120/min and a blood pressure of 92/58 mmHg. Resuscitation has started and urgent endoscopy is being arranged. Which drug should be given now to reduce bleeding from the most likely source?

A 50-year-old woman has several months of progressive symmetrical proximal muscle weakness (struggling to climb stairs and lift her arms), a heliotrope rash on the eyelids and scaly papules over the knuckles. What is the most appropriate next step after confirming the diagnosis?

UN2172.stem: An elderly man who worked in shipbuilding decades ago has progressive breathlessness, chest-wall pain and weight loss. A chest X-ray shows a unilateral pleural effusion with irregular pleural thickening. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old man has a unilateral pleural effusion. A diagnostic tap shows a pleural fluid protein and LDH that, applied to Light's criteria, classify it as an exudate. Which underlying cause does this most support?

A pleural effusion is sampled. The pleural-fluid:serum protein ratio is 0.53 and the pleural-fluid:serum LDH ratio is 0.7, although the absolute fluid protein is borderline at 32 g/L. Using Light's criteria, how is this effusion classified?

A pleural effusion is aspirated. The pleural fluid protein is high relative to serum (pleural:serum protein ratio > 0.5) and the pleural:serum LDH ratio is > 0.6. How is this effusion best classified, and what does it imply?
UN2172.correct_answer: An exudate — suggesting infection, malignancy or inflammation

UN2172.stem: A patient with known heart failure develops dullness to percussion and reduced breath sounds at both lung bases. What is the most likely explanation?

A 76-year-old man who spent 30 years fitting pipe lagging in power stations sees his GP with 3 months of a dull, constant right chest ache, worsening breathlessness and a 7 kg weight loss. Chest X-ray shows a large right pleural effusion. CT shows nodular, irregular pleural thickening encasing the right lung and extending onto the mediastinal pleura. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old man is on day 4 of intravenous antibiotics for community-acquired pneumonia. He still has a fever and his CRP is rising. A chest X-ray shows a new moderate right-sided pleural effusion. What is the most appropriate next investigation?

A 60-year-old man treated for pneumonia is not improving after five days of antibiotics, with swinging fevers and ongoing breathlessness. A pleural effusion is present. Diagnostic aspiration yields turbid fluid with a pH of 7.1 and a low glucose. What is the most appropriate next step?
UN2172.correct_answer: Insert a chest drain to drain the pleural space

UN2174.stem: A patient with known lung cancer develops facial and upper-limb swelling, distended neck and chest wall veins, headache worse on bending, and breathlessness. What is the diagnosis and appropriate action?
UN2174.correct_answer: Superior vena cava obstruction — urgent oncology referral for imaging and treatment

UN2174.stem: A 62-year-old man presents with chest pain and hypotension. Examination reveals distended neck veins and clear lung fields. ECG confirms an inferior STEMI. What is the most likely underlying complication?

A 27-year-old woman whose mother and aunt have had recurrent 'swelling attacks' develops a rapidly enlarging tongue and swollen lips a few hours after a dental extraction. There is no itch or rash. Her voice has become muffled.

Which life-threatening complication must be assessed for first?

Minutes after receiving an intravenous antibiotic, a patient develops widespread urticaria, wheeze, facial swelling and a blood pressure of 78/40 mmHg. What is the most appropriate immediate treatment?
A 34-year-old man presents with throbbing pain in his lower jaw, facial swelling and a tender, fluctuant swelling in the gum next to a tooth with visible decay. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A trauma patient becomes acutely breathless and hypotensive with a deviated trachea, absent breath sounds and hyper-resonance on one side, and distended neck veins. What is the most appropriate immediate management?
UN2174.correct_answer: Immediate needle decompression, then a chest drain

UN2174.stem: A 30-year-old man develops severe respiratory distress after a stab wound to the left chest. He is hypotensive with distended neck veins, the trachea is deviated to the right, and there are absent breath sounds on the left. What is the most appropriate immediate management?
UN2174.correct_answer: Immediate needle (or finger) decompression, then a chest drain

UN2174.stem: A 42-year-old woman is seen at her GP surgery with three days of throbbing pain in an upper premolar tooth, and now a swelling on the gum next to it. There is a tender, fluctuant swelling on the gum beside the tooth. There is no facial swelling, she can open her mouth and swallow normally, and her observations are normal. How should she be managed?
UN2174.correct_answer: Urgent dental review for drainage and treatment of the tooth

UN2178.stem: A 55-year-old man with a history of alcohol excess and a recent episode of reduced consciousness has two weeks of swinging fevers, malaise and a cough productive of large amounts of foul-smelling purulent sputum. CT chest shows a 4 cm thick-walled cavity with an air-fluid level in the right lower lobe and no pleural collection. He is haemodynamically stable. What is the most appropriate initial management?

A 40-year-old woman sees her GP with 2 weeks of fever, sweats and a cough bringing up foul-smelling, bad-tasting sputum. A month ago she took an overdose of sleeping tablets and was found drowsy at home the next morning; she was treated in hospital and is now under the community mental health team. Her teeth are in poor condition with inflamed, bleeding gums. Her temperature is 38.2°C and there are coarse crackles at the back of the right lower chest. A chest X-ray shows a thick-walled cavity containing an air-fluid level in the superior segment of the right lower lobe.

Which organisms are the most likely cause?

UN2178.presentation: Lung abscess — persistent cavity in an improving patient
UN2178.stem:
A 72-year-old woman with Parkinson's disease and swallowing difficulty is on day 12 of intravenous antibiotics for a left lower lobe lung abscess. She has had no fever for 5 days, she is coughing up much less sputum, and her CRP has fallen to a small fraction of its value on admission. She is eating a modified-texture diet, is comfortable on room air and is mobilising with the physiotherapist. A repeat chest X-ray shows the cavity is still there, though its air-fluid level is smaller. Her daughter asks whether the abscess should now be drained.

What should be done next?
UN2178.correct_answer: Switch to oral antibiotics and repeat chest imaging

UN2178.stem: A 51-year-old woman develops fever, a productive cough and increasing breathlessness over two days. A chest X-ray demonstrates a new area of focal consolidation. What is the most appropriate treatment?
UN2178.correct_answer: Antibiotics guided by CURB-65 and local guidance

UN2178.stem: A 66-year-old woman has a pre-operative chest X-ray before a knee replacement. She has had heartburn and regurgitation for several years, worse when lying flat or bending, and has no difficulty swallowing. She has no cough, fever or weight loss. Her BMI is 33 kg/m². The X-ray shows a rounded gas-filled structure with an air–fluid level behind the heart. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 57-year-old woman who smoked 30 cigarettes a day until last year is admitted with 10 days of cough, malaise and poor appetite. Her chest X-ray shows a solitary cavity in the right upper lobe. The respiratory registrar is considering a lung abscess, a cavitating lung cancer and pulmonary tuberculosis while sputum results and a CT scan are awaited.

Which further finding would point most towards a lung abscess?
UN2178.correct_answer: Foul-tasting sputum that began after a recent seizure

UN2420.presentation: Sarcoidosis — first-line treatment for progressive pulmonary disease

What do these appearances most likely represent?

UN2846.stem: A 40-year-old woman with systemic sclerosis has progressive breathlessness. UN3956.correct_answer: Stop the pill and offer other contraception
