UN3956.stem: A 29-year-old woman develops several tender, red, raised nodules on both shins about two weeks after a streptococcal sore throat. The lesions are firm swellings rather than open sores. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A young woman develops tender, red, raised nodules on the shins. They are not ulcerated and fade like bruises over weeks. What does this finding most warrant?

UN3956.presentation: Recurrent anterior uveitis with features of sarcoidosis — first investigation
UN3956.stem:
A 38-year-old woman is being treated in the eye clinic for her second episode of acute anterior uveitis. She has had a dry cough and mild breathlessness for 2 months, and 3 weeks ago she developed tender red lumps on both shins. She has no back pain and no bowel symptoms. The ophthalmologist asks the foundation doctor to arrange the first investigation for an underlying systemic cause.

Which investigation is most appropriate first?

UN3957.presentation: Silicosis with new cavitation — investigation for tuberculosis
UN3957.stem:
A 62-year-old man who worked for 30 years as a stonemason has known silicosis. He sees his GP with 6 weeks of productive cough, night sweats and 5 kg weight loss. His temperature is 37.9°C. A chest X-ray shows a new cavitating lesion in the right upper lobe on a background of nodular upper-lobe changes.

Which investigation is most appropriate next?
UN3957.correct_answer: Sputum for acid-fast bacilli microscopy and culture

UN3957.presentation: Suspected pulmonary fibrosis — key imaging investigation
UN3957.stem: A 69-year-old retired man has had 8 months of progressive breathlessness on exertion and a dry cough. He has finger clubbing and fine bibasal inspiratory crackles. Chest X-ray shows bilateral reticular shadowing at the lung bases, and spirometry shows a restrictive pattern. He is referred to the respiratory clinic. Which imaging investigation is most important to characterise his lung disease?

A 45-year-old woman with systemic sclerosis develops progressive exertional dyspnoea and a dry cough. HRCT shows bilateral lower-zone ground-glass change with fine reticulation and minimal honeycombing. What is the most likely interstitial lung disease pattern?

A 71-year-old retired accountant who has never smoked and has no occupational dust exposure sees his GP with 9 months of gradually worsening breathlessness on exertion and a persistent dry cough. He has finger clubbing and fine, velcro-like crackles at both lung bases. There is no ankle swelling and his JVP is not raised. Spirometry shows a reduced FVC with a normal FEV1/FVC ratio, and his gas transfer is reduced. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 70-year-old man has a chest X-ray before elective hip surgery. He has no respiratory symptoms. The film shows bilateral, irregular calcified areas of pleural thickening along the diaphragms and lateral chest walls, with clear lung fields. He spent many years as a heating engineer fitting and stripping pipe insulation in old buildings. Which occupational exposure most likely explains these findings?

An elderly man who worked in shipbuilding decades ago has progressive breathlessness, chest-wall pain and weight loss. A chest X-ray shows a unilateral pleural effusion with irregular pleural thickening. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A 39-year-old factory line worker develops ongoing forearm and wrist discomfort that flares during repetitive assembly work and settles on days off. What is the most appropriate first step?
UN3957.correct_answer: Evaluate the occupational exposure and consider a work-related musculoskeletal disorder

Two years ago she was started on amiodarone after recurrent atrial fibrillation that could not be controlled with other drugs, and she has noticed a bluish-grey discoloration of her face in the summer. There are fine bibasal inspiratory crackles, no finger clubbing and no peripheral oedema. A chest X-ray shows bilateral reticular shadowing with a normal cardiac silhouette. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A construction worker found collapsed on a very hot day is confused, has stopped sweating and has a core temperature of 41°C. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 77-year-old woman with aortic stenosis and impaired left ventricular function is admitted with worsening breathlessness when lying flat. On auscultation there are fine, late inspiratory crackles over both lower zones that do not clear with coughing. What is the underlying cause of these sounds?
UN3958.correct_answer: Fluid in the lung interstitium and alveoli from raised pulmonary venous pressure

He spent many years as a heating engineer fitting and stripping pipe insulation in old buildings. Which occupational exposure most likely explains these findings?

UN3960.stem: A 58-year-old man newly diagnosed with COPD continues to smoke 20 cigarettes a day. Which single intervention would do the most to change the long-term trajectory of his lung disease?

A 59-year-old woman who has taken prednisolone daily for over a year for interstitial lung disease is admitted with pyelonephritis. She has been vomiting since yesterday and her blood pressure is low. She carries a steroid emergency card. Why is careful management of her steroid treatment essential during this illness?
UN3960.correct_answer: Long-term steroids suppress her adrenal glands, so she cannot mount a normal cortisol response to stress

UN3960.stem: A 45-year-old woman with systemic sclerosis develops progressive exertional dyspnoea and a dry cough. HRCT shows bilateral lower-zone ground-glass change with fine reticulation and minimal honeycombing. What is the most likely interstitial lung disease pattern?

An 86-year-old woman sees her GP because she still feels exhausted six weeks after a urinary tract infection that was treated promptly. Her daughter says she has lost weight over the past year, now finds it hard to get out of a chair, and has taken a long time to recover from every minor illness recently. Examination and routine blood tests show no specific disease. Which term best describes her condition?

UN3960.presentation: Long-Term Risk of Chronic Hepatitis C
UN3960.stem: A patient is newly diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C infection. Over the following years, which complication represents the most significant long-term risk?
A 70-year-old man on long-term amiodarone for atrial fibrillation presents with unintentional weight loss, a fine tremor and palpitations. Which investigation is particularly relevant?

A 68-year-old heavy smoker is found to have hyponatraemia with concentrated urine and normal volume status. A chest X-ray reveals a new mass in the right lung. Why might this pulmonary finding be directly relevant to his sodium disturbance?
UN3960.correct_answer: Lung cancer or other lung disease can cause SIADH

UN3960.stem: A 45-year-old man on long-term lithium for bipolar disorder reports persistent tiredness, unexplained weight gain and feeling cold all the time. Which investigation should be arranged?

UN3962.stem: A patient with known lung cancer develops facial and upper-limb swelling, distended neck and chest wall veins, headache worse on bending, and breathlessness. What is the diagnosis and appropriate action?
UN3962.correct_answer: Superior vena cava obstruction — urgent oncology referral for imaging and treatment

UN3962.stem: Minutes after receiving an intravenous antibiotic, a patient develops widespread urticaria, wheeze, facial swelling and a blood pressure of 78/40 mmHg. What is the most appropriate immediate treatment?

A 27-year-old woman whose mother and aunt have had recurrent 'swelling attacks' develops a rapidly enlarging tongue and swollen lips a few hours after a dental extraction. There is no itch or rash. Her voice has become muffled.

Which life-threatening complication must be assessed for first?
A 34-year-old man presents with throbbing pain in his lower jaw, facial swelling and a tender, fluctuant swelling in the gum next to a tooth with visible decay. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old obese woman presents with a 6-week history of daily headache worse on lying down and on coughing, with transient visual obscurations. Fundoscopy shows bilateral papilloedema. CT head is normal. What is the most appropriate next investigation?
UN3962.correct_answer: Lumbar puncture with measurement of opening pressure

UN3962.stem: A 28-year-old otherwise healthy woman develops facial pressure, nasal blockage and thick nasal discharge for three days, along with mild fatigue. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A young woman on the combined oral contraceptive pill has a progressively worsening headache over days, worse lying down, with papilloedema. Her plain CT head is normal. What is the most appropriate next investigation?
UN3962.correct_answer: CT or MR venography of the cerebral venous sinuses

UN3962.presentation: Delayed Fever and Rash With Organ Involvement
UN3962.stem: Four weeks after starting a new anticonvulsant, a patient develops fever, a widespread rash, marked facial swelling and is found to have eosinophilia and deranged liver function tests. What severe drug reaction should be suspected?

UN3963.stem: A 62-year-old smoker has shoulder and inner-arm pain with wasting of the small muscles of the hand. On the same side he has a drooping eyelid, a constricted pupil and reduced facial sweating. A chest X-ray shows an apical lung shadow. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN3963.presentation: Horner's syndrome from an apical lung tumour
UN3963.stem: A 62-year-old woman who smoked for 35 years sees her GP with 3 months of severe pain in her left shoulder that spreads down the inner side of her arm to her little finger. She has noticed weakness and wasting of the small muscles of her left hand. Her left upper eyelid droops slightly and her left pupil is smaller than the right, with no difference in eye movements. What is the most likely cause?

A patient has a unilateral constricted pupil (miosis), partial drooping of the upper eyelid (ptosis) and reduced sweating on that side of the face (anhidrosis). What does this triad represent, and what serious cause must be considered?
UN3963.correct_answer: Horner's syndrome — consider a Pancoast (apical lung) tumour or carotid dissection

UN3963.stem: A 54-year-old man who works as a painter and decorator has had 2 months of right shoulder pain. The pain is felt over the outer upper arm, is worse when he works with his arm above his head, and wakes him when he lies on that side. There was no injury and he is otherwise well. Passive movement is full, active abduction is painful in the middle of the range and resisted abduction reproduces his pain. His GP diagnoses subacromial pain syndrome. He is keen to keep working. What is the most appropriate initial management?

A 55-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes has several months of progressive shoulder pain and stiffness. Both active and passive movements are restricted, especially external rotation, and X-rays are normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 64-year-old man known to have an aggressive lung tumour of small-cell type becomes muddled, and his sodium is found to be markedly low with no signs of excess fluid. What is the likely underlying mechanism?

A 52-year-old woman with hypothyroidism has had 3 months of left shoulder pain that began without any injury. The pain is severe, wakes her most nights and has not settled with regular paracetamol and ibuprofen, and the shoulder is becoming increasingly stiff. Active and passive movements are restricted in all directions, especially external rotation, and an X-ray of the shoulder is normal. Her GP diagnoses frozen shoulder (adhesive capsulitis). What is the most appropriate next step?

A 67-year-old retired builder has had 4 months of gradually worsening right shoulder pain and now cannot lift his arm to reach a high shelf. He has had no fall or other injury. On examination there is wasting above the spine of the scapula. He cannot actively raise the arm beyond about 40 degrees of abduction and external rotation against resistance is weak, but the examiner can move the shoulder passively through a full range. Sensation over the shoulder and arm is normal and the biceps reflex is present. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN3971.stem: A 35-year-old woman presents with progressive exertional breathlessness, syncope on exertion, and a right parasternal heave. ECG shows right axis deviation and right bundle branch block. Echocardiogram shows estimated RVSP of 70 mmHg (normal below 35 mmHg). Right heart catheterisation confirms mean PAP of 35 mmHg. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 52-year-old woman is under the care of the respiratory clinic at a district general hospital with progressive breathlessness. Echocardiography shows a high probability of pulmonary hypertension with normal left ventricular function and valves. Lung function tests and a high-resolution CT chest are normal, and a ventilation–perfusion scan shows no perfusion defects. Which is the most appropriate next step?
UN3971.correct_answer: Refer to a specialist pulmonary hypertension centre

UN3971.presentation: Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension in Connective Tissue Disease
UN3971.stem: A 40-year-old woman with systemic sclerosis has progressive breathlessness. Lung function shows a low transfer factor out of proportion to lung volumes, and right heart catheterisation gives a mean pulmonary artery pressure of 45 mmHg with a normal wedge pressure and clear lung fields. What is the underlying problem?

A 45-year-old woman has 9 months of progressively worsening breathlessness on exertion. On examination she has a raised jugular venous pressure, a loud second heart sound in the pulmonary area and mild ankle oedema. Her ECG shows right axis deviation and her chest X-ray shows enlarged pulmonary arteries with clear lung fields. Which investigation should be done first to assess for pulmonary hypertension?

A 45-year-old woman with systemic sclerosis develops progressive exertional dyspnoea and a dry cough. HRCT shows bilateral lower-zone ground-glass change with fine reticulation and minimal honeycombing. What is the most likely interstitial lung disease pattern?

Echocardiography shows NORMAL-sized, non-dilated ventricles with PRESERVED systolic function but markedly impaired diastolic filling. Cardiac amyloidosis is suspected. What is the most likely type of cardiomyopathy?

A 68-year-old man with severe COPD has worsening ankle swelling and abdominal fullness. Examination shows a raised JVP, hepatomegaly, pitting peripheral oedema and a loud pulmonary component of the second heart sound. Left ventricular function is preserved on echocardiography. What is the most likely diagnosis?
UN3971.correct_answer: Cor pulmonale (right heart failure secondary to lung disease)

UN3972.correct_answer: Raised venous pressure transmitted back to the capillaries

UN3976.correct_answer: Urgent ITU/HDU referral for monitoring and preparation for potential ventilatory support

UN3977.stem: A 2-year-old boy wheezes repeatedly whenever he catches a cold, but is entirely well between these episodes. Which diagnosis is most likely?
A 45-year-old woman has suspected asthma. She completes a 2-week peak flow diary showing an average morning peak flow of 320 L/min and average evening peak flow of 410 L/min. What does this indicate?
UN3977.correct_answer: Significant diurnal variability consistent with asthma

UN3977.stem: A 35-year-old man sees his GP with several months of cough at night, wheeze and chest tightness that come and go, with good weeks and bad weeks. He has never smoked. The GP plans objective testing to confirm the suspected diagnosis. Which result would most strongly support asthma?
UN3977.correct_answer: Airflow obstruction that improves substantially after a bronchodilator

UN3977.stem: A 19-year-old man has recurring wheeze and cough, along with eczema and hay fever. Which condition commonly occurs together with this pattern?

UN3977.correct_answer: The variability of her respiratory symptoms

UN3977.stem: A 34-year-old man who works as a spray painter in a car body shop has developed cough, wheeze and breathlessness over the past eight months. He has no history of childhood asthma. What is the most appropriate next investigation?
UN3977.correct_answer: Serial peak flow measurements at and away from work

UN4490.stem: A 75-year-old man with longstanding heart failure after previous myocardial infarctions has pitting swelling of both lower legs reaching the mid-shin. His serum albumin is normal. Which change in Starling forces is mainly responsible?
UN4490.correct_answer: Increased hydrostatic pressure in the systemic capillaries

UN4490.correct_answer: An exudate — suggesting infection, malignancy or inflammation

UN4491.stem: A 60-year-old man treated for pneumonia is not improving after five days of antibiotics, with swinging fevers and ongoing breathlessness. A pleural effusion is present. Diagnostic aspiration yields turbid fluid with a pH of 7.1 and a low glucose. What is the most appropriate next step?
UN4491.correct_answer: Insert a chest drain to drain the pleural space

UN4491.presentation: Parapneumonic effusion — interpreting pleural fluid pH
UN4491.stem: A 55-year-old woman with pneumonia has a persistent fever and a pleural effusion. Ultrasound-guided aspiration yields cloudy fluid that is not frank pus. The pleural fluid pH, measured in a blood gas analyser, is 7.05. Ultrasound shows a large volume of fluid that can be safely reached. Based on this result, what is the most appropriate next step?
A known asthmatic develops increasing breathlessness, audible wheeze and is now unable to complete full sentences. What is the appropriate immediate treatment?

A patient treated for pneumonia remains febrile after several days of appropriate antibiotics, and imaging-guided aspiration of a pleural collection yields frank pus. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 51-year-old woman develops fever, a productive cough and increasing breathlessness over two days. A chest X-ray demonstrates a new area of focal consolidation. What is the most appropriate treatment?
UN4491.correct_answer: Antibiotics guided by CURB-65 and local guidance

UN4491.stem: A 70-year-old man is on a medical ward being treated for pneumonia, which caused high fevers for the first two days. He tells the doctor that his upper lip began tingling and burning yesterday, and now a crop of small, painful vesicles has appeared at the same spot, where he says 'fever blisters' have come up occasionally over the years. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN4491.presentation: Infected pancreatic necrosis — gas bubbles on CT
UN4491.stem: A 45-year-old man with severe acute pancreatitis (Glasgow score 6) develops persistent fever and clinical deterioration on day 8 of admission. CT pancreas shows gas bubbles within a necrotic collection. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 38-year-old woman with known myasthenia gravis develops increasing breathlessness and difficulty swallowing over 24 hours following a chest infection. Her forced vital capacity is falling on serial measurement. What is the most important immediate assessment?
UN4491.correct_answer: Serial FVC with airway and ventilation support on standby

UN4492.stem: A patient treated for pneumonia remains febrile after several days of appropriate antibiotics, and imaging-guided aspiration of a pleural collection yields frank pus. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN4492.presentation: Parapneumonic effusion — interpreting pleural fluid pH
UN4492.stem: A 55-year-old woman with pneumonia has a persistent fever and a pleural effusion. Ultrasound-guided aspiration yields cloudy fluid that is not frank pus. The pleural fluid pH, measured in a blood gas analyser, is 7.05. Ultrasound shows a large volume of fluid that can be safely reached. Based on this result, what is the most appropriate next step?

A 47-year-old man is admitted with left-sided pneumonia. After four days of IV antibiotics he still has swinging fevers and his CRP is rising. A chest X-ray shows a new left pleural effusion. Ultrasound-guided diagnostic aspiration yields thick, cloudy, foul-smelling fluid that looks like pus. What is the most appropriate management?
UN4492.correct_answer: Insert an image-guided chest drain and continue antibiotics

UN4492.stem: A 60-year-old man treated for pneumonia is not improving after five days of antibiotics, with swinging fevers and ongoing breathlessness. A pleural effusion is present. Diagnostic aspiration yields turbid fluid with a pH of 7.1 and a low glucose. What is the most appropriate next step?
UN4492.correct_answer: Insert a chest drain to drain the pleural space

UN4492.stem: A 62-year-old man is on day 4 of intravenous antibiotics for community-acquired pneumonia. He still has a fever and his CRP is rising. A chest X-ray shows a new moderate right-sided pleural effusion. What is the most appropriate next investigation?

A 58-year-old man with alcohol dependence has had three weeks of fever and cough productive of foul-smelling sputum after an episode of heavy intoxication. CT chest shows a 4 cm thick-walled cavity with an air-fluid level in the right lower lobe and no pleural collection. He is haemodynamically stable. What is the most appropriate initial management?

A patient with a recent stroke and impaired swallowing develops a pneumonia, with consolidation seen in the right lower lobe. What is the most likely type of pneumonia and an important management consideration?
UN4492.correct_answer: Aspiration pneumonia — antibiotics and a swallow assessment

UN4492.presentation: Gallbladder empyema unfit for surgery — next step
UN4492.stem: An 88-year-old man with severe heart failure has been treated for 72 hours with intravenous antibiotics and fluids for acute calculous cholecystitis. The anaesthetic and surgical teams have agreed that he is not fit for a general anaesthetic. Despite treatment he remains febrile and tachycardic, and repeat ultrasound shows a distended gallbladder containing echogenic fluid consistent with empyema. What is the most appropriate next step?

UN4497.stem: A 70-year-old man has a year of progressive exertional breathlessness and a dry cough. He has finger clubbing and fine bibasal late-inspiratory crackles. HRCT shows basal, peripheral honeycombing with traction bronchiectasis. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 72-year-old retired man tells his GP that over the past year he has become increasingly short of breath walking up hills, and he has an irritating cough that produces no sputum. On examination he has finger clubbing and fine end-inspiratory crackles over both bases posteriorly. There is no wheeze, his jugular venous pressure is not raised and he has no ankle oedema. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 71-year-old retired accountant who has never smoked and has no occupational dust exposure sees his GP with 9 months of gradually worsening breathlessness on exertion and a persistent dry cough. He has finger clubbing and fine, velcro-like crackles at both lung bases. There is no ankle swelling and his JVP is not raised. Spirometry shows a reduced FVC with a normal FEV1/FVC ratio, and his gas transfer is reduced. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN4497.presentation: Newly diagnosed idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis — non-drug management
UN4497.stem: A 72-year-old woman has just been given a diagnosis of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis by the interstitial lung disease multidisciplinary team, based on typical HRCT findings and lung function. She is breathless walking up one flight of stairs but manages her own shopping. Her oxygen saturation is 95% at rest on air and she does not desaturate on a walk test. Which is the most appropriate next step in her management at this stage?

A 71-year-old man has been diagnosed with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis by an interstitial lung disease multidisciplinary team. His forced vital capacity is 65% of predicted. He has stopped smoking and has been assessed for pulmonary rehabilitation. The respiratory consultant discusses a medicine to slow disease progression. Which medicine is most appropriate?

UN4497.presentation: Suspected pulmonary fibrosis — key imaging investigation
UN4497.stem: A 69-year-old retired man has had 8 months of progressive breathlessness on exertion and a dry cough. He has finger clubbing and fine bibasal inspiratory crackles. Chest X-ray shows bilateral reticular shadowing at the lung bases, and spirometry shows a restrictive pattern. He is referred to the respiratory clinic. Which imaging investigation is most important to characterise his lung disease?

A 74-year-old man with atrial fibrillation develops sudden, severe, central abdominal pain. The pain is far more dramatic than the examination findings, which show a soft, only mildly tender abdomen. Blood tests reveal a metabolic acidosis with a markedly raised lactate. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 66-year-old woman with end-stage idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis is visited at home by the community palliative care nurse. She is too breathless to finish a sentence while dressing, although a fan, pacing techniques and treatment of a recent chest infection have been tried. Her oxygen saturation at rest is within her usual range. Which drug treatment is most appropriate to ease her symptoms?

UN4499.presentation: Hearing A Voice With No Stimulus
UN4499.stem: A 36-year-old woman describes hearing a voice talking to her when no one else is in the room, and she is entirely convinced the voice is genuine. What is this symptom called?

UN4499.presentation: Unexplained haemoptysis with a normal chest X-ray — referral
UN4499.stem: A 47-year-old woman who has never smoked sees her GP after coughing up small amounts of fresh blood on several occasions over 3 weeks. She has no fever, no recent chest infection, no nosebleeds and takes no anticoagulants. Examination is normal. An urgent chest X-ray arranged last week is reported as normal. What is the most appropriate next step?
UN4499.correct_answer: Make a suspected cancer pathway referral

UN4499.stem: A 61-year-old woman is admitted from the medical take with six weeks of malaise, weight loss and aching joints, and three days of coughing up blood. She has no sinus, ear or nasal symptoms and no history of asthma. Urine shows blood and red cell casts, and her creatinine has risen sharply over a week. Eosinophil count is normal. Anti-myeloperoxidase (MPO) ANCA is strongly positive and anti-GBM antibodies are negative. Renal biopsy shows necrotising crescentic glomerulonephritis with little or no immune deposition. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old woman has repeated episodes of wheeze and cough, especially at night and after exposure to house dust, with no symptoms in between episodes. Which feature of her history most supports a diagnosis of asthma?
UN4499.correct_answer: The variability of her respiratory symptoms

UN4499.stem: A patient reports years of repeated chest infections along with a daily cough that produces large amounts of thick, purulent sputum. Which underlying condition should be considered?

A 70-year-old woman has years of chronic productive cough with large volumes of purulent sputum and recurrent chest infections. HRCT shows dilated, thickened bronchi with a 'signet-ring' sign. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 57-year-old woman with dermatomyositis diagnosed 3 weeks ago is waiting for her rheumatology follow-up. She already has weakness of her shoulders and hips and a rash on her eyelids and knuckles. She calls her GP practice to report a new symptom. Which new symptom most needs urgent same-day medical assessment?
UN4499.correct_answer: Coughing and choking when she drinks

UN4499.stem: Paramedics attend a 75-year-old man with known cardiac failure who was found bolt upright on the side of his bed, struggling for breath. His oxygen saturation is low and he keeps coughing up foamy, pink-tinged secretions. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN4502.stem: A 42-year-old man who has never smoked presents with progressive breathlessness. CT shows emphysema that is most marked at the lung BASES. He also has deranged liver function tests, and his father died of liver disease. What is the most likely underlying diagnosis?

A 44-year-old woman who has never smoked is seen in the respiratory clinic with progressive breathlessness. CT shows panacinar emphysema mainly in the lower lobes, and blood tests confirm a low alpha-1 antitrypsin level with the PiZZ phenotype. She asks whether any other organ could be affected so that it can be monitored. Which organ is most characteristically affected in this condition besides the lungs?

A 34-year-old woman who drinks very little alcohol is seen in the hepatology clinic after ultrasound showed a cirrhotic liver. Viral hepatitis serology and autoimmune liver screen are negative, and her ferritin and caeruloplasmin are normal. She mentions she has become breathless climbing stairs, and spirometry shows airflow obstruction. Her older brother needed a lung transplant in his forties. Which inherited disorder is most likely?

UN4502.presentation: Early Lung Disease With Liver Involvement
UN4502.stem: A 38-year-old non-smoker presents with breathlessness and is found to have evidence of emphysema on CT chest, alongside deranged liver enzymes. Blood testing reveals a deficiency of a specific protease inhibitor. Which pulmonary condition is this deficiency particularly associated with?

A 50-year-old man has ongoing liver trouble and keeps catching chest infections one after another. Testing confirms he lacks sufficient alpha-1 antitrypsin. Besides the liver, which organ is typically damaged by this condition?

UN4502.presentation: Abdominal Pain and Unusual Urine Colour After a New Drug
UN4502.stem: A 29-year-old woman develops severe colicky abdominal pain, constipation and agitation two days after starting a new antibiotic. Her urine appears unusually dark, almost reddish-brown, after being left standing. What inherited condition should be considered?
A 6-hour-old term baby is tachypnoeic, irritable, and feeding poorly. Which of the following is the strongest risk factor for early-onset neonatal GBS sepsis?
UN4502.correct_answer: Maternal GBS colonisation without intrapartum antibiotics

UN4502.stem:
A term baby boy is 12 hours old on the postnatal ward. During labour his mother developed a fever and was given intravenous antibiotics for suspected infection of the membranes and amniotic fluid. The midwife is now concerned because he is grunting, feeding poorly and his temperature has been unstable. His capillary blood glucose is normal.

Which condition must be assumed until proven otherwise?

UN4505.stem: An overweight middle-aged man has loud snoring, witnessed apnoeas, unrefreshing sleep and marked daytime sleepiness (a high Epworth score). What is the most appropriate investigation and first-line treatment if confirmed?
UN4505.correct_answer: Sleep study, then CPAP (with weight loss) if confirmed moderate-to-severe

UN4505.presentation: Moderate obstructive sleep apnoea syndrome — DVLA advice
UN4505.stem: A 49-year-old man who holds a car licence only has a sleep study showing moderate obstructive sleep apnoea, with an apnoea–hypopnoea index of 22 events per hour. He has excessive daytime sleepiness and recently nearly fell asleep while waiting at traffic lights. Continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) treatment is being arranged. He asks what this means for his driving. What is the most appropriate advice?
UN4505.correct_answer: He must stop driving now and must notify the DVLA himself

UN4505.stem: Which of the following is the single most important risk factor for developing age-related cataracts?

UN4505.presentation: Suspected obstructive sleep apnoea — first diagnostic test
UN4505.stem: A 55-year-old man is seen in a sleep clinic with loud snoring, witnessed pauses in his breathing, unrefreshing sleep and daytime sleepiness. His Epworth Sleepiness Scale score is 14 and his BMI is 36 kg/m². He has no heart failure or chronic lung disease, and all sleep diagnostic services are available locally. Which is the most appropriate first diagnostic test?

A 49-year-old woman with obesity and hypertension sees her GP about tiredness. She wakes with headaches, never feels refreshed and nods off while watching television in the evening. Her husband has moved to the spare room because she snores very loudly and he has heard her choke and gasp during the night. Which diagnosis is most likely?

A 47-year-old man is reviewed in the sleep clinic. His wife reports loud snoring and pauses in his breathing at night, and he has fallen asleep in afternoon meetings at work. He has a BMI of 36 kg/m2 and treated hypertension. An overnight sleep study confirms moderate obstructive sleep apnoea. He has already been referred to a weight management service. What is the most appropriate treatment?

UN4505.presentation: Obstructive sleep apnoea in a child
UN4505.stem:
A 6-year-old girl is brought to the GP because her teacher says she keeps falling asleep in class and struggles to concentrate. Her father says she snores heavily every night, often gasps or snorts, and sleeps restlessly with her neck extended. She breathes through her mouth during the day and her speech sounds nasal. On examination both tonsils are large and almost meet in the midline.

Which is the most likely diagnosis?
UN4505.correct_answer: Obstructive sleep apnoea from adenotonsillar hypertrophy

UN4505.presentation: Risk Factor for a Severe Diarrhoeal Illness
UN4505.stem: A patient develops profuse, foul-smelling diarrhoea two weeks after a course of co-amoxiclav for a chest infection, and stool testing confirms *Clostridioides difficile* infection. What is the most important risk factor for this infection?

UN4506.presentation: Sudden Breathlessness in a Patient With a Known DVT
UN4506.stem: A woman recently diagnosed with a proximal DVT in her left leg suddenly develops severe breathlessness, pleuritic chest pain and a fast heart rate. What complication should be suspected?

A 45-year-old man arrives in the emergency department two days after a long-haul flight with sudden breathlessness and a sharp left-sided chest pain on inspiration. He is tachycardic, his blood pressure is normal and his oxygen saturation is mildly reduced on air. The chest X-ray is unremarkable. His two-level Wells score indicates that pulmonary embolism is likely, and his renal function is normal. Which investigation should be arranged next?

A 58-year-old woman develops sudden severe breathlessness, pleuritic chest pain, a rapid heart rate and a low blood pressure shortly after a long-haul flight. Which complication of pulmonary embolism is particularly concerning in this presentation?

On the fourth day after major abdominal surgery, a patient suddenly becomes breathless with pleuritic chest pain, a tachycardia and mild hypoxia. The chest is clear and there are no new infective features. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A 46-year-old woman presents with sharp chest pain that worsens with inspiration and improves when sitting forward. ECG shows widespread saddle-shaped ST elevation. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A 55-year-old woman with breast cancer presents with sudden breathlessness and pleuritic chest pain. Wells score for PE is calculated as 5. What is the most appropriate next step?

A 45-year-old man has sharp central chest pain that is worse on lying flat and relieved by sitting forward. The pain is also worse on inspiration. His ECG shows widespread (diffuse) concave ST elevation and PR depression. He is haemodynamically stable. What is the most appropriate management?
UN4506.correct_answer: Treat as acute pericarditis with NSAIDs and colchicine

UN4506.stem: A 50-year-old woman has pleuritic chest pain and breathlessness. Using a validated clinical prediction tool, she is assessed as 'PE UNLIKELY'. She is haemodynamically stable. What is the most appropriate next investigation?

UN4508.stem: A 68-year-old woman with long-standing COPD attends the respiratory clinic with a month of increasing swelling of both legs, which now pit to mid-shin. Which examination finding would most strongly indicate that the right side of her heart is failing?

A 35-year-old woman presents with progressive exertional breathlessness, syncope on exertion, and a right parasternal heave. ECG shows right axis deviation and right bundle branch block. Echocardiogram shows estimated RVSP of 70 mmHg (normal below 35 mmHg). Right heart catheterisation confirms mean PAP of 35 mmHg. What is the most likely diagnosis?

An older patient develops signs of predominantly right-sided heart failure (raised JVP, hepatomegaly, peripheral oedema) with exertional breathlessness. Echocardiography shows NORMAL-sized, non-dilated ventricles with PRESERVED systolic function but markedly impaired diastolic filling. Cardiac amyloidosis is suspected. What is the most likely type of cardiomyopathy?
Bibasal fine crackles are heard in a patient with left-sided heart failure. What causes this finding?

A 68-year-old man with long-standing COPD sees his GP because his ankles have been swelling and his abdomen has steadily enlarged over two months. Sitting at 45 degrees, his neck veins are distended almost to the earlobes. There is smooth, tender enlargement of the liver and shifting dullness in the flanks, yet the chest is free of crackles. Which diagnosis best accounts for these findings?

A 45-year-old woman with systemic sclerosis develops progressive exertional dyspnoea and a dry cough. HRCT shows bilateral lower-zone ground-glass change with fine reticulation and minimal honeycombing. What is the most likely interstitial lung disease pattern?

UN4508.presentation: Raised venous pressure and ankle oedema
UN4508.stem: A 70-year-old woman with right-sided heart failure due to pulmonary hypertension says her shoes no longer fit and her socks leave deep marks around both ankles by evening. Her jugular venous pressure is raised. Which mechanism is mainly behind the swelling in her legs?
UN4508.correct_answer: Raised venous pressure transmitted back to the capillaries

UN4508.stem: A 63-year-old woman attends her GP with two months of worsening exertional breathlessness and puffy legs. Sitting at 45 degrees, her neck veins are visibly distended up to the angle of the jaw, and fine crackles are heard at both lung bases. Which diagnosis best explains this combination of signs?

UN4509.stem: A 68-year-old man with severe COPD has worsening ankle swelling and abdominal fullness. Examination shows a raised JVP, hepatomegaly, pitting peripheral oedema and a loud pulmonary component of the second heart sound. Left ventricular function is preserved on echocardiography. What is the most likely diagnosis?
UN4509.correct_answer: Cor pulmonale (right heart failure secondary to lung disease)

UN4509.presentation: Raised venous pressure and ankle oedema
UN4509.stem: A 70-year-old woman with right-sided heart failure due to pulmonary hypertension says her shoes no longer fit and her socks leave deep marks around both ankles by evening. Her jugular venous pressure is raised. Which mechanism is mainly behind the swelling in her legs?
UN4509.correct_answer: Raised venous pressure transmitted back to the capillaries

UN4509.stem:
A 75-year-old retired joiner with long-standing ischaemic cardiomyopathy notices that his socks are leaving deep marks and his shoes feel tight. His GP finds pitting oedema to mid-shin on both sides and a raised jugular venous pressure. Urinalysis is normal and his albumin is within range.

Which process best explains the leg swelling?
UN4509.correct_answer: High venous pressure combined with renal retention of sodium and water

UN4509.stem: An elderly patient with heart failure becomes acutely breathless with a raised jugular venous pressure and HYPERTENSION about two hours into a red-cell transfusion, with pulmonary oedema on chest X-ray. What is the most likely transfusion complication?
A patient with chronic heart failure develops swelling of both ankles. What mechanism underlies this?
UN4509.correct_answer: Raised venous hydrostatic pressure with sodium and water retention

UN4509.stem: A 66-year-old woman with severe COPD, who uses home oxygen, is seen by her GP on a home visit. Over the past month her ankles and legs have become increasingly swollen and her abdomen feels full. She has a raised JVP with large systolic waves, a left parasternal heave, a loud pulmonary component of the second heart sound and a tender, enlarged liver. Her chest is hyperexpanded with no basal crackles. A recent echocardiogram showed a dilated right ventricle with normal left ventricular size and function. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old woman has 9 months of progressively worsening breathlessness on exertion. On examination she has a raised jugular venous pressure, a loud second heart sound in the pulmonary area and mild ankle oedema. Her ECG shows right axis deviation and her chest X-ray shows enlarged pulmonary arteries with clear lung fields. Which investigation should be done first to assess for pulmonary hypertension?
A patient who started amlodipine for blood pressure control several weeks ago now has new swelling around both ankles. Which adverse effect is the most likely explanation?

UN4511.stem: A 62-year-old smoker has shoulder and inner-arm pain with wasting of the small muscles of the hand. On the same side he has a drooping eyelid, a constricted pupil and reduced facial sweating. A chest X-ray shows an apical lung shadow. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN4511.presentation: Horner's syndrome from an apical lung tumour
UN4511.stem: A 62-year-old woman who smoked for 35 years sees her GP with 3 months of severe pain in her left shoulder that spreads down the inner side of her arm to her little finger. She has noticed weakness and wasting of the small muscles of her left hand. Her left upper eyelid droops slightly and her left pupil is smaller than the right, with no difference in eye movements. What is the most likely cause?

A 55-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes has several months of progressive shoulder pain and stiffness. Both active and passive movements are restricted, especially external rotation, and X-rays are normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A patient has a unilateral constricted pupil (miosis), partial drooping of the upper eyelid (ptosis) and reduced sweating on that side of the face (anhidrosis). What does this triad represent, and what serious cause must be considered?
UN4511.correct_answer: Horner's syndrome — consider a Pancoast (apical lung) tumour or carotid dissection

UN4511.stem: A patient is being investigated for a suspected malignancy. Which tumour marker is MOST classically associated with PANCREATIC cancer?

A 54-year-old man who works as a painter and decorator has had 2 months of right shoulder pain. The pain is felt over the outer upper arm, is worse when he works with his arm above his head, and wakes him when he lies on that side. There was no injury and he is otherwise well. Passive movement is full, active abduction is painful in the middle of the range and resisted abduction reproduces his pain. His GP diagnoses subacromial pain syndrome. He is keen to keep working. What is the most appropriate initial management?

A 64-year-old man known to have an aggressive lung tumour of small-cell type becomes muddled, and his sodium is found to be markedly low with no signs of excess fluid. What is the likely underlying mechanism?

A 52-year-old woman with hypothyroidism has had 3 months of left shoulder pain that began without any injury. The pain is severe, wakes her most nights and has not settled with regular paracetamol and ibuprofen, and the shoulder is becoming increasingly stiff. Active and passive movements are restricted in all directions, especially external rotation, and an X-ray of the shoulder is normal. Her GP diagnoses frozen shoulder (adhesive capsulitis). What is the most appropriate next step?

UN4512.stem: A 58-year-old woman sees her GP because her voice has sounded rough and croaky for two months. She drinks heavily, smoked for 30 years and has recently noticed a dull ache in her right ear. She has had no cold or sore throat, and otoscopy is normal. Which diagnosis must be excluded?

A 68-year-old man tells his GP that for six weeks his voice has been weak and breathy, and he gets short of breath when talking for long. He also has a hard, enlarging swelling in the left side of his thyroid gland. He has no difficulty swallowing and his tongue moves normally. Involvement of which structure best explains his voice change?

A 58-year-old publican, who has smoked 20 cigarettes a day for forty years, sees his GP because his voice has been croaky and rough for over a month. He had no cold beforehand, has no sore throat and the hoarseness has not improved. Examination of the neck is normal. What should the GP do next?
UN4512.correct_answer: Referral on the suspected cancer pathway to ENT

UN4512.stem: After undergoing pelvic surgery, a 61-year-old woman notices weakness when trying to straighten her knee and reduced sensation over the inner part of her lower leg. Which nerve is most likely affected?

A 68-year-old man, a current smoker with a significant pack-year history, presents with hoarseness that has persisted for several weeks with no improvement. He denies dysphagia or weight loss. Examination of the neck is unremarkable. What is the most appropriate next step?
UN4512.correct_answer: Suspected cancer pathway referral for laryngeal cancer

UN4512.stem: A patient awakens with a 'wrist drop' (inability to extend the wrist and fingers) after falling asleep with their arm draped over a chair. Sensation is reduced over the dorsum of the hand near the base of the thumb. Which nerve is affected?
UN4512.correct_answer: The radial nerve (at the spiral groove of the humerus)

UN4512.stem: A patient has weakness of the small muscles of the hand with a 'claw' appearance of the ring and little fingers, weak finger abduction/adduction, and sensory loss over the little finger and medial half of the ring finger. There is a positive Froment's sign. Which nerve is affected?
UN4512.correct_answer: The ulnar nerve (commonly at the elbow)

UN4512.stem: A 59-year-old publican who has smoked since his teens and drinks heavily tells his GP that his voice has been rough and croaky for the past two months. He had no cold beforehand, and voice rest has not helped. He has no stridor and no difficulty swallowing. Which action is most appropriate?
UN4512.correct_answer: Refer on a suspected cancer pathway to ENT

UN4513.stem: A 70-year-old man has a chest X-ray before elective hip surgery. He has no respiratory symptoms. The film shows bilateral, irregular calcified areas of pleural thickening along the diaphragms and lateral chest walls, with clear lung fields. He spent many years as a heating engineer fitting and stripping pipe insulation in old buildings. Which occupational exposure most likely explains these findings?
A patient is being investigated for a suspected malignancy. Which tumour marker is MOST classically associated with PANCREATIC cancer?

An elderly man who worked in shipbuilding decades ago has progressive breathlessness, chest-wall pain and weight loss. A chest X-ray shows a unilateral pleural effusion with irregular pleural thickening. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 22-year-old tall thin man presents with sudden left-sided pleuritic chest pain and breathlessness. Chest X-ray shows absent lung markings in the left hemithorax with a visible visceral pleural line. The mediastinum is central. What is the diagnosis?
A 39-year-old factory line worker develops ongoing forearm and wrist discomfort that flares during repetitive assembly work and settles on days off. What is the most appropriate first step?
UN4513.correct_answer: Evaluate the occupational exposure and consider a work-related musculoskeletal disorder

UN4513.stem: A new healthcare worker has no documented evidence of hepatitis B vaccination and is about to begin a role involving regular exposure to blood and body fluids. What is the appropriate approach?
UN4513.correct_answer: Hepatitis B vaccination should be offered based on the individual's occupational risk

UN4513.stem: A factory worker notices that his cough and wheeze are consistently worse during his shifts and improve markedly over weekends and while on annual leave. What is the most likely explanation?

UN4513.presentation: Suspected pulmonary fibrosis — key imaging investigation
UN4513.stem: A 69-year-old retired man has had 8 months of progressive breathlessness on exertion and a dry cough. He has finger clubbing and fine bibasal inspiratory crackles. Chest X-ray shows bilateral reticular shadowing at the lung bases, and spirometry shows a restrictive pattern. He is referred to the respiratory clinic. Which imaging investigation is most important to characterise his lung disease?

UN4515.presentation: Silicosis with new cavitation — investigation for tuberculosis
UN4515.stem:
A 62-year-old man who worked for 30 years as a stonemason has known silicosis. He sees his GP with 6 weeks of productive cough, night sweats and 5 kg weight loss. His temperature is 37.9°C. A chest X-ray shows a new cavitating lesion in the right upper lobe on a background of nodular upper-lobe changes.

Which investigation is most appropriate next?
UN4515.correct_answer: Sputum for acid-fast bacilli microscopy and culture

UN4515.stem: A 45-year-old woman with systemic sclerosis develops progressive exertional dyspnoea and a dry cough. HRCT shows bilateral lower-zone ground-glass change with fine reticulation and minimal honeycombing. What is the most likely interstitial lung disease pattern?

UN4515.presentation: Early Lung Disease With Liver Involvement
UN4515.stem: A 38-year-old non-smoker presents with breathlessness and is found to have evidence of emphysema on CT chest, alongside deranged liver enzymes. Blood testing reveals a deficiency of a specific protease inhibitor. Which pulmonary condition is this deficiency particularly associated with?

A 68-year-old heavy smoker is found to have hyponatraemia with concentrated urine and normal volume status. A chest X-ray reveals a new mass in the right lung. Why might this pulmonary finding be directly relevant to his sodium disturbance?
UN4515.correct_answer: Lung cancer or other lung disease can cause SIADH

UN4515.stem:
A 57-year-old woman who smoked 30 cigarettes a day until last year is admitted with 10 days of cough, malaise and poor appetite. Her chest X-ray shows a solitary cavity in the right upper lobe. The respiratory registrar is considering a lung abscess, a cavitating lung cancer and pulmonary tuberculosis while sputum results and a CT scan are awaited.

Which further finding would point most towards a lung abscess?
UN4515.correct_answer: Foul-tasting sputum that began after a recent seizure

UN4515.stem: A 58-year-old man newly diagnosed with COPD continues to smoke 20 cigarettes a day. Which single intervention would do the most to change the long-term trajectory of his lung disease?

UN4515.presentation: Suspected pulmonary fibrosis — key imaging investigation
UN4515.stem: A 69-year-old retired man has had 8 months of progressive breathlessness on exertion and a dry cough. He has finger clubbing and fine bibasal inspiratory crackles. Chest X-ray shows bilateral reticular shadowing at the lung bases, and spirometry shows a restrictive pattern. He is referred to the respiratory clinic. Which imaging investigation is most important to characterise his lung disease?

UN4515.presentation: Bullous lung disease — pneumothorax versus bulla
UN4515.stem: A 72-year-old woman with severe emphysema and known large apical bullae presents to the emergency department with 2 days of increased breathlessness. She is haemodynamically stable with oxygen saturation of 90% on air. Her chest X-ray shows a large hyperlucent area at the right apex with no lung markings; the radiologist cannot say whether this is a pneumothorax or a large bulla. What is the most appropriate next investigation?

UN4518.stem: A patient with advanced chronic kidney disease has the following biochemistry: HIGH phosphate, LOW calcium, and a markedly RAISED parathyroid hormone (PTH). What is the underlying process, and a key element of management?
UN4518.correct_answer: Secondary hyperparathyroidism — phosphate control, active vitamin D

UN4518.stem: A young adult has a dry cough, fatigue, painful red shin nodules (erythema nodosum) and joint pains. Chest X-ray shows bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, and serum calcium is mildly raised. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A patient is found to have a HIGH serum calcium. The parathyroid hormone (PTH) level is also raised (or inappropriately within the normal range for the high calcium). Renal function is normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old man with Burkitt lymphoma begins intensive chemotherapy. 24 hours later he develops oliguria and severe muscle cramps. Blood results show: potassium 6.2 mmol/L, phosphate 2.8 mmol/L (elevated), calcium 1.6 mmol/L (low), uric acid 750 µmol/L (elevated), and creatinine 280 µmol/L. What is the diagnosis and immediate management?
UN4518.correct_answer: Tumour lysis syndrome — IV hydration and rasburicase

UN4518.presentation: Recurrent Renal Stones With Raised Calcium
UN4518.stem: A 50-year-old woman has had three episodes of renal colic in the past two years and is found on blood testing to have a persistently elevated serum calcium concentration. Which endocrine disorder should be considered?

UN4518.presentation: Sarcoidosis — baseline screening for extrapulmonary disease
UN4518.stem:
A 41-year-old woman is diagnosed with pulmonary sarcoidosis in the respiratory clinic after an endobronchial ultrasound-guided lymph node biopsy shows non-caseating granulomas. She has a mild cough but no palpitations, chest pain, syncope or eye symptoms. Full blood count, renal and liver function and serum calcium have been requested.

Which additional baseline investigation is recommended for all patients with sarcoidosis?

UN4518.presentation: Hypercalcaemia with non-suppressed PTH — excluding familial hypocalciuric hypercalcaemia
UN4518.stem: A 44-year-old woman is found to have a raised albumin-adjusted calcium on two occasions during a health check. She has no symptoms, no kidney stones and no fractures. Her parathyroid hormone (PTH) level is within the upper part of the reference range, and her vitamin D level is normal. Her mother was told years ago that she had 'high calcium that did not need treatment'. Which investigation will best help distinguish primary hyperparathyroidism from familial hypocalciuric hypercalcaemia?
An asymptomatic woman is found to have a raised calcium with an inappropriately high (non-suppressed) parathyroid hormone level and a low phosphate. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN4686.stem: A 45-year-old woman has suspected asthma. She completes a 2-week peak flow diary showing an average morning peak flow of 320 L/min and average evening peak flow of 410 L/min. What does this indicate?
UN4686.correct_answer: Significant diurnal variability consistent with asthma

UN4686.stem: A patient with asthma is acutely breathless. Peak flow is 40% of predicted, with a respiratory rate of 26 and inability to complete full sentences, but no features of life-threatening asthma. How is this classified?

A 24-year-old woman with asthma is acutely breathless and cannot complete sentences. Respiratory rate 32, heart rate 120, SpO2 89% on air, peak flow 33% of predicted. The chest is quiet in places. What is the most appropriate immediate management?
UN4686.correct_answer: High-flow oxygen with back-to-back nebulised salbutamol and ipratropium

UN4686.stem: A 24-year-old woman with asthma is brought to the emergency department by her partner after two days of worsening wheeze despite frequent use of her blue inhaler. She is now drowsy and responds only to voice, her lips look blue and she is too breathless to attempt a peak flow reading. On auscultation there is very little air entry and almost no audible wheeze. How should this attack be classified?

A 19-year-old woman with known asthma develops worsening wheeze and breathlessness over several hours. She can only manage short sentences, and her peak flow measures 32% of her predicted best. What is the most appropriate immediate treatment?
UN4686.correct_answer: Oxygen, nebulised salbutamol and ipratropium, and a steroid

UN4686.presentation: Peak flow variability and reversibility — asthma
UN4686.stem: A 23-year-old woman sees her GP with several months of night-time cough, chest tightness and wheeze, worse in cold air. Her twice-daily home peak flow diary shows wide swings, with the lowest readings on waking. Spirometry shows a reduced FEV1/FVC ratio, and repeat spirometry 15 minutes after inhaled salbutamol shows a substantial rise in FEV1. What do these findings indicate?

UN4686.presentation: Suspected occupational asthma — next step in primary care
UN4686.stem:
A 36-year-old man who works as a vehicle paint sprayer has developed asthma for the first time over the past year. His symptoms are worse on working days and improve when he is on holiday. Serial peak flow readings at and away from work support a work-related pattern. He uses a low-dose inhaled corticosteroid and a reliever inhaler.

What is the most appropriate next step?
UN4686.correct_answer: Refer him to an occupational asthma specialist

UN4686.stem: A 34-year-old man who works as a spray painter in a car body shop has developed cough, wheeze and breathlessness over the past eight months. He has no history of childhood asthma. He notices his chest is tightest by the end of the working week and that he feels considerably better during his annual leave. Examination between episodes is normal. What is the most appropriate next investigation?
UN4686.correct_answer: Serial peak flow measurements at and away from work

UN4778.stem: A 46-year-old woman presents with sharp chest pain that worsens with inspiration and improves when sitting forward. ECG shows widespread saddle-shaped ST elevation. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 29-year-old man has had a cough with clear-to-yellow sputum and a low-grade fever for six days. He has no long-term conditions and is not systemically unwell. His respiratory rate is 16/min, oxygen saturation 98% on air, and there are scattered wheezes with no focal chest signs. He asks for antibiotics. Which is the most appropriate management?

UN4778.presentation: Fever, cough and fast breathing in a child
UN4778.stem:
A 6-year-old girl has had three days of fever and cough. She is breathing faster than expected for her age and has a sharp pain on the right side of her chest when she breathes in deeply. On examination, air entry is reduced and there are coarse crackles at the right base. The rest of the chest is clear and there is no wheeze.

What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 69-year-old woman presents with progressive exertional chest pain, dizziness and breathlessness. Examination reveals an ejection systolic murmur radiating to the carotids. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A 30-year-old man presents with recurrent chest pain and syncope. ECG demonstrates coved ST elevation in leads V1–V3. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A 49-year-old woman presents with burning retrosternal chest discomfort that occurs after large meals and worsens when lying down. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A 74-year-old man presents with sudden tearing chest pain radiating to the back. Blood pressure is 190/110 mmHg. Which risk factor is most strongly associated with this diagnosis?

A 28-year-old presents with chest pain shortly after using cocaine, with hypertension and tachycardia. Regarding pharmacological management of the chest pain and cardiovascular effects, which agent should be AVOIDED?

UN4779.stem: A patient with a suspected large pulmonary embolism becomes acutely hypotensive with signs of obstructive shock. What does this clinical picture represent?

A 45-year-old man arrives in the emergency department two days after a long-haul flight with sudden breathlessness and a sharp left-sided chest pain on inspiration. He is tachycardic, his blood pressure is normal and his oxygen saturation is mildly reduced on air. The chest X-ray is unremarkable. His two-level Wells score indicates that pulmonary embolism is likely, and his renal function is normal. Which investigation should be arranged next?

UN4779.presentation: Sudden Breathlessness in a Patient With a Known DVT
UN4779.stem: A woman recently diagnosed with a proximal DVT in her left leg suddenly develops severe breathlessness, pleuritic chest pain and a fast heart rate. What complication should be suspected?

UN4779.presentation: Suspected pulmonary embolism in pregnancy — investigation
UN4779.stem: A woman at 30 weeks' gestation attends with sudden pleuritic chest pain and breathlessness. She is alert, with a heart rate of 104 beats per minute, respiratory rate 24, oxygen saturation 95% on air and a blood pressure of 118/72 mmHg. Her legs are not swollen or tender. Pulmonary embolism is suspected. What is the most appropriate initial approach to investigation?
UN4779.correct_answer: Chest X-ray, followed by V/Q scanning or CTPA

UN4779.stem: On the fourth day after major abdominal surgery, a patient suddenly becomes breathless with pleuritic chest pain, a tachycardia and mild hypoxia. The chest is clear and there are no new infective features. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 48-year-old woman has a CT pulmonary angiogram confirming a segmental pulmonary embolism. She is haemodynamically stable with normal blood pressure and no right-heart strain, and has no active cancer. What is the most appropriate treatment?
UN4779.correct_answer: A direct oral anticoagulant (e.g. apixaban or rivaroxaban)

UN4779.stem: A 71-year-old man presents with acute chest pain and dyspnoea. Examination reveals unilateral leg swelling. CTPA confirms pulmonary embolism. Arterial blood gas is performed. Which blood gas abnormality is most commonly seen early in pulmonary embolism?

A 34-year-old woman taking the combined oral contraceptive pill presents to the emergency department with sudden right-sided pleuritic chest pain, breathlessness and a small amount of haemoptysis. Her heart rate is 108/min, blood pressure 126/80 mmHg and oxygen saturation 94% on air. A chest X-ray is normal. The two-level Wells score places her in the 'PE likely' group. She is not pregnant, has normal renal function and no bleeding risk factors. The CT scanner will be unavailable for the next 6 hours. What is the most appropriate management?
UN4779.correct_answer: Start interim therapeutic anticoagulation and arrange CTPA

UN4780.stem: During an exacerbation of severe COPD, a patient is given high-flow oxygen before arrival in hospital and becomes increasingly drowsy on arrival. Which complication should be specifically considered?

A 74-year-old woman with severe COPD, who uses nebulisers at home, is brought to the emergency department with increased breathlessness and green sputum. The paramedics have been giving her 15 L/min oxygen via a reservoir mask, and she has become drowsy. Her oxygen saturation is 99%. Which oxygen strategy is most appropriate?
UN4780.correct_answer: Change to controlled oxygen via a Venturi mask, aiming for 88-92%, and check an arterial blood gas

UN4780.stem: A patient with severe COPD is being assessed for long-term oxygen therapy. Which measurement is the key determinant of whether they meet the criteria for this treatment?

A 66-year-old woman returns to the surgical ward after an emergency laparotomy for a perforated diverticulum. A closed-suction drain has been left in the pelvis. Her family asks the trainee why it is there.

What is the main purpose of the drain?
UN4780.correct_answer: To allow blood, pus or other fluid to escape from the area

UN4780.stem: A patient with severe COPD has chronic hypoxaemia confirmed on arterial blood gases (when clinically stable). Which statement best describes long-term oxygen therapy (LTOT)?
UN4780.correct_answer: LTOT improves survival in stable chronic hypoxaemia if used at least 15 hours a day

UN4780.stem: Following several hours of profound low blood pressure during a septic illness, a patient's kidney function deteriorates, and microscopy of the urine reveals coarse, dark brown granular casts. What diagnosis fits best?

A 35-year-old man who is nervous about an upcoming occupational medical has a raised blood pressure when his GP measures it. The GP notices he is sitting with his legs crossed, his arm hanging unsupported, and has been talking throughout. What is the most appropriate approach before drawing conclusions from the reading?
UN4780.correct_answer: Correct the technique, repeat the reading and arrange out-of-office monitoring if it remains raised

UN4780.stem: Staff at a care home find a 79-year-old resident with insulin-treated diabetes slumped in bed. She makes snoring noises when she breathes and does not respond to her name. The attending paramedics confirm a very low blood glucose. Which principle should guide her immediate management?
UN4780.correct_answer: Give glucose by a non-oral route and support her airway

UN4781.stem: A 68-year-old man with known COPD and a history of chronic carbon dioxide retention is admitted with an infective exacerbation. Which oxygen saturation target is generally appropriate?

A 5-week-old boy is admitted with several days of forceful vomiting after every feed. He is dehydrated, and blood tests show a low chloride, low potassium and a raised bicarbonate in keeping with pyloric stenosis. Which change in his breathing would help to correct the acid-base disturbance?
UN4781.correct_answer: Slower, shallower breathing so that carbon dioxide accumulates

UN4781.stem: A patient with several days of profuse watery diarrhoea is found to have a metabolic acidosis on blood gas analysis. Loss of which gastrointestinal secretion is primarily responsible for this acid-base disturbance?

A 23-year-old man is found drowsy in a hostel after injecting heroin. His pupils are pinpoint and his respiratory rate is 6 breaths/min. Arterial gas analysis on room air shows: pH 7.21, PaCO2 9.1 kPa, PaO2 8.0 kPa, bicarbonate 25 mmol/L. Which acid-base disturbance is present?
A patient with an acute exacerbation of COPD has an arterial blood gas showing a LOW oxygen level together with a HIGH carbon dioxide level. How is this respiratory failure best classified?

A 16-year-old girl with newly presenting type 1 diabetes is admitted to the paediatric ward in diabetic ketoacidosis. The nurse notices that she is taking deep, sighing breaths at a fast rate, although her chest is clear and her oxygen saturation is normal. What is the physiological purpose of this breathing pattern?
UN4781.correct_answer: To lower arterial carbon dioxide as partial compensation for the acidosis

UN4781.stem:
A 19-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes has had two days of vomiting and abdominal pain and stopped taking her insulin. She is breathing deeply and rapidly. An arterial blood gas on room air shows:

- pH 7.21
- PaCO₂ 3.1 kPa
- HCO₃⁻ 11 mmol/L

Which acid–base disturbance is shown?

A 74-year-old woman with severe COPD, who has had previous admissions needing non-invasive ventilation, is brought to the emergency department breathless with an exacerbation. The paramedics have given 15 L/min of oxygen via a non-rebreather mask throughout the journey. On arrival her oxygen saturation is 98%, but she has become increasingly drowsy and has a bounding pulse and warm hands. An arterial blood gas shows a raised PaCO2 and acidosis. Which is the most likely explanation for her deterioration?

UN4782.stem: A 35-year-old man sees his GP with several months of cough at night, wheeze and chest tightness that come and go, with good weeks and bad weeks. He has never smoked. The GP plans objective testing to confirm the suspected diagnosis. Which result would most strongly support asthma?
UN4782.correct_answer: Airflow obstruction that improves substantially after a bronchodilator

UN4782.stem: An 87-year-old man is on day four of treatment for cellulitis of the leg. His daughter tells the ward doctor that he has hardly spoken today, is leaving his meals and keeps dozing off in the chair, which is unlike him. When woken he answers questions slowly and loses track halfway through. The nurses say he seems brighter at some times of day than others. Which diagnosis should be considered?

UN4782.presentation: Peak flow variability and reversibility — asthma
UN4782.stem: A 23-year-old woman sees her GP with several months of night-time cough, chest tightness and wheeze, worse in cold air. Her twice-daily home peak flow diary shows wide swings, with the lowest readings on waking. Spirometry shows a reduced FEV1/FVC ratio, and repeat spirometry 15 minutes after inhaled salbutamol shows a substantial rise in FEV1. What do these findings indicate?

A 34-year-old man who works as a spray painter in a car body shop has developed cough, wheeze and breathlessness over the past eight months. He has no history of childhood asthma. He notices his chest is tightest by the end of the working week and that he feels considerably better during his annual leave. Examination between episodes is normal. What is the most appropriate next investigation?
UN4782.correct_answer: Serial peak flow measurements at and away from work

UN4782.stem: A 34-year-old woman has repeated episodes of wheeze and cough, especially at night and after exposure to house dust, with no symptoms in between episodes. Which feature of her history most supports a diagnosis of asthma?
UN4782.correct_answer: The variability of her respiratory symptoms

UN4782.stem: A 2-year-old boy wheezes repeatedly whenever he catches a cold, but is entirely well between these episodes. Which diagnosis is most likely?
A 45-year-old woman has suspected asthma. She completes a 2-week peak flow diary showing an average morning peak flow of 320 L/min and average evening peak flow of 410 L/min. What does this indicate?
UN4782.correct_answer: Significant diurnal variability consistent with asthma

UN4782.stem: A 19-year-old man has recurring wheeze and cough, along with eczema and hay fever. Which condition commonly occurs together with this pattern?

UN4977.stem: A patient with asthma is acutely breathless. Peak flow is 40% of predicted, with a respiratory rate of 26 and inability to complete full sentences, but no features of life-threatening asthma. How is this classified?
An 8-year-old boy with known asthma becomes so breathless during an exacerbation that he can only speak in short, broken phrases rather than full sentences. What does this indicate?

A 24-year-old woman with asthma is acutely breathless and cannot complete sentences. Respiratory rate 32, heart rate 120, SpO2 89% on air, peak flow 33% of predicted. The chest is quiet in places. What is the most appropriate immediate management?
UN4977.correct_answer: High-flow oxygen with back-to-back nebulised salbutamol and ipratropium

UN4977.stem: A known asthmatic develops increasing breathlessness, audible wheeze and is now unable to complete full sentences. What is the appropriate immediate treatment?

A 19-year-old woman with known asthma develops worsening wheeze and breathlessness over several hours. She can only manage short sentences, and her peak flow measures 32% of her predicted best. What is the most appropriate immediate treatment?
UN4977.correct_answer: Oxygen, nebulised salbutamol and ipratropium, and a steroid

UN4977.stem: A 45-year-old woman has suspected asthma. She completes a 2-week peak flow diary showing an average morning peak flow of 320 L/min and average evening peak flow of 410 L/min. What does this indicate?
UN4977.correct_answer: Significant diurnal variability consistent with asthma

UN4977.presentation: Acute Asthma in a Child — Initial Treatment
UN4977.stem: A 6-year-old known asthmatic presents with an acute exacerbation: breathless with a widespread expiratory wheeze, able to talk in short sentences, with oxygen saturations of 93% in air. What is the most appropriate initial treatment?
UN4977.correct_answer: Inhaled salbutamol via spacer or nebuliser plus oral corticosteroids

UN4977.stem: A 34-year-old man who works as a spray painter in a car body shop has developed cough, wheeze and breathlessness over the past eight months. He has no history of childhood asthma. He notices his chest is tightest by the end of the working week and that he feels considerably better during his annual leave. Examination between episodes is normal. What is the most appropriate next investigation?
UN4977.correct_answer: Serial peak flow measurements at and away from work

UN4979.presentation: Unexplained haemoptysis with a normal chest X-ray — referral
UN4979.stem: A 47-year-old woman who has never smoked sees her GP after coughing up small amounts of fresh blood on several occasions over 3 weeks. She has no fever, no recent chest infection, no nosebleeds and takes no anticoagulants. Examination is normal. An urgent chest X-ray arranged last week is reported as normal. What is the most appropriate next step?
UN4979.correct_answer: Make a suspected cancer pathway referral

UN4979.presentation: Painful Red Eye in a Contact Lens Wearer
UN4979.stem: A 24-year-old who sleeps in her soft contact lenses presents with a painful red eye, photophobia and reduced vision over the past day. What diagnosis requires urgent consideration?

A 57-year-old woman who smoked 30 cigarettes a day until last year is admitted with 10 days of cough, malaise and poor appetite. Her chest X-ray shows a solitary cavity in the right upper lobe. The respiratory registrar is considering a lung abscess, a cavitating lung cancer and pulmonary tuberculosis while sputum results and a CT scan are awaited.

Which further finding would point most towards a lung abscess?
UN4979.correct_answer: Foul-tasting sputum that began after a recent seizure

UN4979.stem: A 68-year-old smoker has weight loss, a cough and a low sodium of 119. He is euvolaemic with concentrated urine and a low serum osmolality. A chest X-ray shows a central mass. Which lung cancer type is most associated with this paraneoplastic syndrome?

UN4979.presentation: Haemoptysis and Weight Loss in a Smoker
UN4979.stem: Over recent weeks, a 62-year-old man who has smoked heavily for decades has lost weight without trying, developed a cough that will not settle, and now notices blood in his sputum. What should happen next?
UN4979.correct_answer: Arrange urgent investigation for possible lung cancer

UN4979.stem: A case-control study of 200 patients with lung cancer and 200 controls without lung cancer finds that 120 cases and 60 controls smoked. What is the odds ratio for lung cancer in smokers vs non-smokers?

A 58-year-old woman sees her GP because her voice has sounded rough and croaky for two months. She drinks heavily, smoked for 30 years and has recently noticed a dull ache in her right ear. She has had no cold or sore throat, and otoscopy is normal. Which diagnosis must be excluded?

UN4979.presentation: Prolonged Neonatal Jaundice With Pale Stools
UN4979.stem: A newborn baby is still jaundiced at a few weeks of age and has been passing pale stools. Which diagnosis needs urgent consideration?

UN4980.stem: A 68-year-old man tells his GP that for six weeks his voice has been weak and breathy, and he gets short of breath when talking for long. He also has a hard, enlarging swelling in the left side of his thyroid gland. He has no difficulty swallowing and his tongue moves normally. Involvement of which structure best explains his voice change?

A 68-year-old man, a current smoker with a significant pack-year history, presents with hoarseness that has persisted for several weeks with no improvement. He denies dysphagia or weight loss. Examination of the neck is unremarkable. What is the most appropriate next step?
UN4980.correct_answer: Suspected cancer pathway referral for laryngeal cancer

UN4980.stem: A patient with a persistent cough, weight loss and night sweats is being investigated for possible active pulmonary tuberculosis. Which investigation is especially important for microbiological confirmation?

A 58-year-old woman sees her GP because her voice has sounded rough and croaky for two months. She drinks heavily, smoked for 30 years and has recently noticed a dull ache in her right ear. She has had no cold or sore throat, and otoscopy is normal. Which diagnosis must be excluded?

A 58-year-old publican, who has smoked 20 cigarettes a day for forty years, sees his GP because his voice has been croaky and rough for over a month. He had no cold beforehand, has no sore throat and the hoarseness has not improved. Examination of the neck is normal. What should the GP do next?
UN4980.correct_answer: Referral on the suspected cancer pathway to ENT

UN4980.presentation: Horner's syndrome from an apical lung tumour
UN4980.stem: A 62-year-old woman who smoked for 35 years sees her GP with 3 months of severe pain in her left shoulder that spreads down the inner side of her arm to her little finger. She has noticed weakness and wasting of the small muscles of her left hand. Her left upper eyelid droops slightly and her left pupil is smaller than the right, with no difference in eye movements. What is the most likely cause?

Over the past month, a 55-year-old man's voice has grown steadily more hoarse and he now struggles to swallow; on examining his neck, a firm lump can be felt. Which serious diagnosis needs to be ruled out urgently?

A 59-year-old publican who has smoked since his teens and drinks heavily tells his GP that his voice has been rough and croaky for the past two months. He had no cold beforehand, and voice rest has not helped. He has no stridor and no difficulty swallowing. Which action is most appropriate?
UN4980.correct_answer: Refer on a suspected cancer pathway to ENT

UN5132.stem: A 34-year-old woman has repeated episodes of wheeze and cough, especially at night and after exposure to house dust, with no symptoms in between episodes. Which feature of her history most supports a diagnosis of asthma?
UN5132.correct_answer: The variability of her respiratory symptoms

UN5132.stem: A 2-year-old boy wheezes repeatedly whenever he catches a cold, but is entirely well between these episodes. Which diagnosis is most likely?

A 2-year-old child has had three episodes of wheeze and breathlessness over the past year, all occurring exclusively during viral upper respiratory tract infections. Between episodes he is completely asymptomatic. There is no personal history of atopy, no eczema, and no family history of asthma. What is the most appropriate diagnosis?
A 19-year-old man has recurring wheeze and cough, along with eczema and hay fever. Which condition commonly occurs together with this pattern?

A 10-year-old boy develops a cough and audible wheeze whenever he plays football, but is entirely symptom-free at other times, including at rest between episodes. What does this pattern most likely suggest?

UN5132.presentation: Trigger-Related Wheeze in a Preschool Child
