UN5132.stem: A 3-year-old girl has had several episodes of wheeze and dry cough over the past six months, each triggered by running around or by cold weather, and fully settling between episodes. What is the most appropriate way to approach this presentation?
UN5132.correct_answer: Treat as suspected asthma based on the clinical pattern

UN5132.stem: A 9-year-old boy is brought to the GP by his mother. For the past year he has had a dry cough at night and episodes of wheeze, which happen even without colds. They are worse in spring and after visits to his grandmother's house, where there is a dog. He had eczema as a baby and his father has hay fever. A salbutamol inhaler from the out-of-hours service helped quickly. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old man who works as a spray painter in a car body shop has developed cough, wheeze and breathlessness over the past eight months. He has no history of childhood asthma. He notices his chest is tightest by the end of the working week and that he feels considerably better during his annual leave. Examination between episodes is normal. What is the most appropriate next investigation?
UN5132.correct_answer: Serial peak flow measurements at and away from work

UN5324.stem: A 65-year-old smoker has spirometry showing FEV1 1.4 L (55% predicted), FVC 2.8 L (88% predicted), and FEV1/FVC ratio 0.50. What is the interpretation?

A 65-year-old woman has progressive breathlessness and a dry cough. Spirometry shows FEV1 1.2 L (62% predicted), FVC 1.4 L (58% predicted), FEV1/FVC ratio 0.86. Body plethysmography confirms TLC of 65% predicted. What is the pattern of lung disease?

A 71-year-old retired accountant who has never smoked and has no occupational dust exposure sees his GP with 9 months of gradually worsening breathlessness on exertion and a persistent dry cough. He has finger clubbing and fine, velcro-like crackles at both lung bases. There is no ankle swelling and his JVP is not raised. Spirometry shows a reduced FVC with a normal FEV1/FVC ratio, and his gas transfer is reduced. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN5324.presentation: Peak flow variability and reversibility — asthma
UN5324.stem: A 23-year-old woman sees her GP with several months of night-time cough, chest tightness and wheeze, worse in cold air. Her twice-daily home peak flow diary shows wide swings, with the lowest readings on waking. Spirometry shows a reduced FEV1/FVC ratio, and repeat spirometry 15 minutes after inhaled salbutamol shows a substantial rise in FEV1. What do these findings indicate?

A 59-year-old woman who is an ex-smoker (25 pack-years) has chronic breathlessness and wheeze that varies through the day. Spirometry before salbutamol: FEV1 1.30 L (52% predicted), FVC 2.60 L, FEV1/FVC 0.50. After salbutamol: FEV1 1.82 L, FVC 2.85 L, FEV1/FVC 0.64. Blood eosinophils are 0.6 × 10⁹/L. Which is the best interpretation?

A 55-year-old man who has never smoked has a telephone consultation with his GP. He developed a cold in the spring and has had a dry, tickly cough ever since, now four months later. He feels otherwise well, has no breathlessness and has not coughed up blood. How should his cough be classified?
A new blood test for a disease is reported to have a sensitivity of 90%. What does this figure actually tell you?
UN5324.correct_answer: 90% of people with the disease will test positive

UN5324.stem: A 56-year-old man who smoked 30 pack-years has had asthma since childhood. Over the last 5 years he has developed daily breathlessness and a productive morning cough. Post-bronchodilator spirometry shows a persistently low FEV1/FVC ratio with a large improvement in FEV1 after salbutamol, and his blood eosinophil count is raised. He uses only a salbutamol inhaler and has had two exacerbations this year. Which maintenance treatment is most appropriate to add?
UN5324.correct_answer: An inhaled corticosteroid combined with a long-acting beta-2 agonist

UN5405.stem: A 34-year-old woman has repeated episodes of wheeze and cough, especially at night and after exposure to house dust, with no symptoms in between episodes. Which feature of her history most supports a diagnosis of asthma?
UN5405.correct_answer: The variability of her respiratory symptoms

UN5405.presentation: Trigger-Related Wheeze in a Preschool Child
UN5405.stem: A 3-year-old girl has had several episodes of wheeze and dry cough over the past six months, each triggered by running around or by cold weather, and fully settling between episodes. What is the most appropriate way to approach this presentation?
UN5405.correct_answer: Treat as suspected asthma based on the clinical pattern

UN5405.stem: A 15-year-old boy develops wheeze, tightness in his chest and a cough whenever he exercises, which settles once he rests. What is the likely underlying diagnosis?
A 19-year-old man has recurring wheeze and cough, along with eczema and hay fever. Which condition commonly occurs together with this pattern?

A 45-year-old man suddenly develops the worst headache of his life, reaching maximum intensity within seconds, followed by neck stiffness and photophobia. Which feature most strongly supports a diagnosis of subarachnoid haemorrhage?
UN5405.correct_answer: Meningism developing after a thunderclap-onset headache

UN5405.stem: A 38-year-old teacher has had five months of fatigue, poor concentration and low mood. She has stopped working. Her GP is considering whether she has ME/CFS or a depressive illness. Which feature most strongly supports ME/CFS?
UN5405.correct_answer: Delayed worsening of symptoms after minor exertion

UN5405.presentation: Acute Confusion During a Urinary Infection
UN5405.stem: An 88-year-old woman becomes acutely confused during treatment for a urinary tract infection. Her son reports that her alertness and attention seem to fluctuate throughout the day, and that she has never been confused like this before. Which feature most strongly supports delirium rather than dementia?
UN5405.correct_answer: Fluctuating attention and awareness over hours to days

UN5405.stem: A 2-year-old child has had three episodes of wheeze and breathlessness over the past year, all occurring exclusively during viral upper respiratory tract infections. Between episodes he is completely asymptomatic. There is no personal history of atopy, no eczema, and no family history of asthma. What is the most appropriate diagnosis?

UN5527.stem: A 68-year-old smoker has weight loss, a cough and a low sodium of 119. He is euvolaemic with concentrated urine and a low serum osmolality. A chest X-ray shows a central mass. Which lung cancer type is most associated with this paraneoplastic syndrome?

UN5527.presentation: Haemoptysis and Weight Loss in a Smoker
UN5527.stem: Over recent weeks, a 62-year-old man who has smoked heavily for decades has lost weight without trying, developed a cough that will not settle, and now notices blood in his sputum. What should happen next?
UN5527.correct_answer: Arrange urgent investigation for possible lung cancer

UN5527.stem: A patient with a persistent cough, weight loss and night sweats is being investigated for possible active pulmonary tuberculosis. Which investigation is especially important for microbiological confirmation?

A 71-year-old woman who smoked for 40 years is seen in the respiratory clinic. She has had a cough for 2 months, has lost 6 kg and has new finger clubbing. Her GP arranged a chest X-ray, which shows a left hilar mass with widening of the mediastinum. What is the most appropriate next investigation?
UN5527.correct_answer: Contrast-enhanced CT of the chest including the liver and adrenal glands

UN5527.stem: A patient over 55 has new, persistent dyspepsia with unintentional weight loss and early satiety. Examination reveals an enlarged left supraclavicular lymph node. What is the most appropriate action?
UN5527.correct_answer: Urgent upper GI endoscopy to investigate for gastric cancer

UN5527.presentation: Painless obstructive jaundice with suspected pancreatic cancer — imaging
UN5527.stem: A 72-year-old man presents with 2 weeks of painless jaundice, dark urine, and pale stools. He has lost 4 kg unintentionally. No abdominal pain. Examination: palpable non-tender gallbladder. What is the most appropriate imaging investigation?

A case-control study of 200 patients with lung cancer and 200 controls without lung cancer finds that 120 cases and 60 controls smoked. What is the odds ratio for lung cancer in smokers vs non-smokers?

UN5527.presentation: Lung cancer — troublesome dry cough in advanced disease
UN5527.stem: A 72-year-old man has locally advanced non-small-cell lung cancer and is not suitable for treatment with curative intent. He has a persistent dry, non-productive cough that disturbs his sleep. He is afebrile, there is no wheeze, chest examination is unchanged and a chest X-ray shows no new collapse, effusion or consolidation. Simple linctus has not helped. He takes regular paracetamol only. Which drug is most appropriate to reduce his cough?

UN5528.stem: A 45-year-old woman with systemic sclerosis develops progressive exertional dyspnoea and a dry cough. HRCT shows bilateral lower-zone ground-glass change with fine reticulation and minimal honeycombing. What is the most likely interstitial lung disease pattern?

UN5528.presentation: Suspected pulmonary fibrosis — key imaging investigation
UN5528.stem: A 69-year-old retired man has had 8 months of progressive breathlessness on exertion and a dry cough. He has finger clubbing and fine bibasal inspiratory crackles. Chest X-ray shows bilateral reticular shadowing at the lung bases, and spirometry shows a restrictive pattern. He is referred to the respiratory clinic. Which imaging investigation is most important to characterise his lung disease?

A 65-year-old woman has progressive breathlessness and a dry cough. Spirometry shows FEV1 1.2 L (62% predicted), FVC 1.4 L (58% predicted), FEV1/FVC ratio 0.86. Body plethysmography confirms TLC of 65% predicted. What is the pattern of lung disease?

A 34-year-old man with newly diagnosed HIV and a CD4 count of 120 cells/µL has several weeks of progressive exertional breathlessness and a dry cough. At rest his oxygen saturations are 96%, but they fall markedly after walking. The chest X-ray shows bilateral perihilar interstitial shadowing. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis has been taking methotrexate 20 mg weekly for eight months. She presents with a three-week history of progressive dyspnoea, dry cough, and low-grade fever. Chest X-ray shows bilateral interstitial infiltrates. Oxygen saturation is 93% on air. What is the most likely complication?

A 70-year-old man has a year of progressive exertional breathlessness and a dry cough. He has finger clubbing and fine bibasal late-inspiratory crackles. HRCT shows basal, peripheral honeycombing with traction bronchiectasis. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 71-year-old man has been diagnosed with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis by an interstitial lung disease multidisciplinary team. His forced vital capacity is 65% of predicted. He has stopped smoking and has been assessed for pulmonary rehabilitation. The respiratory consultant discusses a medicine to slow disease progression. Which medicine is most appropriate?

A 47-year-old man has polymyositis with a raised creatine kinase. He also has Raynaud's phenomenon and rough, cracked skin along the sides of his fingers (mechanic's hands). His myositis antibody panel is positive for anti-Jo-1 antibody. This result most strongly indicates that he should be assessed for which complication?

UN5532.stem: A 51-year-old woman develops fever, a productive cough and increasing breathlessness over two days. A chest X-ray demonstrates a new area of focal consolidation. What is the most appropriate treatment?
UN5532.correct_answer: Antibiotics guided by CURB-65 and local guidance

UN5532.stem: A 74-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department by her daughter after 3 days of cough, fever and increasing drowsiness. She is newly confused about the date and place. Respiratory rate is 32 per minute, blood pressure 96/58 mmHg, pulse 112 beats per minute and oxygen saturation 90% on air. Urea is raised. Chest X-ray shows left lower lobe consolidation. What is the most appropriate management?
UN5532.correct_answer: Admission, oxygen and IV antibiotics for high-severity pneumonia

UN5532.stem: A 62-year-old man is on day 4 of intravenous antibiotics for community-acquired pneumonia. He still has a fever and his CRP is rising. A chest X-ray shows a new moderate right-sided pleural effusion. What is the most appropriate next investigation?

UN5532.presentation: Fever, cough and fast breathing in a child
UN5532.stem:
A 6-year-old girl has had three days of fever and cough. She is breathing faster than expected for her age and has a sharp pain on the right side of her chest when she breathes in deeply. On examination, air entry is reduced and there are coarse crackles at the right base. The rest of the chest is clear and there is no wheeze.

What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 68-year-old man develops fever, shaking chills and a cough productive of rust-coloured sputum over 24 hours. He has sharp right-sided chest pain on breathing in. A chest X-ray shows consolidation confined to the right lower lobe. He has no recent travel, hospital admission or exposure to others who are unwell.

Which organism most commonly causes this community-acquired pneumonia?

A 71-year-old woman is seen on a GP home visit. For three days she has had shivering attacks, a cough bringing up rust-coloured sputum and a sharp pain in her right side when she breathes in. Her temperature is 38.6°C and she is mildly tachypnoeic but fully oriented. There is dullness to percussion at the right base with bronchial breathing and coarse crackles over the same area. Which diagnosis best fits?

A 78-year-old man with a history of stroke and dysphagia is admitted with a 48-hour history of cough, fever (38.8°C), and purulent sputum. He is tachypnoeic (RR 28/min) with coarse crackles in the right lower zone. A chest X-ray shows consolidation in the right lower lobe. He has a nasogastric (NG) tube in situ that was placed 5 days ago for feeding. What is the single most important immediate management step to prevent *recurrent* aspiration?
UN5532.correct_answer: Check the NG tube position with a chest X-ray or pH test (and confirm placement)

UN5532.stem: A 74-year-old woman with known ischaemic heart disease is three days into an admission for severe community-acquired pneumonia. Her hypoxaemia is worsening and a new chest X-ray shows bilateral infiltrates. The team is unsure whether this is acute respiratory distress syndrome or cardiogenic pulmonary oedema. Which investigation best distinguishes between them?

UN5534.stem: A 55-year-old woman with breast cancer presents with sudden breathlessness and pleuritic chest pain. Wells score for PE is calculated as 5. What is the most appropriate next step?

A 65-year-old man has fever, productive cough, and right-sided pleuritic chest pain. CXR shows opacification of the right lower zone with air bronchograms visible within the opacity. There is no volume loss. What is the diagnosis?

A 58-year-old woman develops sudden severe breathlessness, pleuritic chest pain, a rapid heart rate and a low blood pressure shortly after a long-haul flight. Which complication of pulmonary embolism is particularly concerning in this presentation?

A 46-year-old woman presents with sudden pleuritic chest pain and shortness of breath. She is tachycardic at 118/min and mildly hypoxic. She recently returned from a long-haul flight. Her blood pressure is 118/76 mmHg. What is the most appropriate next step?
UN5534.correct_answer: Calculate the Wells score, then D-dimer or CTPA accordingly

UN5534.presentation: Excluding PE With a Low Clinical Probability
UN5534.stem: A 35-year-old woman presents with mild pleuritic chest discomfort. Her calculated Wells score suggests pulmonary embolism is clinically unlikely. Which blood test is commonly used next to help exclude venous thromboembolism in this situation?

A 50-year-old woman has pleuritic chest pain and breathlessness. Using a validated clinical prediction tool, she is assessed as 'PE UNLIKELY'. She is haemodynamically stable. What is the most appropriate next investigation?

UN5534.presentation: Sudden Breathlessness in a Patient With a Known DVT
UN5534.stem: A woman recently diagnosed with a proximal DVT in her left leg suddenly develops severe breathlessness, pleuritic chest pain and a fast heart rate. What complication should be suspected?

A 55-year-old man develops pleuritic right-sided chest pain and breathlessness 10 days after an open inguinal hernia repair. Pulse is 104 beats per minute, blood pressure 132/80 mmHg and oxygen saturation 94% on air. CT pulmonary angiography shows segmental pulmonary emboli in the right lower lobe. Renal and liver function are normal and he has no history of cancer or bleeding. What is the most appropriate treatment?

UN6245.stem: An adult with asthma uses a short-acting beta-agonist (salbutamol) inhaler several times a week for symptoms. What is the most appropriate next step in management?
UN6245.correct_answer: Switch to as-needed low-dose ICS/formoterol (AIR therapy)

UN6245.stem: A 69-year-old woman with COPD confirmed on spirometry attends her annual review at the GP surgery. She stopped smoking last year, has completed pulmonary rehabilitation and is up to date with vaccinations. She uses a salbutamol inhaler several times a day and is still breathless when walking to the shops. She has had no exacerbations in the past year. There is no history of atopy, no variation in symptoms during the day and her blood eosinophil count is normal. What is the most appropriate change to her treatment?
UN6245.correct_answer: Add a long-acting muscarinic antagonist with a long-acting beta-2 agonist

UN6245.stem: A 34-year-old woman with mild asthma that is normally well controlled with a low-dose inhaled corticosteroid attends her GP. A neurologist recently started propranolol to prevent her migraines. Since then she has needed her reliever inhaler several times a day and wakes at night wheezing. What is the most likely explanation?
UN6245.correct_answer: Blockade of beta-2 receptors in the airways has caused bronchoconstriction

UN6245.stem: A 58-year-old man with mild asthma, previously well controlled on a low-dose inhaled corticosteroid, was started on propranolol for essential tremor by a locum a week ago. He now reports a night-time cough, chest tightness and needing his reliever inhaler several times a day. He has no fever or ankle swelling. Which mechanism best explains his deterioration?

UN6245.presentation: Asthma–COPD overlap — stepping down inhaled corticosteroid
UN6245.stem: A 62-year-old woman with asthma–COPD overlap is stable on an inhaled corticosteroid and long-acting beta-2 agonist combination inhaler. A locum proposes switching her to a long-acting muscarinic antagonist plus long-acting beta-2 agonist inhaler, with no inhaled corticosteroid, to reduce her pneumonia risk. She had a life-threatening asthma attack 4 years ago. Which is the most important risk of this change?
UN6245.correct_answer: Severe asthma attack from loss of corticosteroid

UN6245.stem: A 56-year-old man who smoked 30 pack-years has had asthma since childhood. Over the last 5 years he has developed daily breathlessness and a productive morning cough. Post-bronchodilator spirometry shows a persistently low FEV1/FVC ratio with a large improvement in FEV1 after salbutamol, and his blood eosinophil count is raised. He uses only a salbutamol inhaler and has had two exacerbations this year. Which maintenance treatment is most appropriate to add?
UN6245.correct_answer: An inhaled corticosteroid combined with a long-acting beta-2 agonist

UN6245.stem: A 50-year-old man with asthma reports needing his reliever inhaler almost every day because of recurring wheeze and breathlessness. What does this level of reliever use indicate?
A patient with asthma admits to using their salbutamol inhaler most days, sometimes more than once a day, to manage breathlessness. What does this pattern of reliever use most likely indicate?

UN6246.presentation: Infective Exacerbation of COPD — Oxygen Target
UN6246.stem: A 70-year-old man with known COPD attends with increased breathlessness, increased sputum volume and purulence. He is alert. While awaiting blood gases, what is the most appropriate INITIAL oxygen approach?
UN6246.correct_answer: Controlled oxygen titrated to a target saturation of 88–92% pending blood gases

UN6246.stem: A man with known COPD presents with three days of worsening breathlessness, increased volume of sputum, and sputum that has turned from white to green. What does this presentation represent?

A 70-year-old woman has years of chronic productive cough with large volumes of purulent sputum and recurrent chest infections. HRCT shows dilated, thickened bronchi with a 'signet-ring' sign. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN6246.presentation: Features of an Infective COPD Exacerbation
UN6246.stem: A 73-year-old man with known COPD becomes more breathless over three days and notices his sputum has turned from clear to thick and green. Which feature most strongly suggests an infective exacerbation rather than his usual baseline?
A patient reports years of repeated chest infections along with a daily cough that produces large amounts of thick, purulent sputum. Which underlying condition should be considered?

A 55-year-old man with a history of alcohol excess and a recent episode of reduced consciousness has two weeks of swinging fevers, malaise and a cough productive of large amounts of foul-smelling purulent sputum. Chest X-ray shows a cavity with an air–fluid level. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 74-year-old woman with severe COPD, who uses nebulisers at home, is brought to the emergency department with increased breathlessness and green sputum. The paramedics have been giving her 15 L/min oxygen via a reservoir mask, and she has become drowsy. Her oxygen saturation is 99%. Which oxygen strategy is most appropriate?
UN6246.correct_answer: Change to controlled oxygen via a Venturi mask, aiming for 88-92%, and check an arterial blood gas

UN6246.stem: A 51-year-old woman develops fever, a productive cough and increasing breathlessness over two days. A chest X-ray demonstrates a new area of focal consolidation. What is the most appropriate treatment?
UN6246.correct_answer: Antibiotics guided by CURB-65 and local guidance

UN6247.stem: A patient with COPD and known CO₂ retention has an infective exacerbation. What is the most appropriate initial oxygen strategy while awaiting a blood gas?

UN6247.presentation: Long-term oxygen therapy in COPD — eligibility
UN6247.stem: A patient with stable COPD has persistent chronic hypoxaemia (a low PaO₂ on repeated measurements when stable). They have stopped smoking. What intervention improves survival?
UN6247.correct_answer: Long-term oxygen therapy (used at least 15 hours a day)

UN6247.stem: A patient with severe COPD has chronic hypoxaemia confirmed on arterial blood gases (when clinically stable). Which statement best describes long-term oxygen therapy (LTOT)?
UN6247.correct_answer: LTOT improves survival in stable chronic hypoxaemia if used at least 15 hours a day

UN6247.stem: A 74-year-old woman with severe COPD, who uses nebulisers at home, is brought to the emergency department with increased breathlessness and green sputum. The paramedics have been giving her 15 L/min oxygen via a reservoir mask, and she has become drowsy. Her oxygen saturation is 99%. Which oxygen strategy is most appropriate?
UN6247.correct_answer: Change to controlled oxygen via a Venturi mask, aiming for 88-92%, and check an arterial blood gas

UN6247.stem: A man with known COPD presents with three days of worsening breathlessness, increased volume of sputum, and sputum that has turned from white to green. What does this presentation represent?
A 68-year-old man with known COPD and a history of chronic carbon dioxide retention is admitted with an infective exacerbation. Which oxygen saturation target is generally appropriate?

UN6247.presentation: Infective Exacerbation of COPD — Oxygen Target
UN6247.stem: A 70-year-old man with known COPD attends with increased breathlessness, increased sputum volume and purulence. He is alert. While awaiting blood gases, what is the most appropriate INITIAL oxygen approach?
UN6247.correct_answer: Controlled oxygen titrated to a target saturation of 88–92% pending blood gases

UN6247.stem: During an exacerbation of severe COPD, a patient is given high-flow oxygen before arrival in hospital and becomes increasingly drowsy on arrival. Which complication should be specifically considered?

UN6259.stem: A 34-year-old woman has repeated episodes of wheeze and cough, especially at night and after exposure to house dust, with no symptoms in between episodes. Which feature of her history most supports a diagnosis of asthma?
UN6259.correct_answer: The variability of her respiratory symptoms

UN6259.stem: A 35-year-old man sees his GP with several months of cough at night, wheeze and chest tightness that come and go, with good weeks and bad weeks. He has never smoked. The GP plans objective testing to confirm the suspected diagnosis. Which result would most strongly support asthma?
UN6259.correct_answer: Airflow obstruction that improves substantially after a bronchodilator

UN6259.stem: A 15-year-old boy develops wheeze, tightness in his chest and a cough whenever he exercises, which settles once he rests. What is the likely underlying diagnosis?

A 38-year-old teacher has had five months of fatigue, poor concentration and low mood. She has stopped working. Her GP is considering whether she has ME/CFS or a depressive illness. Which feature most strongly supports ME/CFS?
UN6259.correct_answer: Delayed worsening of symptoms after minor exertion

UN6259.stem: A 45-year-old man suddenly develops the worst headache of his life, reaching maximum intensity within seconds, followed by neck stiffness and photophobia. Which feature most strongly supports a diagnosis of subarachnoid haemorrhage?
UN6259.correct_answer: Meningism developing after a thunderclap-onset headache

UN6259.presentation: Peak flow variability and reversibility — asthma
UN6259.stem: A 23-year-old woman sees her GP with several months of night-time cough, chest tightness and wheeze, worse in cold air. Her twice-daily home peak flow diary shows wide swings, with the lowest readings on waking. Spirometry shows a reduced FEV1/FVC ratio, and repeat spirometry 15 minutes after inhaled salbutamol shows a substantial rise in FEV1. What do these findings indicate?

UN6259.presentation: Acute severe asthma in a child
UN6259.stem:
A 10-year-old girl with known asthma is brought to the GP surgery by her father after a day of worsening cough and chest tightness that followed a cold. She can say only a few words between breaths and is using her neck muscles to breathe. She is alert and talking sensibly, her lips are pink and there is widespread wheeze. Her blue reliever inhaler has given little benefit at home.

What is the most appropriate next step?
UN6259.correct_answer: Treat as a severe attack with bronchodilator and steroid

UN6259.presentation: Acute Confusion During a Urinary Infection
UN6259.stem: An 88-year-old woman becomes acutely confused during treatment for a urinary tract infection. Her son reports that her alertness and attention seem to fluctuate throughout the day, and that she has never been confused like this before. Which feature most strongly supports delirium rather than dementia?
UN6259.correct_answer: Fluctuating attention and awareness over hours to days

UN6260.correct_answer: Arrange urgent investigation for possible lung cancer

UN6260.stem: A patient with a persistent cough, weight loss and night sweats is being investigated for possible active pulmonary tuberculosis. Which investigation is especially important for microbiological confirmation?

A 68-year-old smoker has weight loss, a cough and a low sodium of 119. He is euvolaemic with concentrated urine and a low serum osmolality. A chest X-ray shows a central mass. Which lung cancer type is most associated with this paraneoplastic syndrome?

A 27-year-old woman attends the emergency department with fevers for two weeks and a cough producing blood-streaked sputum. Her chest X-ray shows several rounded cavitating lesions in both lungs, and echocardiography finds a large vegetation on the tricuspid valve. Which part of her history most likely explains this?

A 63-year-old man develops worsening swallowing difficulty, nasal-sounding speech and proximal limb weakness, with notably reduced tendon reflexes that increase slightly after sustained muscle contraction. Which condition should be considered, particularly given its association with small-cell lung cancer?

UN6260.presentation: Chronic Diarrhoea With Raised Inflammatory Markers
UN6260.stem: A 45-year-old man reports several months of loose stools and unintentional weight loss. Blood tests reveal a low haemoglobin and an elevated CRP. Which diagnosis should be considered?

A patient has weeks of cough, haemoptysis, night sweats, weight loss and fever, with upper-lobe changes on chest X-ray. Sputum is positive for acid-fast bacilli. What is the standard initial treatment regimen?
UN6260.correct_answer: RIPE for 2 months, then rifampicin and isoniazid

UN6260.stem: A case-control study of 200 patients with lung cancer and 200 controls without lung cancer finds that 120 cases and 60 controls smoked. What is the odds ratio for lung cancer in smokers vs non-smokers?

UN6261.stem: A 66-year-old woman who has smoked heavily for 40 years has a central lung mass on chest X-ray. She presents with nausea and new confusion. She appears neither dehydrated nor fluid overloaded, and she takes no diuretics. Blood tests show a low sodium with low serum osmolality; her urine is inappropriately concentrated with a raised urine sodium. Thyroid function and cortisol are normal. Which diagnosis best explains these findings?
UN6261.correct_answer: Syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion

UN6261.stem: A 68-year-old smoker has weight loss, a cough and a low sodium of 119. He is euvolaemic with concentrated urine and a low serum osmolality. A chest X-ray shows a central mass. Which lung cancer type is most associated with this paraneoplastic syndrome?

A 71-year-old woman who smoked for 40 years is seen in the respiratory clinic. She has had a cough for 2 months, has lost 6 kg and has new finger clubbing. Her GP arranged a chest X-ray, which shows a left hilar mass with widening of the mediastinum. What is the most appropriate next investigation?
UN6261.correct_answer: Contrast-enhanced CT of the chest including the liver and adrenal glands

UN6261.stem: A 22-year-old tall thin man presents with sudden left-sided pleuritic chest pain and breathlessness. Chest X-ray shows absent lung markings in the left hemithorax with a visible visceral pleural line. The mediastinum is central. What is the diagnosis?

A 68-year-old heavy smoker is found to have hyponatraemia with concentrated urine and normal volume status. A chest X-ray reveals a new mass in the right lung. Why might this pulmonary finding be directly relevant to his sodium disturbance?
UN6261.correct_answer: Lung cancer or other lung disease can cause SIADH

UN6261.presentation: Lung cancer — troublesome dry cough in advanced disease
UN6261.stem: A 72-year-old man has locally advanced non-small-cell lung cancer and is not suitable for treatment with curative intent. He has a persistent dry, non-productive cough that disturbs his sleep. He is afebrile, there is no wheeze, chest examination is unchanged and a chest X-ray shows no new collapse, effusion or consolidation. Simple linctus has not helped. He takes regular paracetamol only. Which drug is most appropriate to reduce his cough?

A 62-year-old smoker has shoulder and inner-arm pain with wasting of the small muscles of the hand. On the same side he has a drooping eyelid, a constricted pupil and reduced facial sweating. A chest X-ray shows an apical lung shadow. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN6261.presentation: Unexplained haemoptysis with a normal chest X-ray — referral
UN6261.stem: A 47-year-old woman who has never smoked sees her GP after coughing up small amounts of fresh blood on several occasions over 3 weeks. She has no fever, no recent chest infection, no nosebleeds and takes no anticoagulants. Examination is normal. An urgent chest X-ray arranged last week is reported as normal. What is the most appropriate next step?
UN6261.correct_answer: Make a suspected cancer pathway referral

UN6489.stem: A young adult has a dry cough, fatigue, painful red shin nodules (erythema nodosum) and joint pains. Chest X-ray shows bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, and serum calcium is mildly raised. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A 28-year-old woman recovering from a streptococcal throat infection develops several painful, tender red lumps over both shins. Which diagnosis is most likely?

A 34-year-old man presents to his GP with a 10-day history of fever, painful swollen ankles and tender red lumps on both shins. A chest X-ray shows bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy with clear lung fields. He has no cough, eye symptoms or weight loss. Serum calcium, renal function and liver tests are normal, and respiratory review finds normal lung function. What is the most appropriate management?
UN6489.correct_answer: NSAIDs for symptoms and clinical review; spontaneous resolution is expected

UN6489.stem: A 27-year-old man attends the medical admissions unit with a week of fever and painful, swollen ankles. On both shins there are several raised, tender, bruise-like red-purple lumps a few centimetres across, which are warm to touch. There are no blisters, ulcers or target lesions. His chest X-ray shows bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy. What are the skin lesions?

UN6489.presentation: Tender Shin Nodules After Sore Throat
UN6489.stem: A 29-year-old woman develops several tender, red, raised nodules on both shins about two weeks after a streptococcal sore throat. The lesions are firm swellings rather than open sores. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A young woman develops tender, red, raised nodules on the shins. They are not ulcerated and fade like bruises over weeks. What does this finding most warrant?

A 22-year-old woman has had tender red nodules on both shins for 10 days. She started a combined oral contraceptive pill 6 weeks ago. She has no sore throat, cough, bowel symptoms or joint swelling. Chest X-ray, throat swab, anti-streptolysin O titre and full blood count are normal.

What is the most appropriate management?
UN6489.correct_answer: Stop the pill and offer other contraception

UN6489.presentation: Tender shin nodules in Crohn disease
UN6489.stem: A 23-year-old woman with Crohn disease is reviewed in the gastroenterology clinic during a flare. She has developed several tender, warm, raised red lumps on both shins over the past week. They look like bruises and the overlying skin is intact. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN6903.stem: A patient with asthma is acutely breathless. Peak flow is 40% of predicted, with a respiratory rate of 26 and inability to complete full sentences, but no features of life-threatening asthma. How is this classified?

A 24-year-old woman with asthma is brought to the emergency department by her partner after two days of worsening wheeze despite frequent use of her blue inhaler. She is now drowsy and responds only to voice, her lips look blue and she is too breathless to attempt a peak flow reading. On auscultation there is very little air entry and almost no audible wheeze. How should this attack be classified?
An 8-year-old boy with known asthma becomes so breathless during an exacerbation that he can only speak in short, broken phrases rather than full sentences. What does this indicate?

UN6903.presentation: Asthma–COPD overlap — stepping down inhaled corticosteroid
UN6903.stem: A 62-year-old woman with asthma–COPD overlap is stable on an inhaled corticosteroid and long-acting beta-2 agonist combination inhaler. A locum proposes switching her to a long-acting muscarinic antagonist plus long-acting beta-2 agonist inhaler, with no inhaled corticosteroid, to reduce her pneumonia risk. She had a life-threatening asthma attack 4 years ago. Which is the most important risk of this change?
UN6903.correct_answer: Severe asthma attack from loss of corticosteroid

UN6903.stem: A 16-year-old girl with known asthma develops wheeze and chest tightness during a cross-country run on a cold morning. When the school nurse assesses her, she can talk normally in full sentences, her breathing rate is only slightly raised and she is alert and pink. What should she be given first for quick relief?

UN6903.presentation: Metabolic Effect of Repeated Bronchodilator Doses
UN6903.stem: A patient receiving repeated nebulised salbutamol for a severe asthma attack is found on blood tests to have developed a notable electrolyte abnormality. Which abnormality is most likely?
An otherwise healthy adult has acute diarrhoea and vomiting after a meal, with no severe dehydration and no significant comorbidity. What is the most appropriate general management?
UN6903.correct_answer: Oral rehydration and supportive care, generally avoiding routine antibiotics

UN6903.presentation: Acute Asthma in a Child — Initial Treatment
UN6903.stem: A 6-year-old known asthmatic presents with an acute exacerbation: breathless with a widespread expiratory wheeze, able to talk in short sentences, with oxygen saturations of 93% in air. What is the most appropriate initial treatment?
UN6903.correct_answer: Inhaled salbutamol via spacer or nebuliser plus oral corticosteroids

UN6904.stem: A 35-year-old man sees his GP with several months of cough at night, wheeze and chest tightness that come and go, with good weeks and bad weeks. He has never smoked. The GP plans objective testing to confirm the suspected diagnosis. Which result would most strongly support asthma?
UN6904.correct_answer: Airflow obstruction that improves substantially after a bronchodilator

UN6904.stem: An 8-year-old boy with known asthma becomes so breathless during an exacerbation that he can only speak in short, broken phrases rather than full sentences. What does this indicate?

UN6904.presentation: Peak flow variability and reversibility — asthma
UN6904.stem: A 23-year-old woman sees her GP with several months of night-time cough, chest tightness and wheeze, worse in cold air. Her twice-daily home peak flow diary shows wide swings, with the lowest readings on waking. Spirometry shows a reduced FEV1/FVC ratio, and repeat spirometry 15 minutes after inhaled salbutamol shows a substantial rise in FEV1. What do these findings indicate?
A 45-year-old woman has suspected asthma. She completes a 2-week peak flow diary showing an average morning peak flow of 320 L/min and average evening peak flow of 410 L/min. What does this indicate?
UN6904.correct_answer: Significant diurnal variability consistent with asthma

UN6904.stem: A patient with asthma is acutely breathless. Peak flow is 40% of predicted, with a respiratory rate of 26 and inability to complete full sentences, but no features of life-threatening asthma. How is this classified?

A 19-year-old woman with known asthma develops worsening wheeze and breathlessness over several hours. She can only manage short sentences, and her peak flow measures 32% of her predicted best. What is the most appropriate immediate treatment?
UN6904.correct_answer: Oxygen, nebulised salbutamol and ipratropium, and a steroid

UN6904.stem: A 24-year-old woman with asthma is brought to the emergency department by her partner after two days of worsening wheeze despite frequent use of her blue inhaler. She is now drowsy and responds only to voice, her lips look blue and she is too breathless to attempt a peak flow reading. On auscultation there is very little air entry and almost no audible wheeze. How should this attack be classified?

A 24-year-old woman with asthma is acutely breathless and cannot complete sentences. Respiratory rate 32, heart rate 120, SpO2 89% on air, peak flow 33% of predicted. The chest is quiet in places. What is the most appropriate immediate management?
UN6904.correct_answer: High-flow oxygen with back-to-back nebulised salbutamol and ipratropium

UN6907.stem: A 65-year-old man has fever, productive cough, and right-sided pleuritic chest pain. CXR shows opacification of the right lower zone with air bronchograms visible within the opacity. There is no volume loss. What is the diagnosis?

An 81-year-old woman is admitted from her care home with three days of cough productive of green sputum, and a chest X-ray shows right lower lobe consolidation. Staff say that until yesterday she was fully orientated, but she now does not know where she is or what day it is. She has bronchial breathing at the right base and a raised white cell count. Which feature most clearly indicates more severe pneumonia?

A 51-year-old woman develops fever, a productive cough and increasing breathlessness over two days. A chest X-ray demonstrates a new area of focal consolidation. What is the most appropriate treatment?
UN6907.correct_answer: Antibiotics guided by CURB-65 and local guidance

UN6907.presentation: Fever, cough and fast breathing in a child
UN6907.stem:
A 6-year-old girl has had three days of fever and cough. She is breathing faster than expected for her age and has a sharp pain on the right side of her chest when she breathes in deeply. On examination, air entry is reduced and there are coarse crackles at the right base. The rest of the chest is clear and there is no wheeze.

What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 70-year-old man has fever, productive cough and right-sided pleuritic pain. He is confused, with a respiratory rate of 32, blood pressure 88/56, and urea 8 mmol/L. What does his CURB-65 assessment indicate?
UN6907.correct_answer: High severity — admit and treat as severe pneumonia

UN6907.stem:
A 68-year-old man develops fever, shaking chills and a cough productive of rust-coloured sputum over 24 hours. He has sharp right-sided chest pain on breathing in. A chest X-ray shows consolidation confined to the right lower lobe. He has no recent travel, hospital admission or exposure to others who are unwell.

Which organism most commonly causes this community-acquired pneumonia?

A 71-year-old woman is seen on a GP home visit. For three days she has had shivering attacks, a cough bringing up rust-coloured sputum and a sharp pain in her right side when she breathes in. Her temperature is 38.6°C and she is mildly tachypnoeic but fully oriented. There is dullness to percussion at the right base with bronchial breathing and coarse crackles over the same area. Which diagnosis best fits?

A 58-year-old man is brought to the emergency department with a three-day history of fever and a productive cough. The team suspects pneumonia. His observations give a NEWS2 score of 9.

Using current NICE sepsis guidance, how should this score be interpreted?
UN6907.correct_answer: High risk of severe illness or death from sepsis

UN6912.stem: A patient with a suspected large pulmonary embolism becomes acutely hypotensive with signs of obstructive shock. What does this clinical picture represent?

A 48-year-old woman has a CT pulmonary angiogram confirming a segmental pulmonary embolism. She is haemodynamically stable with normal blood pressure and no right-heart strain, and has no active cancer. What is the most appropriate treatment?
UN6912.correct_answer: A direct oral anticoagulant (e.g. apixaban or rivaroxaban)

UN6912.stem: On the fourth day after major abdominal surgery, a patient suddenly becomes breathless with pleuritic chest pain, a tachycardia and mild hypoxia. The chest is clear and there are no new infective features. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 71-year-old man presents with acute chest pain and dyspnoea. Examination reveals unilateral leg swelling. CTPA confirms pulmonary embolism. Arterial blood gas is performed. Which blood gas abnormality is most commonly seen early in pulmonary embolism?

Three days after a total knee replacement, a 72-year-old woman becomes suddenly breathless and collapses on the orthopaedic ward. Her systolic pressure stays low despite fluids, her neck veins are distended and a bedside echocardiogram shows a dilated right ventricle. Clot is later confirmed in the main pulmonary arteries. How should this event be classified?

A 52-year-old man with metastatic pancreatic cancer develops pleuritic chest pain and breathlessness at home, and his left calf has been swollen for several days. In the ambulance he becomes grey and drowsy, with a systolic blood pressure of 76 mmHg and a pulse of 130 per minute. What does this picture indicate?

A 45-year-old man arrives in the emergency department two days after a long-haul flight with sudden breathlessness and a sharp left-sided chest pain on inspiration. He is tachycardic, his blood pressure is normal and his oxygen saturation is mildly reduced on air. The chest X-ray is unremarkable. His two-level Wells score indicates that pulmonary embolism is likely, and his renal function is normal. Which investigation should be arranged next?

A 34-year-old woman taking the combined oral contraceptive pill presents to the emergency department with sudden right-sided pleuritic chest pain, breathlessness and a small amount of haemoptysis. Her heart rate is 108/min, blood pressure 126/80 mmHg and oxygen saturation 94% on air. A chest X-ray is normal. The two-level Wells score places her in the 'PE likely' group. She is not pregnant, has normal renal function and no bleeding risk factors. The CT scanner will be unavailable for the next 6 hours. What is the most appropriate management?
UN6912.correct_answer: Start interim therapeutic anticoagulation and arrange CTPA

UN6914.stem: A 70-year-old man has a year of progressive exertional breathlessness and a dry cough. He has finger clubbing and fine bibasal late-inspiratory crackles. HRCT shows basal, peripheral honeycombing with traction bronchiectasis. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 71-year-old retired accountant who has never smoked and has no occupational dust exposure sees his GP with 9 months of gradually worsening breathlessness on exertion and a persistent dry cough. He has finger clubbing and fine, velcro-like crackles at both lung bases. There is no ankle swelling and his JVP is not raised. Spirometry shows a reduced FVC with a normal FEV1/FVC ratio, and his gas transfer is reduced. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 72-year-old retired man tells his GP that over the past year he has become increasingly short of breath walking up hills, and he has an irritating cough that produces no sputum. On examination he has finger clubbing and fine end-inspiratory crackles over both bases posteriorly. There is no wheeze, his jugular venous pressure is not raised and he has no ankle oedema. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN6914.presentation: Suspected pulmonary fibrosis — key imaging investigation
UN6914.stem: A 69-year-old retired man has had 8 months of progressive breathlessness on exertion and a dry cough. He has finger clubbing and fine bibasal inspiratory crackles. Chest X-ray shows bilateral reticular shadowing at the lung bases, and spirometry shows a restrictive pattern. He is referred to the respiratory clinic. Which imaging investigation is most important to characterise his lung disease?

A 5-month-old infant presents with 3 days of coryza, cough, poor feeding, and increased work of breathing. Examination shows a respiratory rate of 60, subcostal recession, and widespread fine end-inspiratory crackles with an expiratory wheeze. Oxygen saturation is 93% in air. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 71-year-old man has been diagnosed with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis by an interstitial lung disease multidisciplinary team. His forced vital capacity is 65% of predicted. He has stopped smoking and has been assessed for pulmonary rehabilitation. The respiratory consultant discusses a medicine to slow disease progression. Which medicine is most appropriate?

UN6914.presentation: Newly diagnosed idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis — non-drug management
UN6914.stem: A 72-year-old woman has just been given a diagnosis of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis by the interstitial lung disease multidisciplinary team, based on typical HRCT findings and lung function. She is breathless walking up one flight of stairs but manages her own shopping. Her oxygen saturation is 95% at rest on air and she does not desaturate on a walk test. Which is the most appropriate next step in her management at this stage?

A 48-year-old dairy farmer sees his GP in late winter. Several times this month, on the evenings after forking damp, mouldy hay to his cattle, he has developed fever, aches, a dry cough and breathlessness, which settle over a day or two. He has no wheeze and feels well at weekends when his son does the feeding. Fine inspiratory crackles are heard at both lung bases. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN7070.stem: A patient with known heart failure develops dullness to percussion and reduced breath sounds at both lung bases. What is the most likely explanation?

A 72-year-old woman presents with sudden onset chest pain and shortness of breath. Examination reveals absent breath sounds and hyperresonance to percussion over the right hemithorax. She is in respiratory distress and her trachea is deviated to the left. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 69-year-old woman presents with progressive exertional chest pain, dizziness and breathlessness. Examination reveals an ejection systolic murmur radiating to the carotids. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN7070.presentation: Sudden Breathlessness and Shock After Trauma
UN7070.stem: After a road traffic collision, a patient suddenly becomes severely breathless and hypotensive, with markedly reduced breath sounds on one side of the chest consistent with obstructive shock. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A known asthmatic develops increasing breathlessness, audible wheeze and is now unable to complete full sentences. What is the appropriate immediate treatment?

A 71-year-old woman is seen on a GP home visit. For three days she has had shivering attacks, a cough bringing up rust-coloured sputum and a sharp pain in her right side when she breathes in. Her temperature is 38.6°C and she is mildly tachypnoeic but fully oriented. There is dullness to percussion at the right base with bronchial breathing and coarse crackles over the same area. Which diagnosis best fits?

A 76-year-old man develops chest pain and breathlessness. Examination reveals a new early diastolic murmur. CT angiography confirms an ascending aortic dissection. Which valve abnormality is most likely present?

A 70-year-old man develops chest pain and hypotension shortly after an acute myocardial infarction. Examination reveals a new loud holosystolic murmur best heard at the lower left sternal border. What is the most likely complication?

UN7074.stem: A young adult has a dry cough, fatigue, painful red shin nodules (erythema nodosum) and joint pains. Chest X-ray shows bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, and serum calcium is mildly raised. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old man presents to his GP with a 10-day history of fever, painful swollen ankles and tender red lumps on both shins. A chest X-ray shows bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy with clear lung fields. He has no cough, eye symptoms or weight loss. Serum calcium, renal function and liver tests are normal, and respiratory review finds normal lung function. What is the most appropriate management?
UN7074.correct_answer: NSAIDs for symptoms and clinical review; spontaneous resolution is expected

UN7074.stem: A 27-year-old man attends the medical admissions unit with a week of fever and painful, swollen ankles. On both shins there are several raised, tender, bruise-like red-purple lumps a few centimetres across, which are warm to touch. There are no blisters, ulcers or target lesions. His chest X-ray shows bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy. What are the skin lesions?

A 72-year-old woman presents with sudden onset chest pain and shortness of breath. Examination reveals absent breath sounds and hyperresonance to percussion over the right hemithorax. She is in respiratory distress and her trachea is deviated to the left. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old woman presents with chest pain and shortness of breath. ECG demonstrates sinus tachycardia and an S wave in lead I, Q wave in lead III and T-wave inversion in lead III. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 46-year-old woman presents with sudden pleuritic chest pain and shortness of breath. She is tachycardic at 118/min and mildly hypoxic. She recently returned from a long-haul flight. Her blood pressure is 118/76 mmHg. What is the most appropriate next step?
UN7074.correct_answer: Calculate the Wells score, then D-dimer or CTPA accordingly

UN7074.presentation: Recurrent Painful Big Toe With Raised Urate
UN7074.stem: A 39-year-old man has recurrent episodes of intensely painful, red, swollen first metatarsophalangeal joints. Blood tests during an episode show a raised serum urate level. Which crystal is most likely to be found in his joint fluid?
A 7-year-old boy presents with both eyes red and gritty, with watery discharge, but his vision remains normal on testing. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN7075.stem: A 35-year-old man sees his GP with several months of cough at night, wheeze and chest tightness that come and go, with good weeks and bad weeks. He has never smoked. The GP plans objective testing to confirm the suspected diagnosis. Which result would most strongly support asthma?
UN7075.correct_answer: Airflow obstruction that improves substantially after a bronchodilator

UN7075.stem: A 34-year-old woman has repeated episodes of wheeze and cough, especially at night and after exposure to house dust, with no symptoms in between episodes. Which feature of her history most supports a diagnosis of asthma?
UN7075.correct_answer: The variability of her respiratory symptoms

UN7075.stem: A 2-year-old child has had three episodes of wheeze and breathlessness over the past year, all occurring exclusively during viral upper respiratory tract infections. Between episodes he is completely asymptomatic. There is no personal history of atopy, no eczema, and no family history of asthma. What is the most appropriate diagnosis?

A 9-year-old boy has recurrent episodes of severe central abdominal pain lasting one to several hours, associated with facial pallor and loss of appetite; he occasionally vomits but not always. He is completely well between attacks, and his mother has a history of migraine. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN7075.presentation: Abdominal Migraine and Functional Abdominal Pain
UN7075.stem: A 7-year-old girl is reviewed in the paediatric clinic with recurrent episodes of periumbilical abdominal pain over the past year. The episodes occur every 3 to 4 weeks, each lasts 4 to 6 hours, and the pain is intense enough to stop her playing and keep her off school. Every episode follows the same pattern, with pallor and nausea but no vomiting. She is completely well between episodes and has normal growth and development. Examination and investigations are all normal. There is a family history of migraine. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 66-year-old man with hypertension and a long smoking history has had three brief episodes this week, each lasting under ten minutes, of double vision, slurred speech and feeling unsteady on his feet. He is completely well between episodes and neurological examination today is normal.

Which arterial territory is most likely to be involved?
A 2-year-old boy wheezes repeatedly whenever he catches a cold, but is entirely well between these episodes. Which diagnosis is most likely?

A 32-year-old woman describes recurrent episodes that begin with zigzag lines and flashing lights in her vision lasting about 20 minutes. These are followed within an hour by a throbbing right-sided headache with nausea and sensitivity to light, lasting 4 to 6 hours. Between episodes she is well, and neurological examination is normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN7129.stem: A 68-year-old smoker has weight loss, a cough and a low sodium of 119. He is euvolaemic with concentrated urine and a low serum osmolality. A chest X-ray shows a central mass. Which lung cancer type is most associated with this paraneoplastic syndrome?

A 71-year-old woman who smoked for 40 years is seen in the respiratory clinic. She has had a cough for 2 months, has lost 6 kg and has new finger clubbing. Her GP arranged a chest X-ray, which shows a left hilar mass with widening of the mediastinum. What is the most appropriate next investigation?
UN7129.correct_answer: Contrast-enhanced CT of the chest including the liver and adrenal glands

UN7129.presentation: Lung cancer — troublesome dry cough in advanced disease
UN7129.stem: A 72-year-old man has locally advanced non-small-cell lung cancer and is not suitable for treatment with curative intent. He has a persistent dry, non-productive cough that disturbs his sleep. He is afebrile, there is no wheeze, chest examination is unchanged and a chest X-ray shows no new collapse, effusion or consolidation. Simple linctus has not helped. He takes regular paracetamol only. Which drug is most appropriate to reduce his cough?

UN7129.presentation: Progressive Swallowing Difficulty in an Older Smoker
UN7129.stem: A 68-year-old man with a 40-pack-year smoking history and regular heavy alcohol intake reports three months of worsening difficulty swallowing solid food and unintentional weight loss of 6 kg. What serious diagnosis must be excluded?

A 68-year-old man with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and a 40 pack-year smoking history presents to the emergency department with sudden right-sided chest pain and worsening breathlessness. His oxygen saturation is 89% on air, heart rate 104 beats per minute and blood pressure 132/80 mmHg. His trachea is central. Chest X-ray shows a right pneumothorax with a 3 cm rim of air laterally. What is the most appropriate management?
UN7129.correct_answer: Chest drain insertion and hospital admission

UN7129.presentation: Haemoptysis and Weight Loss in a Smoker
UN7129.stem: Over recent weeks, a 62-year-old man who has smoked heavily for decades has lost weight without trying, developed a cough that will not settle, and now notices blood in his sputum. What should happen next?
UN7129.correct_answer: Arrange urgent investigation for possible lung cancer

UN7129.stem: A 63-year-old man develops worsening swallowing difficulty, nasal-sounding speech and proximal limb weakness, with notably reduced tendon reflexes that increase slightly after sustained muscle contraction. Which condition should be considered, particularly given its association with small-cell lung cancer?

A 70-year-old man with small-cell lung cancer is found to have a sodium of 118 mmol/L on routine bloods. He is alert and asymptomatic, clinically euvolaemic, with low serum and inappropriately high urine osmolality. What is the most appropriate initial management?

UN7130.stem: A 65-year-old woman has progressive breathlessness and a dry cough. Spirometry shows FEV1 1.2 L (62% predicted), FVC 1.4 L (58% predicted), FEV1/FVC ratio 0.86. Body plethysmography confirms TLC of 65% predicted. What is the pattern of lung disease?
A 65-year-old smoker has spirometry showing FEV1 1.4 L (55% predicted), FVC 2.8 L (88% predicted), and FEV1/FVC ratio 0.50. What is the interpretation?

A 71-year-old retired accountant who has never smoked and has no occupational dust exposure sees his GP with 9 months of gradually worsening breathlessness on exertion and a persistent dry cough. He has finger clubbing and fine, velcro-like crackles at both lung bases. There is no ankle swelling and his JVP is not raised. Spirometry shows a reduced FVC with a normal FEV1/FVC ratio, and his gas transfer is reduced. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN7130.presentation: Suspected pulmonary fibrosis — key imaging investigation
UN7130.stem: A 69-year-old retired man has had 8 months of progressive breathlessness on exertion and a dry cough. He has finger clubbing and fine bibasal inspiratory crackles. Chest X-ray shows bilateral reticular shadowing at the lung bases, and spirometry shows a restrictive pattern. He is referred to the respiratory clinic. Which imaging investigation is most important to characterise his lung disease?

UN7130.presentation: Peak flow variability and reversibility — asthma
UN7130.stem: A 23-year-old woman sees her GP with several months of night-time cough, chest tightness and wheeze, worse in cold air. Her twice-daily home peak flow diary shows wide swings, with the lowest readings on waking. Spirometry shows a reduced FEV1/FVC ratio, and repeat spirometry 15 minutes after inhaled salbutamol shows a substantial rise in FEV1. What do these findings indicate?

A 56-year-old man who smoked 30 pack-years has had asthma since childhood. Over the last 5 years he has developed daily breathlessness and a productive morning cough. Post-bronchodilator spirometry shows a persistently low FEV1/FVC ratio with a large improvement in FEV1 after salbutamol, and his blood eosinophil count is raised. He uses only a salbutamol inhaler and has had two exacerbations this year. Which maintenance treatment is most appropriate to add?
UN7130.correct_answer: An inhaled corticosteroid combined with a long-acting beta-2 agonist

UN7130.stem: A 59-year-old woman who is an ex-smoker (25 pack-years) has chronic breathlessness and wheeze that varies through the day. Spirometry before salbutamol: FEV1 1.30 L (52% predicted), FVC 2.60 L, FEV1/FVC 0.50. After salbutamol: FEV1 1.82 L, FVC 2.85 L, FEV1/FVC 0.64. Blood eosinophils are 0.6 × 10⁹/L. Which is the best interpretation?

A 63-year-old man who has smoked about a packet a day since his teens sees the practice nurse because he gets breathless walking up hills. He has coughed up white sputum most winter mornings for several years. He never had childhood wheeze or hay fever, and his symptoms change little from day to day. Post-bronchodilator spirometry shows an obstructive pattern that does not reverse. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN7470.presentation: Suspected occupational asthma — next step in primary care
UN7470.stem:
A 36-year-old man who works as a vehicle paint sprayer has developed asthma for the first time over the past year. His symptoms are worse on working days and improve when he is on holiday. Serial peak flow readings at and away from work support a work-related pattern. He uses a low-dose inhaled corticosteroid and a reliever inhaler.

What is the most appropriate next step?
UN7470.correct_answer: Refer him to an occupational asthma specialist

UN7470.stem: A 55-year-old man who has never smoked has a telephone consultation with his GP. He developed a cold in the spring and has had a dry, tickly cough ever since, now four months later. He feels otherwise well, has no breathlessness and has not coughed up blood. How should his cough be classified?
A factory worker notices that his cough and wheeze are consistently worse during his shifts and improve markedly over weekends and while on annual leave. What is the most likely explanation?

A 34-year-old man who works as a spray painter in a car body shop has developed cough, wheeze and breathlessness over the past eight months. He has no history of childhood asthma. He notices his chest is tightest by the end of the working week and that he feels considerably better during his annual leave. Examination between episodes is normal. What is the most appropriate next investigation?
UN7470.correct_answer: Serial peak flow measurements at and away from work

UN7470.stem: A 71-year-old retired accountant who has never smoked and has no occupational dust exposure sees his GP with 9 months of gradually worsening breathlessness on exertion and a persistent dry cough. He has finger clubbing and fine, velcro-like crackles at both lung bases. There is no ankle swelling and his JVP is not raised. Spirometry shows a reduced FVC with a normal FEV1/FVC ratio, and his gas transfer is reduced. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old university student attends her GP with three months of a dry cough that wakes her most nights. She becomes wheezy and tight-chested when cycling in cold air, and the symptoms ease completely over a few days at a time. She had eczema as a child. Examination today is normal and she has never smoked. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old woman has repeated episodes of wheeze and cough, especially at night and after exposure to house dust, with no symptoms in between episodes. Which feature of her history most supports a diagnosis of asthma?
UN7470.correct_answer: The variability of her respiratory symptoms

UN7470.stem: A 35-year-old man sees his GP with several months of cough at night, wheeze and chest tightness that come and go, with good weeks and bad weeks. He has never smoked. The GP plans objective testing to confirm the suspected diagnosis. Which result would most strongly support asthma?
UN7470.correct_answer: Airflow obstruction that improves substantially after a bronchodilator

UN7471.stem: A 58-year-old publican, who has smoked 20 cigarettes a day for forty years, sees his GP because his voice has been croaky and rough for over a month. He had no cold beforehand, has no sore throat and the hoarseness has not improved. Examination of the neck is normal. What should the GP do next?
UN7471.correct_answer: Referral on the suspected cancer pathway to ENT

UN7471.stem: A 63-year-old man who has smoked 20 cigarettes a day since his teens sees his GP because his wife says his voice has become rough and croaky. It began about two months ago with a cold and has not improved since. He has no difficulty swallowing and has not noticed any lumps. Examination of the mouth and neck is normal. What is the most appropriate action?
UN7471.correct_answer: Suspected cancer pathway referral to ENT

UN7471.stem: A 66-year-old retired publican tells his GP that his voice has been croaky for about two months without any preceding cold. He now feels a lump in his throat and gets pain in his right ear when he swallows. He has smoked 20 cigarettes a day since his teens and drinks heavily. Which diagnosis must be excluded urgently?

A 35-year-old man sees his GP with several months of cough at night, wheeze and chest tightness that come and go, with good weeks and bad weeks. He has never smoked. The GP plans objective testing to confirm the suspected diagnosis. Which result would most strongly support asthma?
UN7471.correct_answer: Airflow obstruction that improves substantially after a bronchodilator

UN7471.stem: A 55-year-old man who has never smoked has a telephone consultation with his GP. He developed a cold in the spring and has had a dry, tickly cough ever since, now four months later. He feels otherwise well, has no breathlessness and has not coughed up blood. How should his cough be classified?

A 29-year-old man presents with pain on passing urine and discharge from the urethra after a recent episode of unprotected sex. Which investigation is commonly used to test for chlamydia and gonorrhoea?

UN7471.correct_answer: Antibiotics guided by CURB-65 and local guidance

UN7472.stem: Over recent weeks, a 62-year-old man who has smoked heavily for decades has lost weight without trying, developed a cough that will not settle, and now notices blood in his sputum. What should happen next?
UN7472.correct_answer: Arrange urgent investigation for possible lung cancer

UN7472.stem: An elderly man who worked in shipbuilding decades ago has progressive breathlessness, chest-wall pain and weight loss. A chest X-ray shows a unilateral pleural effusion with irregular pleural thickening. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 57-year-old woman who smoked 30 cigarettes a day until last year is admitted with 10 days of cough, malaise and poor appetite. Her chest X-ray shows a solitary cavity in the right upper lobe. The respiratory registrar is considering a lung abscess, a cavitating lung cancer and pulmonary tuberculosis while sputum results and a CT scan are awaited.

Which further finding would point most towards a lung abscess?
UN7472.correct_answer: Foul-tasting sputum that began after a recent seizure

UN7472.presentation: Cavitating lesion in a smoker — next imaging
UN7472.stem: A 63-year-old man who smokes 20 cigarettes a day is admitted to the medical ward after four weeks of fever, cough and weight loss. He has no history of alcohol misuse, seizures, dental disease or swallowing problems. A chest X-ray shows a cavitating lesion with an air-fluid level in the right upper lobe. Which imaging is most appropriate next to characterise the lesion and look for an underlying cause?

UN7472.presentation: Lung cancer — troublesome dry cough in advanced disease
UN7472.stem: A 72-year-old man has locally advanced non-small-cell lung cancer and is not suitable for treatment with curative intent. He has a persistent dry, non-productive cough that disturbs his sleep. He is afebrile, there is no wheeze, chest examination is unchanged and a chest X-ray shows no new collapse, effusion or consolidation. Simple linctus has not helped. He takes regular paracetamol only. Which drug is most appropriate to reduce his cough?

A 9-year-old child presents with a 3-week history of polydipsia, polyuria, unexplained weight loss, and fatigue. Random blood glucose is 18.5 mmol/L. Urinalysis shows glucose 3+ and ketones 2+. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A patient with a persistent cough, weight loss and night sweats is being investigated for possible active pulmonary tuberculosis. Which investigation is especially important for microbiological confirmation?

UN7589.presentation: Unexplained haemoptysis with a normal chest X-ray — referral
UN7589.stem: A 47-year-old woman who has never smoked sees her GP after coughing up small amounts of fresh blood on several occasions over 3 weeks. She has no fever, no recent chest infection, no nosebleeds and takes no anticoagulants. Examination is normal. An urgent chest X-ray arranged last week is reported as normal. What is the most appropriate next step?
UN7589.correct_answer: Make a suspected cancer pathway referral

UN7589.stem: A 66-year-old retired publican tells his GP that his voice has been croaky for about two months without any preceding cold. He now feels a lump in his throat and gets pain in his right ear when he swallows. He has smoked 20 cigarettes a day since his teens and drinks heavily. Which diagnosis must be excluded urgently?

UN7589.stem: A 68-year-old smoker has weight loss, a cough and a low sodium of 119. He is euvolaemic with concentrated urine and a low serum osmolality. A chest X-ray shows a central mass. Which lung cancer type is most associated with this paraneoplastic syndrome?

A 59-year-old woman sees her GP because her voice has been husky for two months and has not improved since a cold settled. Over the past month, meat and bread have started to feel as if they catch in her throat, and her clothes have become loose. She has smoked a pack a day since her teens and drinks heavily. There is no palpable neck mass. What diagnosis must be excluded urgently?
UN7589.correct_answer: Head and neck or oesophageal cancer

UN7589.stem: Someone on long-term lithium therapy is brought in unwell: he has been vomiting, his tremor has become coarse rather than fine, he is unsteady on his feet, and he is growing progressively more drowsy. Which diagnosis must be excluded urgently?

UN7589.presentation: Haemoptysis and Weight Loss in a Smoker
UN7589.stem: Over recent weeks, a 62-year-old man who has smoked heavily for decades has lost weight without trying, developed a cough that will not settle, and now notices blood in his sputum. What should happen next?
UN7589.correct_answer: Arrange urgent investigation for possible lung cancer

UN7589.stem: A 58-year-old woman sees her GP because her voice has sounded rough and croaky for two months. She drinks heavily, smoked for 30 years and has recently noticed a dull ache in her right ear. She has had no cold or sore throat, and otoscopy is normal. Which diagnosis must be excluded?

UN7633.stem: During an exacerbation of severe COPD, a patient is given high-flow oxygen before arrival in hospital and becomes increasingly drowsy on arrival. Which complication should be specifically considered?

UN7633.presentation: Acute Hypercapnic Respiratory Failure in COPD
UN7633.stem: A 68-year-old man with COPD has an infective exacerbation. Despite controlled oxygen, nebulisers and steroids, he remains drowsy and tachypnoeic. ABG on 28% oxygen: pH 7.28, PaCO2 9.0 kPa, PaO2 7.2 kPa, HCO3 30. What is the most appropriate next step?

UN7633.presentation: Drowsiness and Slow Breathing on Opioids
UN7633.stem: A patient taking a strong opioid analgesic for pain becomes increasingly drowsy, with breathing that is slow and shallow. Which adverse effect requires the most urgent attention?
A patient with an acute exacerbation of COPD has an arterial blood gas showing a LOW oxygen level together with a HIGH carbon dioxide level. How is this respiratory failure best classified?
A patient admitted with severe community-acquired pneumonia has an arterial blood gas showing marked hypoxaemia with a PaCO2 that is normal. What type of respiratory failure does this represent?

A 45-year-old man is on the high dependency unit with severe acute pancreatitis due to gallstones. On day three his breathing becomes rapid and his oxygen saturation falls despite high-flow oxygen. A chest X-ray shows diffuse bilateral shadowing with a normal heart size, and he has no fever above his previous level.

Which complication has most likely developed?

A 74-year-old woman with severe COPD, who has had previous admissions needing non-invasive ventilation, is brought to the emergency department breathless with an exacerbation. The paramedics have given 15 L/min of oxygen via a non-rebreather mask throughout the journey. On arrival her oxygen saturation is 98%, but she has become increasingly drowsy and has a bounding pulse and warm hands. An arterial blood gas shows a raised PaCO2 and acidosis. Which is the most likely explanation for her deterioration?

A 30-year-old man with acute liver failure is on the ward awaiting transfer to a specialist liver unit. Over 30 minutes he becomes sweaty, confused and drowsy, with a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 13. His heart rate is 110 bpm, blood pressure 112/70 mmHg and oxygen saturation 97% on air. What should be done first?

UN7972.stem: An adult with asthma uses a short-acting beta-agonist (salbutamol) inhaler several times a week for symptoms. What is the most appropriate next step in management?
UN7972.correct_answer: Switch to as-needed low-dose ICS/formoterol (AIR therapy)

UN7972.stem: A patient with asthma admits to using their salbutamol inhaler most days, sometimes more than once a day, to manage breathlessness. What does this pattern of reliever use most likely indicate?

A 69-year-old woman with COPD confirmed on spirometry attends her annual review at the GP surgery. She stopped smoking last year, has completed pulmonary rehabilitation and is up to date with vaccinations. She uses a salbutamol inhaler several times a day and is still breathless when walking to the shops. She has had no exacerbations in the past year. There is no history of atopy, no variation in symptoms during the day and her blood eosinophil count is normal. What is the most appropriate change to her treatment?
UN7972.correct_answer: Add a long-acting muscarinic antagonist with a long-acting beta-2 agonist

UN7972.stem: A 50-year-old man with asthma reports needing his reliever inhaler almost every day because of recurring wheeze and breathlessness. What does this level of reliever use indicate?

A 10-year-old boy develops a cough and audible wheeze whenever he plays football, but is entirely symptom-free at other times, including at rest between episodes. What does this pattern most likely suggest?

A 9-year-old boy is brought to the GP by his mother. For the past year he has had a dry cough at night and episodes of wheeze, which happen even without colds. They are worse in spring and after visits to his grandmother's house, where there is a dog. He had eczema as a baby and his father has hay fever. A salbutamol inhaler from the out-of-hours service helped quickly. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old woman with mild asthma that is normally well controlled with a low-dose inhaled corticosteroid attends her GP. A neurologist recently started propranolol to prevent her migraines. Since then she has needed her reliever inhaler several times a day and wakes at night wheezing. What is the most likely explanation?
UN7972.correct_answer: Blockade of beta-2 receptors in the airways has caused bronchoconstriction

UN7972.stem: A 58-year-old man with mild asthma, previously well controlled on a low-dose inhaled corticosteroid, was started on propranolol for essential tremor by a locum a week ago. He now reports a night-time cough, chest tightness and needing his reliever inhaler several times a day. He has no fever or ankle swelling. Which mechanism best explains his deterioration?

UN8125.stem: A patient with COPD and known CO₂ retention has an infective exacerbation. What is the most appropriate initial oxygen strategy while awaiting a blood gas?

A 74-year-old woman with severe COPD, who uses nebulisers at home, is brought to the emergency department with increased breathlessness and green sputum. The paramedics have been giving her 15 L/min oxygen via a reservoir mask, and she has become drowsy. Her oxygen saturation is 99%. Which oxygen strategy is most appropriate?
UN8125.correct_answer: Change to controlled oxygen via a Venturi mask, aiming for 88-92%, and check an arterial blood gas

UN8125.stem: A breathless patient with a known COPD history has an ABG: pH 7.26, PaCO₂ 9.0 kPa, PaO₂ 7.5 kPa on controlled oxygen, HCO₃⁻ 30 mmol/L. He is drowsy. Besides controlled oxygen, what is the most appropriate next step?

A 47-year-old man is on day 2 of an admission with severe acute pancreatitis. He becomes increasingly breathless, with a respiratory rate of 36/min, oxygen saturation of 86% on 15 L/min oxygen via a non-rebreathe reservoir mask, and he is using his accessory muscles. A chest X-ray shows bilateral diffuse infiltrates. His jugular venous pressure is not raised and his fluid balance is even. What is the most appropriate next step?

UN8125.presentation: Infective Exacerbation of COPD — Oxygen Target
UN8125.stem: A 70-year-old man with known COPD attends with increased breathlessness, increased sputum volume and purulence. He is alert. While awaiting blood gases, what is the most appropriate INITIAL oxygen approach?
UN8125.correct_answer: Controlled oxygen titrated to a target saturation of 88–92% pending blood gases
