An 81-year-old woman with known left ventricular systolic dysfunction is woken at night by severe breathlessness. She is sitting bolt upright, coughing pink frothy sputum, and has fine crackles to both mid-zones. Her oxygen saturation is in the low 80s on room air and her blood pressure is well maintained.

What is the most appropriate immediate management?
UN8125.correct_answer: Sit her up, give oxygen and intravenous furosemide

UN8125.stem: During an exacerbation of severe COPD, a patient is given high-flow oxygen before arrival in hospital and becomes increasingly drowsy on arrival. Which complication should be specifically considered?

UN8126.stem: A 16-year-old girl with known asthma develops wheeze and chest tightness during a cross-country run on a cold morning. When the school nurse assesses her, she can talk normally in full sentences, her breathing rate is only slightly raised and she is alert and pink. What should she be given first for quick relief?
A 15-year-old boy develops wheeze, tightness in his chest and a cough whenever he exercises, which settles once he rests. What is the likely underlying diagnosis?

A 34-year-old woman has repeated episodes of wheeze and cough, especially at night and after exposure to house dust, with no symptoms in between episodes. Which feature of her history most supports a diagnosis of asthma?
UN8126.correct_answer: The variability of her respiratory symptoms

UN8126.stem: A 35-year-old man sees his GP with several months of cough at night, wheeze and chest tightness that come and go, with good weeks and bad weeks. He has never smoked. The GP plans objective testing to confirm the suspected diagnosis. Which result would most strongly support asthma?
UN8126.correct_answer: Airflow obstruction that improves substantially after a bronchodilator

UN8126.stem: A 45-year-old man with adult-onset asthma and recurrent nasal polyps sprains his ankle playing football and takes ibuprofen bought from a pharmacy. Within an hour his nose becomes blocked and runny and he develops marked wheeze and chest tightness. He recalls a similar reaction some years ago after taking aspirin for a headache. What is the most likely explanation?
A 2-year-old boy suddenly starts coughing forcefully and develops a wheeze heard only over the right side of his chest while he is eating grapes. What is the most likely cause?

A 47-year-old woman with asthma attends the emergency department with acute wheeze and chest tightness that began about an hour after she took ibuprofen for back pain. She has no rash, her lips and tongue are not swollen and her blood pressure is normal. For several years she has had a constantly blocked nose and has lost her sense of smell. Anterior rhinoscopy shows grey, glistening, insensate masses in both nostrils. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old woman has had recurrent, unexpected episodes of intense fear over three months. Each lasts about ten minutes with palpitations, chest tightness, breathlessness, dizziness and a fear of dying. Between episodes she worries about having another. ECG, examination and thyroid function are normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN8333.stem: An 8-year-old boy with known asthma becomes so breathless during an exacerbation that he can only speak in short, broken phrases rather than full sentences. What does this indicate?
A known asthmatic develops increasing breathlessness, audible wheeze and is now unable to complete full sentences. What is the appropriate immediate treatment?

A 19-year-old woman with known asthma develops worsening wheeze and breathlessness over several hours. She can only manage short sentences, and her peak flow measures 32% of her predicted best. What is the most appropriate immediate treatment?
UN8333.correct_answer: Oxygen, nebulised salbutamol and ipratropium, and a steroid

UN8333.stem: A patient with asthma is acutely breathless. Peak flow is 40% of predicted, with a respiratory rate of 26 and inability to complete full sentences, but no features of life-threatening asthma. How is this classified?

UN8333.presentation: Acute Asthma in a Child — Initial Treatment
UN8333.stem: A 6-year-old known asthmatic presents with an acute exacerbation: breathless with a widespread expiratory wheeze, able to talk in short sentences, with oxygen saturations of 93% in air. What is the most appropriate initial treatment?
UN8333.correct_answer: Inhaled salbutamol via spacer or nebuliser plus oral corticosteroids

She has no fever, no recent chest infection, no nosebleeds and takes no anticoagulants. Examination is normal. An urgent chest X-ray arranged last week is reported as normal. What is the most appropriate next step?
UN8335.correct_answer: Make a suspected cancer pathway referral

UN8335.stem: A case-control study of 200 patients with lung cancer and 200 controls without lung cancer finds that 120 cases and 60 controls smoked. What is the odds ratio for lung cancer in smokers vs non-smokers?

UN8335.presentation: Lung cancer — troublesome dry cough in advanced disease
UN8335.stem: A 72-year-old man has locally advanced non-small-cell lung cancer and is not suitable for treatment with curative intent. He has a persistent dry, non-productive cough that disturbs his sleep. He is afebrile, there is no wheeze, chest examination is unchanged and a chest X-ray shows no new collapse, effusion or consolidation. Simple linctus has not helped. He takes regular paracetamol only. Which drug is most appropriate to reduce his cough?

UN8335.presentation: Cough persisting after 'bronchitis' in an ex-smoker
UN8335.stem: A 58-year-old man who stopped smoking 10 years ago was diagnosed with acute bronchitis six weeks ago. His cough has not settled. He has no haemoptysis, feels otherwise well and his chest is clear on examination. Which is the most appropriate next step?

A 68-year-old heavy smoker is found to have hyponatraemia with concentrated urine and normal volume status. A chest X-ray reveals a new mass in the right lung. Why might this pulmonary finding be directly relevant to his sodium disturbance?
UN8335.correct_answer: Lung cancer or other lung disease can cause SIADH

UN8872.correct_answer: Start the Sepsis Six and escalate to critical care outreach

UN8872.stem: A frail older inpatient becomes acutely confused over two days, with fluctuating attention and altered consciousness, in the context of a urinary tract infection. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN8872.correct_answer: Identify and treat the cause (e.g. infection, pain, constipation, drugs)

UN8874.stem: A woman recently diagnosed with a proximal DVT in her left leg suddenly develops severe breathlessness, pleuritic chest pain and a fast heart rate. What complication should be suspected?
A 55-year-old woman with breast cancer presents with sudden breathlessness and pleuritic chest pain. Wells score for PE is calculated as 5. What is the most appropriate next step?

A 39-year-old man attends the urgent treatment centre two days after returning from Australia, a journey with over 20 hours of flying. His left calf has become tense, warm and painful and his ankle is visibly puffier than the right. He has no breathlessness or chest pain. Which diagnosis should be excluded first?

A 58-year-old woman develops sudden severe breathlessness, pleuritic chest pain, a rapid heart rate and a low blood pressure shortly after a long-haul flight. Which complication of pulmonary embolism is particularly concerning in this presentation?

There is no erythema or warmth, and she is afebrile. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A 58-year-old woman develops a painful, swollen calf in one leg several days after major surgery. Which diagnosis must be considered?

A 61-year-old woman receiving chemotherapy for ovarian cancer telephones her GP practice. Over the last day her right calf has become sore and her right leg looks thicker than the left, with pitting at the ankle. She has not had any injury. What diagnosis should the GP suspect?

UN8887.correct_answer: Treat as suspected asthma based on the clinical pattern

UN8887.stem: A patient treated for anaphylaxis after a wasp sting appears to recover fully, but several hours later develops recurrent wheeze and hypotension without any further sting or allergen exposure. What is this phenomenon called?
A patient who started ramipril a few weeks ago develops recurrent episodes of non-itchy swelling of the lips and tongue, without urticaria. What is the most likely cause and the key action?
UN8887.correct_answer: ACE inhibitor-induced angioedema — stop the ACE inhibitor permanently

UN9241.stem: A 31-year-old man develops sneezing, nasal blockage and watery, itchy eyes every year during the spring pollen season. Symptoms settle completely over winter. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN9241.presentation: Recurrent Facial Pain With Nasal Discharge
UN9241.stem: A 39-year-old woman has recurring bouts of facial pain, a blocked nose and thick nasal discharge lasting several days whenever she catches a cold. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old man is seen in the emergency department 20 minutes after sharing a takeaway curry containing cashew nuts. His lips have become itchy, he has crampy central abdominal pain with two episodes of loose stool, and a wheeze is audible on auscultation. He has never had symptoms like this before. Which mechanism best explains his reaction?
UN9241.correct_answer: IgE-mediated immediate hypersensitivity to a food

UN9241.stem: A 22-year-old trainee gardener sees his GP because every May he gets bouts of sneezing, an itchy runny nose and itchy, watering eyes. He does not have nasal blockage. He would like a tablet to take on bad days that will not make him drowsy at work. Which treatment is most appropriate?
UN9241.correct_answer: Non-sedating oral antihistamine such as cetirizine

UN9241.stem: An 8-year-old girl is seen in a paediatric allergy clinic. At a birthday party she ate a biscuit containing peanut, and within 15 minutes her lips swelled, she developed raised itchy weals over her neck, vomited twice and started coughing. Her symptoms settled after treatment by paramedics. Which immunological mechanism best explains this reaction?
A 28-year-old otherwise healthy woman develops facial pressure, nasal blockage and thick nasal discharge for three days, along with mild fatigue. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 40-year-old woman has had nasal blockage, facial pressure and a reduced sense of smell continuously for the past four months, with no clear improvement. Which diagnosis is most consistent with this presentation?

A 14-year-old girl with cystic fibrosis attends clinic with a two-year decline in lung function and frequent exacerbations. She brings up thick, discoloured sputum most days. Cultures in early childhood grew Staphylococcus aureus, but the cystic fibrosis team now describes a pattern of chronic infection with a different organism that is hard to eradicate, and they are planning long-term inhaled antibiotic treatment.

Which organism is most characteristically associated with this stage of chronic lung infection in cystic fibrosis?
UN9320.correct_answer: Chronic Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection of the lungs

Her medicines include aspirin, a statin, bisoprolol and perindopril. She has no wheeze, fever or sputum, and her chest is clear. Which mechanism most likely explains her cough?

He is tachycardic, his blood pressure is normal and his oxygen saturation is mildly reduced on air. The chest X-ray is unremarkable. His two-level Wells score indicates that pulmonary embolism is likely, and his renal function is normal. Which investigation should be arranged next?
A 55-year-old woman with breast cancer presents with sudden breathlessness and pleuritic chest pain. Wells score for PE is calculated as 5. What is the most appropriate next step?

A 55-year-old man develops pleuritic right-sided chest pain and breathlessness 10 days after an open inguinal hernia repair. Pulse is 104 beats per minute, blood pressure 132/80 mmHg and oxygen saturation 94% on air. CT pulmonary angiography shows segmental pulmonary emboli in the right lower lobe. Renal and liver function are normal and he has no history of cancer or bleeding. What is the most appropriate treatment?

A 71-year-old man presents with acute chest pain and dyspnoea. Examination reveals unilateral leg swelling. CTPA confirms pulmonary embolism. Arterial blood gas is performed. Which blood gas abnormality is most commonly seen early in pulmonary embolism?

A 48-year-old woman has a CT pulmonary angiogram confirming a segmental pulmonary embolism. She is haemodynamically stable with normal blood pressure and no right-heart strain, and has no active cancer. What is the most appropriate treatment?
UN9417.correct_answer: A direct oral anticoagulant (e.g. apixaban or rivaroxaban)

UN9417.presentation: Sudden Breathlessness in a Patient With a Known DVT
UN9417.stem: A woman recently diagnosed with a proximal DVT in her left leg suddenly develops severe breathlessness, pleuritic chest pain and a fast heart rate. What complication should be suspected?

UN9417.presentation: Suspected pulmonary embolism in pregnancy — investigation
UN9417.stem: A woman at 30 weeks' gestation attends with sudden pleuritic chest pain and breathlessness. She is alert, with a heart rate of 104 beats per minute, respiratory rate 24, oxygen saturation 95% on air and a blood pressure of 118/72 mmHg. Her legs are not swollen or tender. Pulmonary embolism is suspected. What is the most appropriate initial approach to investigation?
UN9417.correct_answer: Chest X-ray, followed by V/Q scanning or CTPA

UN9417.stem: On the fourth day after major abdominal surgery, a patient suddenly becomes breathless with pleuritic chest pain, a tachycardia and mild hypoxia. The chest is clear and there are no new infective features. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN9459.stem: A 68-year-old man with known COPD and a history of chronic carbon dioxide retention is admitted with an infective exacerbation. Which oxygen saturation target is generally appropriate?
A patient with COPD and known CO₂ retention has an infective exacerbation. What is the most appropriate initial oxygen strategy while awaiting a blood gas?

UN9459.presentation: Infective Exacerbation of COPD — Oxygen Target
UN9459.stem: A 70-year-old man with known COPD attends with increased breathlessness, increased sputum volume and purulence. He is alert. While awaiting blood gases, what is the most appropriate INITIAL oxygen approach?
UN9459.correct_answer: Controlled oxygen titrated to a target saturation of 88–92% pending blood gases

UN9459.stem: A 74-year-old woman with severe COPD, who uses nebulisers at home, is brought to the emergency department with increased breathlessness and green sputum. The paramedics have been giving her 15 L/min oxygen via a reservoir mask, and she has become drowsy. Her oxygen saturation is 99%. Which oxygen strategy is most appropriate?
UN9459.correct_answer: Change to controlled oxygen via a Venturi mask, aiming for 88-92%, and check an arterial blood gas

UN9459.stem: A 69-year-old man with known COPD is brought to the emergency department by ambulance with an exacerbation. The crew gave high-flow oxygen through a non-rebreathe mask throughout the journey. On arrival he is increasingly drowsy and difficult to rouse. Pulse oximetry reads 99%, his hands are warm with a bounding pulse, and he has a coarse flapping tremor. His temperature is 37.3°C, capillary glucose is normal, he has not received any sedating medicines and he has no known liver disease. What is the most likely cause of his reduced consciousness?
UN9459.correct_answer: Carbon dioxide retention worsened by uncontrolled oxygen

UN9459.stem: A 74-year-old woman with severe COPD, who has had previous admissions needing non-invasive ventilation, is brought to the emergency department breathless with an exacerbation. The paramedics have given 15 L/min of oxygen via a non-rebreather mask throughout the journey. On arrival her oxygen saturation is 98%, but she has become increasingly drowsy and has a bounding pulse and warm hands. An arterial blood gas shows a raised PaCO2 and acidosis. Which is the most likely explanation for her deterioration?

A foundation doctor on a medical ward is asked to write up oxygen for a 45-year-old man admitted with community-acquired pneumonia. He has no history of lung disease or other risk factors for carbon dioxide retention, and he is mildly hypoxic on air. Which approach to his oxygen prescription is most appropriate?
UN9459.correct_answer: Prescribe oxygen to a target saturation range suited to him and titrate to it

UN9459.stem: A patient with an acute exacerbation of COPD has an arterial blood gas showing a LOW oxygen level together with a HIGH carbon dioxide level. How is this respiratory failure best classified?

UN9636.stem: A 35-year-old man sees his GP with several months of cough at night, wheeze and chest tightness that come and go, with good weeks and bad weeks. He has never smoked. The GP plans objective testing to confirm the suspected diagnosis. Which result would most strongly support asthma?
UN9636.correct_answer: Airflow obstruction that improves substantially after a bronchodilator

UN9636.presentation: Peak flow variability and reversibility — asthma
UN9636.stem: A 23-year-old woman sees her GP with several months of night-time cough, chest tightness and wheeze, worse in cold air. Her twice-daily home peak flow diary shows wide swings, with the lowest readings on waking. Spirometry shows a reduced FEV1/FVC ratio, and repeat spirometry 15 minutes after inhaled salbutamol shows a substantial rise in FEV1. What do these findings indicate?

A 34-year-old woman has repeated episodes of wheeze and cough, especially at night and after exposure to house dust, with no symptoms in between episodes. Which feature of her history most supports a diagnosis of asthma?
UN9636.correct_answer: The variability of her respiratory symptoms

UN9636.presentation: Acute severe asthma in a child
UN9636.stem:
A 10-year-old girl with known asthma is brought to the GP surgery by her father after a day of worsening cough and chest tightness that followed a cold. She can say only a few words between breaths and is using her neck muscles to breathe. She is alert and talking sensibly, her lips are pink and there is widespread wheeze. Her blue reliever inhaler has given little benefit at home.

What is the most appropriate next step?
UN9636.correct_answer: Treat as a severe attack with bronchodilator and steroid

UN9636.stem: A 15-year-old boy develops wheeze, tightness in his chest and a cough whenever he exercises, which settles once he rests. What is the likely underlying diagnosis?

A 34-year-old woman who drinks very little alcohol is seen in the hepatology clinic after ultrasound showed a cirrhotic liver. Viral hepatitis serology and autoimmune liver screen are negative, and her ferritin and caeruloplasmin are normal. She mentions she has become breathless climbing stairs, and spirometry shows airflow obstruction. Her older brother needed a lung transplant in his forties. Which inherited disorder is most likely?

A 27-year-old woman has had recurrent, unexpected episodes of intense fear over three months. Each lasts about ten minutes with palpitations, chest tightness, breathlessness, dizziness and a fear of dying. Between episodes she worries about having another. ECG, examination and thyroid function are normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 9-year-old boy with asthma is reviewed by the practice nurse. His mother says his cough and wheeze flare every year from late spring into summer, at the same time as he has sneezing and itchy, watery eyes. His symptoms are worse on dry, windy days and settle by the autumn. Which category of trigger best explains his flares?

UN9637.stem: A 55-year-old man who has never smoked has a telephone consultation with his GP. He developed a cold in the spring and has had a dry, tickly cough ever since, now four months later. He feels otherwise well, has no breathlessness and has not coughed up blood. How should his cough be classified?

UN9637.presentation: Influenza in an at-risk adult — antiviral choice
UN9637.stem: A 71-year-old man with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) sees his GP in January. National surveillance shows that influenza is circulating in the community. He has had fever, muscle aches and a dry cough for 30 hours. His breathing is at his usual baseline, his observations are stable and there are no signs of pneumonia. Which medicine is most appropriate?

A 63-year-old man who has smoked about a packet a day since his teens sees the practice nurse because he gets breathless walking up hills. He has coughed up white sputum most winter mornings for several years. He never had childhood wheeze or hay fever, and his symptoms change little from day to day. Post-bronchodilator spirometry shows an obstructive pattern that does not reverse. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 68-year-old man with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and a 40 pack-year smoking history presents to the emergency department with sudden right-sided chest pain and worsening breathlessness. His oxygen saturation is 89% on air, heart rate 104 beats per minute and blood pressure 132/80 mmHg. His trachea is central. Chest X-ray shows a right pneumothorax with a 3 cm rim of air laterally. What is the most appropriate management?
UN9637.correct_answer: Chest drain insertion and hospital admission

UN9637.stem: A 70-year-old man has a year of progressive exertional breathlessness and a dry cough. He has finger clubbing and fine bibasal late-inspiratory crackles. HRCT shows basal, peripheral honeycombing with traction bronchiectasis. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 69-year-old woman presents with progressive exertional chest pain, dizziness and breathlessness. Examination reveals an ejection systolic murmur radiating to the carotids. What is the most likely diagnosis?

During a health check at her surgery, a 52-year-old woman asks the practice nurse which habits could make cancer of the gullet more likely.

Which factor increases her risk?

A 34-year-old man with newly diagnosed HIV and a CD4 count of 120 cells/µL has several weeks of progressive exertional breathlessness and a dry cough. At rest his oxygen saturations are 96%, but they fall markedly after walking. The chest X-ray shows bilateral perihilar interstitial shadowing. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN9638.stem: A man with known COPD presents with three days of worsening breathlessness, increased volume of sputum, and sputum that has turned from white to green. What does this presentation represent?

UN9638.presentation: Features of an Infective COPD Exacerbation
UN9638.stem: A 73-year-old man with known COPD becomes more breathless over three days and notices his sputum has turned from clear to thick and green. Which feature most strongly suggests an infective exacerbation rather than his usual baseline?
During an exacerbation of severe COPD, a patient is given high-flow oxygen before arrival in hospital and becomes increasingly drowsy on arrival. Which complication should be specifically considered?
A patient reports years of repeated chest infections along with a daily cough that produces large amounts of thick, purulent sputum. Which underlying condition should be considered?
A patient with an acute exacerbation of COPD has an arterial blood gas showing a LOW oxygen level together with a HIGH carbon dioxide level. How is this respiratory failure best classified?

UN9638.presentation: Infective Exacerbation of COPD — Oxygen Target
UN9638.stem: A 70-year-old man with known COPD attends with increased breathlessness, increased sputum volume and purulence. He is alert. While awaiting blood gases, what is the most appropriate INITIAL oxygen approach?
UN9638.correct_answer: Controlled oxygen titrated to a target saturation of 88–92% pending blood gases

UN9638.presentation: VTE risk assessment in medical inpatients
UN9638.stem: A 71-year-old man is admitted to the respiratory ward with an infective exacerbation of COPD. He is breathless on minimal exertion and is expected to stay largely in bed or in a chair for several days. He has no history of bleeding and takes no anticoagulants. As the clerking doctor, what is the most appropriate approach to venous thromboembolism prevention?
UN9638.correct_answer: Assess his individual risks of thrombosis and bleeding and then decide on prophylaxis

UN9638.stem: A breastfeeding woman at 3 weeks postpartum presents with a red, tender, warm, and swollen segment of the left breast. She has a temperature of 38.5°C and feels generally unwell with myalgia. Her symptoms have worsened over the past 24 hours despite frequent feeding and expressing from the affected breast. What is the most appropriate management?
UN9638.correct_answer: Continue breastfeeding, prescribe oral flucloxacillin, and advise analgesia

UN9641.presentation: Excluding PE With a Low Clinical Probability
UN9641.stem: A 35-year-old woman presents with mild pleuritic chest discomfort. Her calculated Wells score suggests pulmonary embolism is clinically unlikely. Which blood test is commonly used next to help exclude venous thromboembolism in this situation?

A 50-year-old woman has pleuritic chest pain and breathlessness. Using a validated clinical prediction tool, she is assessed as 'PE UNLIKELY'. She is haemodynamically stable. What is the most appropriate next investigation?

In the emergency department, a 29-year-old woman with pleuritic chest pain is judged to have a low clinical probability of pulmonary embolism. A blood test known to have very high sensitivity but low specificity for venous thromboembolism comes back negative. Why is this result useful?
UN9641.correct_answer: Most people with the disease test positive, so a negative result makes it unlikely

UN9641.stem: A 46-year-old woman presents with sudden pleuritic chest pain and shortness of breath. She is tachycardic at 118/min and mildly hypoxic. She recently returned from a long-haul flight. Her blood pressure is 118/76 mmHg. What is the most appropriate next step?
UN9641.correct_answer: Calculate the Wells score, then D-dimer or CTPA accordingly

UN9641.stem: A 55-year-old woman presents with chest pain and shortness of breath. ECG demonstrates sinus tachycardia and an S wave in lead I, Q wave in lead III and T-wave inversion in lead III. What is the most likely diagnosis?

On the fourth day after major abdominal surgery, a patient suddenly becomes breathless with pleuritic chest pain, a tachycardia and mild hypoxia. The chest is clear and there are no new infective features. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A 55-year-old woman with breast cancer presents with sudden breathlessness and pleuritic chest pain. Wells score for PE is calculated as 5. What is the most appropriate next step?

A 58-year-old woman develops sudden severe breathlessness, pleuritic chest pain, a rapid heart rate and a low blood pressure shortly after a long-haul flight. Which complication of pulmonary embolism is particularly concerning in this presentation?

UN9805.stem: A 50-year-old man with asthma reports needing his reliever inhaler almost every day because of recurring wheeze and breathlessness. What does this level of reliever use indicate?
A patient with asthma admits to using their salbutamol inhaler most days, sometimes more than once a day, to manage breathlessness. What does this pattern of reliever use most likely indicate?

A 29-year-old woman with asthma says her inhalers are not helping even though she takes them as prescribed. When asked to demonstrate, she appears to use her inhaler device incorrectly. What should be checked first?

A 34-year-old woman with mild asthma that is normally well controlled with a low-dose inhaled corticosteroid attends her GP. A neurologist recently started propranolol to prevent her migraines. Since then she has needed her reliever inhaler several times a day and wakes at night wheezing. What is the most likely explanation?
UN9805.correct_answer: Blockade of beta-2 receptors in the airways has caused bronchoconstriction

UN9805.stem: A 58-year-old man with mild asthma, previously well controlled on a low-dose inhaled corticosteroid, was started on propranolol for essential tremor by a locum a week ago. He now reports a night-time cough, chest tightness and needing his reliever inhaler several times a day. He has no fever or ankle swelling. Which mechanism best explains his deterioration?
A patient with poorly controlled asthma is about to be prescribed a NON-selective beta-blocker for another indication. What is the main concern?
UN9805.correct_answer: It may precipitate bronchospasm and worsen asthma

UN9805.stem: A 38-year-old woman with asthma and nasal polyps took naproxen for period pain. Within an hour she became wheezy, with a streaming, blocked nose, and needed her reliever inhaler several times. She asks the community pharmacist what painkillers she should avoid in future. What is the most appropriate advice?
An adult with asthma uses a short-acting beta-agonist (salbutamol) inhaler several times a week for symptoms. What is the most appropriate next step in management?
UN9805.correct_answer: Switch to as-needed low-dose ICS/formoterol (AIR therapy)

UN9834.stem: A 31-year-old man develops sneezing, nasal blockage and watery, itchy eyes every year during the spring pollen season. Symptoms settle completely over winter. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old woman has repeated episodes of wheeze and cough, especially at night and after exposure to house dust, with no symptoms in between episodes. Which feature of her history most supports a diagnosis of asthma?
UN9834.correct_answer: The variability of her respiratory symptoms

UN9834.stem: A 2-year-old child has had three episodes of wheeze and breathlessness over the past year, all occurring exclusively during viral upper respiratory tract infections. Between episodes he is completely asymptomatic. There is no personal history of atopy, no eczema, and no family history of asthma. What is the most appropriate diagnosis?
Every year in May and June, a 19-year-old develops bilateral itchy, watery, red eyes along with frequent sneezing. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN9834.presentation: Acute sinusitis beyond 10 days — medicine to consider
UN9834.stem: A 30-year-old woman sees her GP with 12 days of nasal congestion, discoloured nasal discharge and facial pressure that began with a cold. Her symptoms have not improved but are not worsening, she is systemically well and there are no red flags. After discussion she prefers to avoid an antibiotic, and asks whether any medicine might help her symptoms. Which medicine is most appropriate to consider?
A patient who started ramipril a few weeks ago develops recurrent episodes of non-itchy swelling of the lips and tongue, without urticaria. What is the most likely cause and the key action?
UN9834.correct_answer: ACE inhibitor-induced angioedema — stop the ACE inhibitor permanently

UN9834.stem: A 26-year-old man sees his GP with 6 days of nasal congestion, purulent discharge and left-sided facial pain. Since this morning his left upper and lower eyelids have become red and swollen, and he has double vision when looking to the left. His temperature is 38.2°C. What is the most appropriate management?
UN9834.correct_answer: Refer to hospital for same-day assessment

UN9834.presentation: Antibiotics for a Viral Upper Respiratory Infection
UN9834.stem: Convinced he needs antibiotics, a 35-year-old man visits his GP describing three days of nasal congestion, a sore throat and a cough, but he is otherwise systemically well. How should the GP respond?
UN9834.correct_answer: Explain that antibiotics are not routinely indicated; give symptomatic advice

UN10124.stem: A 21-year-old university student has 10 days of dry cough, malaise and low-grade fever. The chest signs are less impressive than the diffuse changes on the chest X-ray. Blood tests show anaemia with red-cell agglutination, and she has developed a target-lesion rash on her arms. What is the most likely causative organism?

UN10124.presentation: New Dry Cough After Starting an Antihypertensive
UN10124.stem: A 55-year-old man develops a persistent dry, irritating cough six weeks after starting treatment for high blood pressure. Chest examination and chest X-ray are normal. Which of his medications is the most likely cause?

UN10124.presentation: Dry Cough After Starting a New Drug
UN10124.stem: A 57-year-old man with hypertension starts ramipril. Six weeks later he develops a persistent dry, irritating cough with no other new symptoms. What is the most likely cause?
UN10124.correct_answer: An adverse effect of the ACE inhibitor

UN10124.stem: A young adult has a dry cough, fatigue, painful red shin nodules (erythema nodosum) and joint pains. Chest X-ray shows bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, and serum calcium is mildly raised. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A 55-year-old man has been started on ramipril for hypertension. Two weeks later he develops a persistent dry cough. He has no wheeze or breathlessness. What is the most appropriate management?
UN10124.correct_answer: Stop ramipril and switch to an ARB such as losartan

UN10124.stem:
A 68-year-old man develops fever, shaking chills and a cough productive of rust-coloured sputum over 24 hours. He has sharp right-sided chest pain on breathing in. A chest X-ray shows consolidation confined to the right lower lobe. He has no recent travel, hospital admission or exposure to others who are unwell.

Which organism most commonly causes this community-acquired pneumonia?

UN10124.presentation: Lung cancer — troublesome dry cough in advanced disease
UN10124.stem: A 72-year-old man has locally advanced non-small-cell lung cancer and is not suitable for treatment with curative intent. He has a persistent dry, non-productive cough that disturbs his sleep. He is afebrile, there is no wheeze, chest examination is unchanged and a chest X-ray shows no new collapse, effusion or consolidation. Simple linctus has not helped. He takes regular paracetamol only. Which drug is most appropriate to reduce his cough?

A 55-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis has been taking methotrexate 20 mg weekly for eight months. She presents with a three-week history of progressive dyspnoea, dry cough, and low-grade fever. Chest X-ray shows bilateral interstitial infiltrates. Oxygen saturation is 93% on air. What is the most likely complication?

UN10444.stem: A patient with asthma continues to have frequent symptoms despite being on an inhaled corticosteroid. On questioning, he admits he often forgets doses and is unsure how to use the inhaler properly. What should be addressed before anything else?

A 29-year-old woman with asthma says her inhalers are not helping even though she takes them as prescribed. When asked to demonstrate, she appears to use her inhaler device incorrectly. What should be checked first?

A patient with stable but symptomatic COPD remains breathless on minimal exertion despite being on maximal appropriate inhaled therapy. Which non-drug intervention would most improve his exercise capacity and quality of life?

A mother reports that her 6-year-old son struggles to press down his metered-dose inhaler at exactly the same time as breathing in, so much of the medication seems to be lost. What change would most improve drug delivery?
UN10444.correct_answer: Add a spacer device to the inhaler

UN10444.stem: A woman with gestational diabetes has not achieved glucose targets after 1–2 weeks of diet and exercise. What is the most appropriate next step?
UN10444.correct_answer: Start metformin, adding insulin if targets are still not met

UN10444.presentation: Alternative Analgesia Route in Palliative Care
UN10444.stem: A 68-year-old man with advanced malignancy has escalating pain despite being on regular oral analgesia, but he is now struggling to swallow tablets. What is an important principle of symptom management in this situation?
UN10444.correct_answer: Consider switching to an alternative route of drug administration

UN10444.stem: A 50-year-old man with asthma reports needing his reliever inhaler almost every day because of recurring wheeze and breathlessness. What does this level of reliever use indicate?

UN10444.presentation: Asthma–COPD overlap — stepping down inhaled corticosteroid
UN10444.stem: A 62-year-old woman with asthma–COPD overlap is stable on an inhaled corticosteroid and long-acting beta-2 agonist combination inhaler. A locum proposes switching her to a long-acting muscarinic antagonist plus long-acting beta-2 agonist inhaler, with no inhaled corticosteroid, to reduce her pneumonia risk. She had a life-threatening asthma attack 4 years ago. Which is the most important risk of this change?
UN10444.correct_answer: Severe asthma attack from loss of corticosteroid

UN10446.stem: A 58-year-old man newly diagnosed with COPD continues to smoke 20 cigarettes a day. Which single intervention would do the most to change the long-term trajectory of his lung disease?

A motivated patient wants to stop smoking and asks about medication to help. Alongside behavioural support, which of the following is an appropriate first-line pharmacological aid to smoking cessation?

UN10446.presentation: Smoking Cessation After a Cancer Diagnosis
UN10446.stem: A 70-year-old man newly diagnosed with oesophageal cancer, who has smoked for many years, asks his doctor whether there is still any point in trying to quit. Which advice is most appropriate?
UN10446.correct_answer: Smoking cessation should be encouraged, as it has health benefits and may reduce further risks

UN10446.stem: A patient with Graves' disease has gritty, watery, protruding eyes (proptosis) with lid retraction. The disease is currently mild. She is a current smoker. Apart from controlling the thyroid, what is the most appropriate management?
UN10446.correct_answer: Smoking cessation and supportive measures (lubricants), with selenium

UN10446.presentation: Modifiable Risk Factor for Osteoporotic Fracture
UN10446.stem: A 70-year-old woman with known osteoporosis asks her doctor which lifestyle change would most help reduce her risk of further fractures. Which is most appropriate?

A 55-year-old man who has never smoked has a telephone consultation with his GP. He developed a cold in the spring and has had a dry, tickly cough ever since, now four months later. He feels otherwise well, has no breathlessness and has not coughed up blood. How should his cough be classified?

A 45-year-old man is seen in the pre-operative assessment clinic before a hernia repair. He smokes 20 cigarettes a day and wants to stop. He tried once before using willpower alone and relapsed within a week. Which approach offers him the best chance of stopping?
UN10446.correct_answer: Referral to a stop smoking service for behavioural support combined with stop-smoking medication

UN10446.stem: A 59-year-old woman attends the vascular clinic with cramping pain in her right calf that comes on after walking about 100 metres and settles with rest. Her ankle–brachial pressure index is reduced. She already takes atorvastatin and clopidogrel. She smokes 20 cigarettes a day. Which lifestyle measure will most reduce her risk of cardiovascular events and amputation?

UN10447.stem: A man with known COPD presents with three days of worsening breathlessness, increased volume of sputum, and sputum that has turned from white to green. What does this presentation represent?

UN10447.presentation: Acute Lip Swelling after a New Drug
UN10447.stem: A 27-year-old woman develops itchy raised wheals over her trunk and swelling of her lips within an hour of starting a new medication. Her airway is clear, breathing is normal, and blood pressure is stable. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN10447.presentation: Food-Triggered Rash With Lip Swelling and Breathing Difficulty
UN10447.stem: A 7-year-old girl develops a widespread itchy rash minutes after eating a new snack containing nuts. She now has swollen lips and is struggling to breathe. What is the most appropriate immediate treatment?

A coastguard team recovers a 67-year-old fisherman from cold harbour water. He is unresponsive, has a palpable pulse and is breathing slowly and shallowly. There is no history of a fall or dive. What is the immediate priority?
UN10447.correct_answer: Open and support his airway and breathing, ventilating with oxygen

UN10447.stem: A man is pulled unconscious from a swimming pool and, once out of the water, is noted to be breathing inadequately. What is the immediate priority in his management?
UN10447.correct_answer: Secure and support his airway and breathing

UN10447.stem: On day 6 after an abdominal laparotomy, a patient notices pink serous fluid soaking through the dressing, and on inspection the wound edges have partially separated. What is the most likely complication?
A heart failure patient wakes suddenly at night gasping for breath and has to sit upright. What is this called?

A 35-year-old man who is nervous about an upcoming occupational medical has a raised blood pressure when his GP measures it. The GP notices he is sitting with his legs crossed, his arm hanging unsupported, and has been talking throughout. What is the most appropriate approach before drawing conclusions from the reading?
UN10447.correct_answer: Correct the technique, repeat the reading and arrange out-of-office monitoring if it remains raised

UN10448.stem: A 70-year-old man has fever, productive cough and right-sided pleuritic pain. He is confused, with a respiratory rate of 32, blood pressure 88/56, and urea 8 mmol/L. What does his CURB-65 assessment indicate?
UN10448.correct_answer: High severity — admit and treat as severe pneumonia

UN10448.stem: A 68-year-old with pneumonia has new confusion, a urea of 8 mmol/L, a respiratory rate of 32, and a blood pressure of 88/56. What does the CURB-65 score indicate about his management?
UN10448.correct_answer: High score — admit and manage as high-severity pneumonia

UN10448.stem: A 72-year-old man with community-acquired pneumonia has a new-onset confusion, urea 12 mmol/L, respiratory rate 30 breaths/min, and blood pressure 100/70 mmHg. What is his CURB-65 score?

A 51-year-old woman develops fever, a productive cough and increasing breathlessness over two days. A chest X-ray demonstrates a new area of focal consolidation. What is the most appropriate treatment?
UN10448.correct_answer: Antibiotics guided by CURB-65 and local guidance

UN10448.stem: A 71-year-old woman is seen on a GP home visit. For three days she has had shivering attacks, a cough bringing up rust-coloured sputum and a sharp pain in her right side when she breathes in. Her temperature is 38.6°C and she is mildly tachypnoeic but fully oriented. There is dullness to percussion at the right base with bronchial breathing and coarse crackles over the same area. Which diagnosis best fits?

A 74-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department by her daughter after 3 days of cough, fever and increasing drowsiness. She is newly confused about the date and place. Respiratory rate is 32 per minute, blood pressure 96/58 mmHg, pulse 112 beats per minute and oxygen saturation 90% on air. Urea is raised. Chest X-ray shows left lower lobe consolidation. What is the most appropriate management?
UN10448.correct_answer: Admission, oxygen and IV antibiotics for high-severity pneumonia

UN10448.presentation: Elements of the Functional Capacity Test
UN10448.stem: When assessing whether an adult has the capacity to consent to a particular treatment, which of the following forms part of that assessment?
UN10448.correct_answer: Whether they can understand, retain and weigh the information and communicate a choice

UN10448.stem: A patient admitted with severe community-acquired pneumonia has an arterial blood gas showing marked hypoxaemia with a PaCO2 that is normal. What type of respiratory failure does this represent?

UN10449.stem: A 72-year-old man with community-acquired pneumonia has a new-onset confusion, urea 12 mmol/L, respiratory rate 30 breaths/min, and blood pressure 100/70 mmHg. What is his CURB-65 score?
A 68-year-old with pneumonia has new confusion, a urea of 8 mmol/L, a respiratory rate of 32, and a blood pressure of 88/56. What does the CURB-65 score indicate about his management?
UN10449.correct_answer: High score — admit and manage as high-severity pneumonia

UN10449.stem: A 70-year-old man has fever, productive cough and right-sided pleuritic pain. He is confused, with a respiratory rate of 32, blood pressure 88/56, and urea 8 mmol/L. What does his CURB-65 assessment indicate?
UN10449.correct_answer: High severity — admit and treat as severe pneumonia

UN10449.stem:
A 46-year-old woman admitted with pyelonephritis has her observations recorded on the ward. Her pulse, blood pressure, temperature, oxygen saturation and alertness all score 0, but her respiratory rate of 26/min scores 3, giving a total NEWS2 score of 3.

According to NICE sepsis guidance, what is the most appropriate action?
UN10449.correct_answer: Ask for a high-priority review by an FY2 doctor or above

UN10449.stem: A 51-year-old woman develops fever, a productive cough and increasing breathlessness over two days. A chest X-ray demonstrates a new area of focal consolidation. What is the most appropriate treatment?
UN10449.correct_answer: Antibiotics guided by CURB-65 and local guidance

UN10449.presentation: Fluid-refractory septic shock on the ward
UN10449.stem:
A 58-year-old woman was admitted from the emergency department with acute pyelonephritis and was given intravenous antibiotics within an hour of arrival. Five hours later she is confused. Her blood pressure is 78/40 mmHg, heart rate 128 bpm, respiratory rate 30/min and oxygen saturation 93% on supplemental oxygen, and her catheter bag holds only a few millilitres. She has already received 1 litre of crystalloid in small boluses without improvement, and the medical registrar is now with her. Her creatinine is about three times the value from a routine GP blood test last month, her platelet count is low, her bilirubin is raised and her venous lactate is 5.6 mmol/L. An ultrasound shows no hydronephrosis. Before this illness she lived independently, and no limits on her treatment have been set.

Which step should the registrar take next?
UN10449.correct_answer: Critical care referral for vasopressors and organ support

UN10449.stem: A 74-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department by her daughter after 3 days of cough, fever and increasing drowsiness. She is newly confused about the date and place. Respiratory rate is 32 per minute, blood pressure 96/58 mmHg, pulse 112 beats per minute and oxygen saturation 90% on air. Urea is raised. Chest X-ray shows left lower lobe consolidation. What is the most appropriate management?
UN10449.correct_answer: Admission, oxygen and IV antibiotics for high-severity pneumonia

UN10449.presentation: COVID-19 — pulse oximetry overestimation in dark skin
UN10449.stem: A 52-year-old woman of Black African heritage attends the emergency department on day 7 of confirmed COVID-19. She is increasingly breathless and cannot finish sentences, and her respiratory rate is 30 breaths/min. Her pulse oximeter reading is 95% on air on two repeat readings. The FY1 is considering discharge with home monitoring because the saturation is reassuring. What is the most appropriate next step?
UN10449.correct_answer: Arterial blood gas to measure oxygenation

UN10450.stem: A 55-year-old woman with breast cancer presents with sudden breathlessness and pleuritic chest pain. Wells score for PE is calculated as 5. What is the most appropriate next step?

Ten days after a right total knee replacement, a 58-year-old woman sees her GP with a dull ache in her right calf. She is otherwise well. Which examination finding would most strongly suggest a deep vein thrombosis?
UN10450.correct_answer: Swelling of the right calf, which is clearly wider than the left

UN10450.presentation: Wells score and D-dimer — the pathway
UN10450.stem: A patient has a low Wells score for pulmonary embolism. A D-dimer is requested and comes back negative. What is the most appropriate next step?
UN10450.correct_answer: PE is effectively excluded — look for an alternative diagnosis

UN10450.stem: A 45-year-old man arrives in the emergency department two days after a long-haul flight with sudden breathlessness and a sharp left-sided chest pain on inspiration. He is tachycardic, his blood pressure is normal and his oxygen saturation is mildly reduced on air. The chest X-ray is unremarkable. His two-level Wells score indicates that pulmonary embolism is likely, and his renal function is normal. Which investigation should be arranged next?
A patient with a suspected large pulmonary embolism becomes acutely hypotensive with signs of obstructive shock. What does this clinical picture represent?

A 44-year-old woman comes to the emergency department with a swollen, tender right calf that started two days after a long coach journey. She is not breathless and has no chest pain. What is the most appropriate approach to investigating a possible deep vein thrombosis?
UN10450.correct_answer: Calculate a two-level Wells score to direct D-dimer testing or proximal leg vein ultrasound

UN10450.stem: A 39-year-old man attends the urgent treatment centre two days after returning from Australia, a journey with over 20 hours of flying. His left calf has become tense, warm and painful and his ankle is visibly puffier than the right. He has no breathlessness or chest pain. Which diagnosis should be excluded first?

UN10450.presentation: Excluding PE With a Low Clinical Probability
UN10450.stem: A 35-year-old woman presents with mild pleuritic chest discomfort. Her calculated Wells score suggests pulmonary embolism is clinically unlikely. Which blood test is commonly used next to help exclude venous thromboembolism in this situation?

UN10453.stem: A patient with known heart failure develops dullness to percussion and reduced breath sounds at both lung bases. What is the most likely explanation?

A 65-year-old man has a unilateral pleural effusion. A diagnostic tap shows a pleural fluid protein and LDH that, applied to Light's criteria, classify it as an exudate. Which underlying cause does this most support?

UN10453.presentation: Sudden Breathlessness and Shock After Trauma
UN10453.stem: After a road traffic collision, a patient suddenly becomes severely breathless and hypotensive, with markedly reduced breath sounds on one side of the chest consistent with obstructive shock. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 76-year-old man who spent 30 years fitting pipe lagging in power stations sees his GP with 3 months of a dull, constant right chest ache, worsening breathlessness and a 7 kg weight loss. Chest X-ray shows a large right pleural effusion. CT shows nodular, irregular pleural thickening encasing the right lung and extending onto the mediastinal pleura. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 59-year-old man with alcohol-related liver disease is admitted with a swollen abdomen. A foundation doctor examines him on the ward and wants to confirm at the bedside whether the swelling is due to free intraperitoneal fluid. Which examination finding would best support this?

A 72-year-old woman presents with sudden onset chest pain and shortness of breath. Examination reveals absent breath sounds and hyperresonance to percussion over the right hemithorax. She is in respiratory distress and her trachea is deviated to the left. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A pleural effusion is sampled. The pleural-fluid:serum protein ratio is 0.53 and the pleural-fluid:serum LDH ratio is 0.7, although the absolute fluid protein is borderline at 32 g/L. Using Light's criteria, how is this effusion classified?
On examining a teenage boy with acute testicular pain, which finding would most support a diagnosis of testicular torsion?
